scripts/measure_depth_offset.py tested three hypotheses against both a synthetic sanity check (known injected depths, so any deviation from 1.00× is the harness's own methodological bias) and the real cached KIC 3542116 photometry:

Synthetic sanity check (known truth):

Method median ratio scatter current (detrended, rolling baseline) 0.946x 0.041 H1 (detrended, out-of-event baseline) 0.947x 0.067 H2 (fitted comet-model depth) 1.145x 0.062 H3 (raw flux, rolling baseline) 0.948x 0.043 H1+H3 combined 1.016x 0.064

Even on data with perfectly known injected depths, the current method reads 5.4% low — a methodological floor present regardless of which real-data hypothesis is correct.

Real KIC 3542116 data (cached, offline):

Method median ratio scatter current (detrended, rolling baseline) 0.772x 0.098 H1 (detrended, out-of-event baseline) 0.852x 0.103 H2 (fitted comet-model depth) 1.316x 1.009 H3 (raw flux, rolling baseline) 0.779x 0.098 H1+H3 combined 0.879x 0.122

Reading these numbers honestly, matching the research log's own conclusions verbatim in substance:

  • H3 (Savitzky-Golay detrending absorbing part of the dip) is ruled out. 0.779x vs. 0.772x for the current method is statistically indistinguishable, matching the synthetic-data result and ruling out detrending as a meaningful contributor.
  • H1 (baseline contamination — the rolling-median reference window is dragged down by the dip itself) is real but only partial. Isolating it moves the ratio from 0.772x to 0.852x — roughly a third of the total gap.
  • H1+H3 combined reaches 0.879x — still 12 percentage points short of unbiased (1.0x), and — this is the research log's own explicitly flagged surprise — worse than the synthetic check would have predicted: "the real-data shortfall is larger than the synthetic-data shortfall by more than the difference between the two hypotheses tested. Something present in real KIC 3542116 photometry and absent from the synthetic injection is contributing an additional ~10-15% on top."
  • H2 (fitted comet-model depth) is unusable as reported — its median (1.316x) looks closer to unbiased than the others, but its scatter (standard deviation 1.009, "essentially as large as the mean") reveals per-dip ratios ranging from 0.99x to 3.47x, which research log 006 attributes to a separate model-fit instability bug, not evidence about the depth-bias question (see 15_model_fitting.md §15.5).

A supplementary baseline-window-width sweep (2.06 d shipped → 20 d) found the ratio peaks at 0.849x around a 5-day window and decays back toward the shipped value by 20 days — non-monotonic, and the research log explicitly recommends not widening the shipped window based on this alone: "0.849x at its best point is still an 15-point gap, and the non-monotonic shape means 'wider is better' is not a safe rule to extrapolate from this data alone."

docs.title: 22.5 What remains unexplained (quoted candidates, not resolved here)
docs.text:
Research log 006 lists, in its own stated order of suspicion, what has not been tested as of 2026-09-15/16:

  1. The published depths may themselves come from a full model fit with different free parameters than this pipeline's comet model, not a raw observed minimum — untested by anything in log 006.
  2. Quarter-to-quarter flux-normalisation offsets from stitching 16 separate Kepler quarters, each with its own PDC normalisation — the leading suspect for the remaining gap per docs/NEXT_STEPS.md's "FIRST THING NEXT SESSION" framing, not yet tested as of this document.
  3. The comet-model fit's own instability on shallow events (H2's 3.47× outlier) deserves independent investigation regardless of the depth question.

No code change was made in response to log 006 — its own final section states this explicitly ("This investigation did NOT do" — no change to detect/comet_detector.py, detect/baseline.py, or how depth is reported). This document does not assert the depth-offset question is resolved; the correct summary is: ~5 points of the 22.8-point gap is a measurement-methodology floor visible even on synthetic data, ~8 points is real and attributable to baseline contamination, and ~10-15 points remain genuinely unexplained as of commit 01c2051.

docs.title: 23.3 ingest.yml — the active workflow
docs.text:
Two sequenced jobs, kepler then tess (needs: kepler), each timeout-minutes: 45. Trigger: cron: "0 * * * *" (hourly) plus workflow_dispatch with optional time_budget_minutes (default "25") and max_targets inputs. concurrency: {group: ingest, cancel-in-progress: false} — a second trigger queues rather than running in parallel, matching scripts/ingest.py's own documented concurrency assumption (11_pipeline.md §11.7).

Each job: checkout → setup Python 3.12 → pip install -e ".[dev]" → clone AJpro-merc/exocomet-hunter-data (using secrets.DATA_REPO_TOKEN, over HTTPS with an x-access-token credential) into data-repo/ → run scripts/ingest.py --mission {Kepler,TESS} --data-repo-dir data-repo --time-budget-minutes ... → pytest tests/unit -q → commit and push any new ledger/extract/results files back to the data repo, with git pull --rebase --autostash before pushing to handle a concurrent writer.

Direct consequence of the sequenced needs: kepler: if the kepler job fails outright (as it did in both 2026-09-16 failures, per §23.2), the tess job never runs at all for that hourly cycle — this is the specific mechanism by which the five-bad-KIC-ID bug also silently starved TESS ingestion, not only Kepler, on both occasions.

All output (ledger.jsonl, extract/, results/) is pushed to the separate AJpro-merc/exocomet-hunter-data repository, never to this repo's own git history — matching scripts/ingest.py's module docstring layout description (11_pipeline.md §11.1).

docs.title: 23.4 survey.yml — disabled, older/separate pipeline
docs.text: Verified disabled_manually. This is a distinct, older pipeline (scripts/monitor_new_data.py) with its own state file (results/processed_ledger.json, a whole-file-rewrite pattern — not the append-only JSONL ledger io/ledger.py implements for ingest.py). Scheduled daily at 0 5 * * * when active, capped to a handful of targets per run via --limit (default 5), watching config/watchlist.txt for new TESS sectors. Commits results directly to this repository (not the separate data repo), unlike ingest.yml. Session Log 2026-09-15 §5 records the disable reason: gh run list showed train.yml burning ~2h16m of real compute across four consecutive failures producing zero output, traced to the scheduled trigger referencing a stale pre-force-push commit SHA after a history-cleaning force-push orphaned it; both survey.yml and train.yml were disabled together pending a real commit to re-anchor main. This document's own gh workflow list --all query independently confirms both remain disabled as of 2026-09-16 — this is not merely a historical claim carried forward from the session log.

docs.title: 23.5 train.yml — disabled, classifier training pipeline
docs.text:
Verified disabled_manually. Two cron schedules in one workflow: 0 */2 * * * (generation — kepler/tess jobs run scripts/generate_training_labels.py, capped at --max-new-rows 400, --bootstrap-draws 300, writing labelled parquet rows to the data repo) and 0 6 * * 1 (weekly retrain — the train job, gated if: always() && (...), runs scripts/train_classifier.py against whatever accumulated data exists, skipping a mission's refit if its data's SHA-256 hash is unchanged since the last run). The workflow's own top-of-file comment explains why generation and training are split this way rather than combined, and why this runs on GitHub Actions rather than a Claude Cloud routine: "Claude Cloud routines cannot reach mast.stsci.edu (a 403 from the sandbox's own egress proxy, confirmed 2026-09-14)." Both jobs, like ingest.yml, push results to AJpro-merc/exocomet-hunter-data using the same DATA_REPO_TOKEN secret.

docs/NEXT_STEPS.md (working tree) lists re-enabling train.yml as downstream of ingest.yml running unattended successfully; as of this document neither train.yml nor survey.yml has been re-enabled since the 2026-09-15 disable.

docs.title: 23.6 DATA_REPO_TOKEN
docs.text: Per Session Log 2026-09-15 §12, this secret was added by the repository owner after the session that built ingest.py, and a subsequent live workflow_dispatch run confirmed the full ingest cycle (fetch → extract → detrend → detect → save results → push) succeeding end-to-end on GitHub's own infrastructure, with files independently verified to land in exocomet-hunter-data via the GitHub API. This document did not re-verify the token's presence directly (no gh secret list permission was exercised during this review), but the run history in §23.2 — specifically the two successful ingest runs on 2026-09-15 — is consistent with the token being present and working prior to the unrelated five-bad-KIC-ID regression that then caused the two subsequent failures on 2026-09-16.

docs.title: 24.1 What this is, and is not
docs.text: scripts/build_local_db.py builds a disposable SQLite view of the append-only ledger. Its own module docstring is explicit that it is not a second source of truth: "The ledger ... is the source of truth. This script is not a second source of truth — it is a queryable view, rebuilt from scratch on demand, never committed to git, never written by CI." build_local_db() (lines 169–288) deletes any existing file at --out and recreates it from ledger.jsonl (plus, for candidate counts, the results files the ledger points at) on every invocation — "there is no 'did the DB miss an update' question to ask, because the DB never survives between runs." Default output path is local.db in the current directory, deliberately not inside --data-repo-dir, so a stray git add -A in the separate exocomet-hunter-data clone can never accidentally commit this regenerated binary file.

docs.title: attempts — full retry history, one row per raw ledger line
docs.text:
CREATE TABLE attempts (
    target_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
    mission       TEXT NOT NULL,
    status        TEXT NOT NULL,
    timestamp_utc TEXT NOT NULL,
    attempt       INTEGER NOT NULL,
    error         TEXT,
    extract_path  TEXT,
    results_path  TEXT
);

Nothing deduplicated — every ledger line, including every retry and failure, becomes one row here. Answers "show me the retry history for star X."

docs.title: targets — latest-status view, one row per (target_id, mission)
docs.text:
CREATE TABLE targets (
    target_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
    mission       TEXT NOT NULL,
    status        TEXT NOT NULL,
    timestamp_utc TEXT NOT NULL,
    attempt       INTEGER NOT NULL,
    error         TEXT,
    extract_path  TEXT,
    results_path  TEXT,
    retries_left  INTEGER,
    n_candidates  INTEGER,
    n_flagged     INTEGER,
    PRIMARY KEY (target_id, mission)
);

Built from exocomet.io.ledger.latest_entries() — the last ledger line seen per key. retries_left is computed as max(max_attempts - entry.attempt, 0), only meaningful when status='failed' (None otherwise). n_candidates/n_flagged are read by opening the results file at entry.results_path and counting rows (n_flagged = count where row.get("flagged") is truthy).

The NULL vs. 0 distinction is deliberate and documented as the whole reason this table reads results files at all, rather than trusting the ledger's path strings alone: n_candidates/n_flagged are NULL when results_path is unset or the file does not exist on disk (a failed or never-attempted target — nothing to count), and 0 when the results file exists but is genuinely empty (a star fully processed and found quiet). _read_results_rows() (lines 139–166) implements this: returns None (distinct from []) for "not processed / nothing to read."

docs.title: candidates — one row per detected event
docs.text:
CREATE TABLE candidates (
    target_id         TEXT NOT NULL,
    mission           TEXT NOT NULL,
    t_min             REAL,
    depth_ppm         REAL,
    duration_days     REAL,
    a_dur_sigma       REAL,
    significance      REAL,
    delta_bic         REAL,
    tau_over_sigma    REAL,
    signs_agree       INTEGER,
    flagged           INTEGER,
    periodic          INTEGER,
    period_days       REAL,
    vetting_status    TEXT,
    vetting_reasons   TEXT,
    FOREIGN KEY (target_id, mission) REFERENCES targets (target_id, mission)
);

Columns mirror CandidateRecord.to_row() (core/types.py) minus target_id itself (already a column) plus mission (needed here since target_id alone is not globally unique — to_row() does not include mission). vetting_status/ vetting_reasons will be NULL for every row currently produced, per 18_vetting.md — the schema has the columns, but nothing populates them.

docs.title: Indexes
docs.text:
CREATE INDEX idx_attempts_target ON attempts (target_id, mission);
CREATE INDEX idx_candidates_target ON candidates (target_id, mission);
CREATE INDEX idx_candidates_flagged ON candidates (flagged);

docs.title: 24.3 Failure modes and tolerances
docs.text:
• A corrupt/truncated last line in the ledger (a process killed mid-write) is skipped with a logged warning by read_ledger(), not raised — build_local_db inherits this tolerance since it calls read_ledger directly.
  • A corrupt line in a results JSONL file is likewise skipped and logged (_read_results_rows), "mirroring read_ledger's tolerance of a torn trailing write — one bad line should not hide an otherwise-good results file."
  • main() (lines 319–341) checks for the data-repo directory and ledger.jsonl existing before attempting a build, printing a plain-language message and returning 0 (not an error) if nothing has been ingested yet — "nothing to build yet" is treated as a normal, expected state rather than a failure.

docs.title: 24.4 CLI
docs.text:
python scripts/build_local_db.py [--data-repo-dir data-repo] [--out local.db]
                                  [--max-attempts 3]

--max-attempts must match scripts/ingest.py's own --max-attempts for retries_left to be computed accurately — this is a documented, not enforced, cross-script contract (no runtime check compares the two).

docs.title: 25. Reproducibility
docs.text: Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051. Written against the actual pipeline, CI workflows, and Next Steps.md PART E (engineering) — not aspirational.

docs.title: 25.1 What is captured today
docs.text:
Reproducibility today is partial and comes from several independent, uncoordinated sources rather than one designed mechanism:

  • Git commit identity. Every CI run (ingest.yml, train.yml, formerly survey.yml) checks out a specific commit via actions/checkout, so the code version that produced any given exocomet-hunter-data commit is recoverable in principle by cross-referencing timestamps against git log. There is no field that stores the commit SHA inside the output data itself.
  • Committed configuration. config/thresholds.yaml, config/validation_targets.yaml, config/watchlist.txt, and the mission host lists are checked into the repository, versioned by git like any other source file. A run against a given commit used exactly the thresholds present in that commit's config/thresholds.yaml — recoverable, but only by checking out that commit, not by reading a per-run manifest.
  • The ledger (io/ledger.py). scripts/ingest.py appends one JSON line per attempt to ledger.jsonl in the external AJpro-merc/exocomet-hunter-data repository: target_id, mission, status, timestamp_utc, attempt, error, extract_path, results_path. This is real per-run provenance — it answers "was this target processed, when, and did it succeed" — but carries no config hash, package versions, or git commit.
  • The training manifest (scripts/train_classifier.py). Each training run appends one line to models/manifest_<mission>.jsonl with row count, class counts, host stars, training_set_hash (a SHA-256 over the input parquet files), package_versions (exocomet, scikit-learn, pandas, numpy, read via importlib.metadata.version), the chosen threshold, and both backtest results. This is the most complete provenance record that exists anywhere in the project, but it is scoped to classifier training only — it says nothing about how the underlying detection features were produced.
  • author/exptime/sector-or-quarter list in lc.meta. Since the A2 fix (io/download.py), every LightCurveData carries which pipeline (author) and cadence (exptime) it was pinned to, and which sectors/quarters were stitched. This metadata flows into every generated training row (generate_training_labels.py) but is not currently attached to detection results (CandidateRecord.to_row() has no author/exptime/sector columns).

docs.title: 25.2 What is NOT captured — E3, NOT IMPLEMENTED
docs.text:
Next Steps PART E, item E3 specifies a full provenance manifest that does not exist yet:

Every run writes results/runs/<timestamp>.json with config, package version, git commit, Python/OS, seed, target-list hash, lightkurve author/exptime, output checksums.

Status: NOT IMPLEMENTED. No file matching results/runs/*.json is produced anywhere in the codebase; grep across src/ and scripts/ finds no reference to such a path. Concretely, the following are absent from any single artifact today:

  • Git commit SHA recorded alongside a specific output.
  • Full Python/OS environment description for a detection run (training manifests record package versions; detection runs do not).
  • The RNG seed used for a specific detection run (runtime.rng_seed: 42 in config/thresholds.yaml is a single shared default, not a per-run recorded value — a caller can override it, and that override is not logged).
  • A target-list hash (which exact list of stars a batch was run against).
  • Output checksums.
  • A single JSON manifest tying config + commit + environment + inputs + outputs together for one run.

docs.title: 25.3 Net effect
docs.text:
Reproducing a specific historical detection result today requires manually correlating three independent, imperfectly-timestamped sources — git history, the ledger, and (for training) the manifest — rather than reading one file. This is workable for the project's current scale (a handful of contributors, one machine, everything in git) and would not scale to an external reviewer trying to audit a specific candidate without direct access to the author's git history and CI logs.

E3 is the concrete fix and is unbuilt. Until it exists, any claim of "this result is reproducible" should be read as "reproducible by someone with git and CI-log access who is willing to do the correlation by hand," not "reproducible from a single artifact."

docs.title: 28. Limitations
docs.text: Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051. Every item below is a real, currently-open issue from Next Steps.md PART B and PART J, or a finding recorded in docs/research_log/. Nothing here is hypothetical.

docs.title: 28.1 B1 — Measured depths run ~78% of published values (OPEN, PARTIALLY INVESTIGATED)
docs.text:
All six recovered dips in the primary validation target, KIC 3542116, report depths systematically below the Rappaport et al. (2018) published values:

Dip Published (ppm) Reported (ppm) Ratio D140, shallow 491 442 0.90× D742, shallow 524 461 0.88× D793, shallow 679 412 0.61× D992, deep 1200 940 0.78× D1176, deep 1500 1094 0.73× D1268, deep 1900 1445 0.76× median ratio 0.772×

docs/research_log/006-depth-offset-investigation.md (2026-09-15) tested three hypotheses against real cached photometry using scripts/measure_depth_offset.py:

  • Detrending absorption (H3): ruled out. Statistically identical to the current method on real data (0.779× vs 0.772×), and confirmed on a synthetic sanity check too.
  • Baseline contamination (H1): real, but partial. Closes roughly a third of the gap (0.772× → 0.852× on real data, isolated).
  • H1+H3 combined: 0.879×, still 12 percentage points short of unbiased. The real-data shortfall is larger than what the same combination predicted on synthetic data with known injected depths — something specific to real photometry (not reproduced by the synthetic check) contributes an additional ~10-15% unexplained.

Leading untested hypothesis: quarter-to-quarter flux-normalization offsets from stitching 16 separate Kepler quarters, each with its own PDC normalization — named explicitly in the research log as the next thing to test and in Next Steps.md's "FIRST THING NEXT SESSION" list, but not yet run.

Status: 🟠 open, investigated, not resolved. No detector code has been changed as a result of this investigation (research log 006 is explicit that this was measurement only).

docs.title: 28.2 A model-fit instability found while investigating B1 (OPEN, UNINVESTIGATED as its own bug)
docs.text:
The same research log's test of a fourth hypothesis (fitted vs. observed depth, "H2") surfaced a separate, real problem: the comet-profile least-squares fit (detect/model_comparison.py) is wildly unstable on shallow events. One dip (D140, published 491 ppm) fit at 3.47× its published depth (1704 ppm fitted). The scatter across all six dips under this method was essentially as large as the mean (median ratio 1.316×, standard deviation 1.009) — the H2 numbers are not usable as a depth-bias measurement precisely because the fit itself is diverging for at least the shallow events.

This has never been investigated as its own issue. It matters beyond B1's depth question: if the comet-model fit diverges for shallow events, the ΔBIC ranking and τ/σ statistic computed from that same fit for those events may be less trustworthy than currently assumed — and ΔBIC/τ/σ are exactly what the A4 flagging rule (research log 007) decides on. Status: 🔴 flagged as a priority in Next Steps.md ("FIRST THING NEXT SESSION" item 4), NOT IMPLEMENTED / NOT INVESTIGATED.

docs.title: 28.3 The trials-factor / look-elsewhere problem (D5, NOT IMPLEMENTED)
docs.text:
Per-event significance in this pipeline (bootstrap a_dur_sigma, ΔBIC, τ/σ) is computed for one event considered in isolation. None of it is corrected for how many places were searched — how many stars, how many candidate windows per star, how many cadences. This is the standard "look-elsewhere effect" that applies to any blind search, and the README states it plainly under "Honest limitations": "Per-event significance is not corrected for the number of trials."

Next Steps.md PART D, item D5 names the intended fix (estimate the empirical false-alarm rate from time-reversed and control light curves) and PART J, item J2 sharpens it (run the detector over ~10,000 quiet or time-reversed light curves and report "N candidates per 10,000 null curves at this threshold" as a defensible, empirically-measured false-alarm rate rather than a formal p-value the project cannot yet justify). No empirical false-alarm rate has ever been measured. Status: PLANNED, NOT IMPLEMENTED.

docs.title: 28.4 No pixel-level vetting (J1, NOT IMPLEMENTED — the largest single gap)
docs.text:
For any flagged candidate, nothing in this pipeline currently checks whether the dimming genuinely originates from the target star rather than a background eclipsing binary bleeding light into the photometric aperture. This is a real, well-known false-positive mode in transit photometry (aperture contamination), and it is currently uncatchable here.

Per Next Steps.md PART J: "Both reviews rank this the single biggest missing capability, and the README already admits it ('no pixel-level vetting yet')." Two independent external reviews (2026-09-15) converged on the same conclusion. The intended fix — inspecting the target pixel file (TPF) and checking dimming against source centroid position — belongs in src/exocomet/vetting/, which as of this writing is an empty directory. Status: PLANNED, NOT IMPLEMENTED. This is the project's own stated top-priority gap, not an assessment invented for this document.

docs.title: 28.5 Other stated limitations (from the README, current and accurate)
docs.text:
• Kepler has already been searched exhaustively, including a 2025 neural-network survey of all 201,820 stars. This pipeline is positioned as an independent-method cross-check with characterized sensitivity, not a discovery hunt over unexplored data.
  • A flagged event is a candidate, never a confirmed exocomet — confirmation requires follow-up (e.g. pixel-level vetting, spectroscopy, multi-epoch persistence) that this pipeline does not provide.
  • The detection-efficiency numbers reported anywhere prior to the A1/A4 fixes (window-sizing in physical time, ΔBIC+τ/σ flagging) are stale per Next Steps B8 and have not been re-measured since (see 26_performance.md §26.2).

docs.title: 28.6 What is explicitly NOT a limitation of this pipeline (scope boundary)
docs.text: Per 00_document_control.md's terminology section and the project's own standing rule, this document — and the project itself — never describes a flagged event as "confirmed." Every limitation above is a limitation on how much confidence a candidate deserves, not evidence that the underlying detection method itself is unsound; the validation gate (recovering all six published KIC 3542116 dips) remains the strongest available check that the core detrend → detect → score pipeline works at all.

docs.title: 29. Reliability
docs.text: Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051. Every incident below is a real, previously-hit failure, root-caused and (except where noted) fixed during development, drawn directly from Session Log 2026-09-15.md §4 and §11. These are not hypothetical failure modes — they were hit in production-shaped testing against real MAST data.

docs.title: 29.1 Incident 1 — the MAST "hang" was a truncated FITS file, not an infinite hang
docs.text:
Symptom (2026-09-14): a backtest step calling out to MAST appeared to hang for 9+ minutes with zero CPU progress, and was killed before ever completing.

What it actually was, confirmed 2026-09-15: after MAST-timeout hardening was added to io/download.py (bounded timeout + retry around search_lightcurve/download_all, explicit astroquery.mast.conf.timeout/pagesize configuration — the astroquery 0.4.11 API does not have the Observations.TIMEOUT attribute the original brief assumed), re-running the same backtest against the same dirty local cache failed in 31 seconds, not 9 minutes, with a clear error:

kplr003542116-2013098041711_llc.fits ... may be corrupt due to an interrupted download

Inspecting the file directly found it was exactly 65,536 bytes — 64 KiB, a round block boundary — the signature of a download that was killed mid-transfer, then cached as-is. An earlier claim in this same investigation ("17 complete, healthy FITS files" in the cache) was itself wrong: that check had only looked for files under 1 KB, not files truncated at a larger, round block size. The file was quarantined (moved aside, not deleted) rather than silently patched over.

Root cause: not an infinite hang in the network layer — a finite, well-defined failure against a poisoned local cache, previously mistaken for a hang because nothing bounded how long the retry loop would keep re-attempting the same doomed read.

docs.title: 29.2 Incident 2 — the ledger claimed success for a file that didn't exist
docs.text:
Symptom (2026-09-15, during real ingest.py testing against live MAST): the first single-target test run (KIC 1161345) printed "1 succeeded," but the extract file was missing from disk afterward when checked directly.

Root cause, found by tracing rather than dismissing the anomaly: a genuine, live recurrence of the same corruption class as Incident 1 — a truncated FITS file, this time for a different star — caused download_all to fail. But the deeper bug was in the retry mechanism itself: _call_with_retries retried the exact same call with no cleanup between attempts. A retry against a cache that is already poisoned by a truncated file fails identically on every attempt — it is not a retry in any meaningful sense, just the same guaranteed failure repeated on a timer, while the surrounding code went on to log a false success.

Fix: _call_with_retries gained an optional cleanup callback, wired at the download_all call site to _discard_cached(cache, target_id) — an existing helper, reused rather than reinvented — invoked between attempts. Re-tested against the same failing target after the fix: clean success. A belt-and-braces immediate readback check was also added right after save_extract in ingest.py, so a ledger line asserting success for an absent output file cannot recur silently even from some other, future cause.

Status: fixed and re-verified against live MAST data, then proven on a real GitHub Actions run (§29.4 below).

docs.title: 29.3 Incident 3 — the cache directory was silently wrong depending on working directory
docs.text:
Symptom: running ingest.py from inside scripts/ (matching the convention several sibling scripts already used) silently created scripts/data/raw/ instead of the repository-root cache location the rest of the codebase assumes exists.

Root cause: DEFAULT_CACHE_DIR = Path("data/raw") in the download module is a relative path, resolved against the process's current working directory — not against the repository root or the module's own file location. This had already been flagged as a known risk earlier in the same session (noted by the MAST-timeout-hardening work as "not trivially safe to change") before it actually manifested as a live bug.

Fix: ingest.py now computes an explicit raw_cache_dir from Path(__file__) — independent of the process's current working directory — and passes it into fetch_light_curve rather than relying on the library's CWD-relative default.

docs.title: 29.4 Verification: proven end-to-end on GitHub's own infrastructure
docs.text: After both fixes above, the full scripts/ingest.py pipeline (fetch → save extract → delete FITS → detect → save results → append ledger) was run for real, watched, on an actual GitHub Actions runner via workflow_dispatch (capped to a 3-minute budget, 1 target). Every step succeeded — checkout, install, clone the data repo, real MAST fetch, detrend, detect, save results, test suite — on GitHub's infrastructure, not a local machine. The only step that failed was the final push to exocomet-hunter-data, with the expected, correctly-diagnosed error Invalid username or token — because DATA_REPO_TOKEN did not yet exist as a repository secret at that point in time. This has since been resolved (Session Log 2026-09-15 §12): the token was added, ingest.yml was re-triggered, and the push succeeded, independently confirmed via the GitHub API that real files landed in the data repository.

docs.title: 29.5 A known, unrelated infrastructure quirk (not a code bug)
docs.text: git push to AJpro-merc/exocomet-hunter from this development machine fails under a plain git push because the machine's active gh credential is for a different account (elpis-app), not AJpro-merc. The workaround used throughout (and by the CI workflows themselves) is pushing through an explicit https://AJpro-merc:<token>@github.com/... URL obtained via gh auth token -u AJpro-merc. A persistent local credential-config fix (rather than rediscovering this workaround each session) is listed in Next Steps.md's "FIRST THING NEXT SESSION" as still outstanding. See 41_troubleshooting.md for the full incident, including its GitHub Actions compute-burning counterpart.

docs.title: 29.6 Summary
docs.text: Incident Root cause Fixed? MAST "hang" 65,536-byte truncated FITS file from an interrupted download, retried against the same poisoned cache with no cleanup Yes — timeout/retry hardening + cache quarantine Ledger false success _call_with_retries had no cleanup callback between attempts, so retries against a poisoned cache failed identically every time while a success was logged Yes — cleanup callback added, wired to cache discard; readback check added after save_extract CWD-relative cache path DEFAULT_CACHE_DIR = Path("data/raw") resolved against process CWD, not repo root Yes — ingest.py computes an explicit path from Path(__file__) git push account mismatch Local gh credential is for a different GitHub account than the repo needs Workaround in place (explicit token URL); a persistent fix is still outstanding

docs.title: 30. Future Detectors
docs.text: Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051. This section covers Next Steps.md PART H, item H4 — a second Detector subclass, entirely unbuilt. PLANNED, NOT IMPLEMENTED.

docs.title: 30.1 H4 — Technosignature / anomalous-dimming detector (PLANNED, NOT IMPLEMENTED)
docs.text:
Quoted from Next Steps.md PART H, verbatim:

H4. Project 2 — technosignature / anomalous dimming. New Detector subclass (Isolation Forest on light-curve features), validated on Boyajian's Star (KIC 8462852), reusing io/, detrend/, core/, vetting/.

Nothing beyond this scoping sentence exists. There is no IsolationForestDetector class, no feature set defined for it, no code referencing KIC 8462852, and no test file anywhere in src/ or tests/ related to this idea. A repository-wide search for "Boyajian" or "8462852" returns no source-code hits — only this planning note.

docs.title: 30.2 Why this is architecturally cheap to add later (design intent, not a built capability)
docs.text:
The project's stated design rationale (README, "Design" section) is that Detector is an abstract base class specifically so that a different kind of search does not require modifying the existing exocomet pipeline:

The package is a framework, not a script. Detector is an abstract base class; the exocomet detector is its first implementation. Adding a different search — the planned anomalous-dimming (technosignature) detector, for instance — means writing one class, not modifying the pipeline.

This is a real architectural claim about core/interfaces.py's Detector abstraction, and it is consistent with how AsymmetricDipDetector is structured (it is the only concrete Detector subclass in the codebase today). Whether that abstraction genuinely accommodates an Isolation-Forest-based whole-light-curve anomaly detector without modification is untested — no second detector has ever been written against it, so the claim that "one class" would suffice is a design intention, not a verified fact.

docs.title: 30.3 What H4 would need, per its own one-line scope
docs.text:
• A new Detector subclass performing unsupervised anomaly detection (Isolation Forest, per the note) over light-curve-level features, rather than the existing pipeline's per-event dip detection and shape-model comparison.
  • Reuse of io/ (fetching/caching light curves), detrend/ (the existing Savitzky-Golay/spline detrending), and core/ (shared types) — plausible given those modules have no dependency on the exocomet-specific detection logic.
  • Reuse of vetting/ — currently an empty directory (see 28_limitations.md §28.4); H4 reusing something that does not yet exist is itself a dependency worth noting, separate from H4's own PLANNED status.
  • Validation against Boyajian's Star (KIC 8462852), the well-known real anomalous-dimming target, analogous to how the exocomet detector is validated against KIC 3542116's published dips.

docs.title: 30.4 Status summary
docs.text: Item Status IsolationForestDetector (or equivalent) class NOT IMPLEMENTED Feature set for whole-light-curve anomaly scoring NOT IMPLEMENTED KIC 8462852 validation NOT IMPLEMENTED — no code references this target Reuse of vetting/ Blocked on vetting/ itself existing (see §28.4) Overall PLANNED. This is explicitly listed in Next Steps.md PART H as "later, agreed but parked" — not scheduled for near-term work.

docs.title: 31. Machine Learning
docs.text: Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051. This is the single most important accuracy checkpoint in this specification. The goal of PART C (Next Steps.md) is to replace the hand-set ΔBIC+τ/σ flagging rule (research log 007, detect/scoring.py) with a trained classifier, and to measure how good it is before trusting it. As of this commit, that measurement has never happened. Read this section literally — no accuracy, precision, recall, ROC-AUC, or any other classifier-quality number is stated anywhere below, because none exist.

docs.title: 31.1 C1 — Labelled training set generator: BUILT — scripts/generate_training_labels.py
docs.text:
Status: IMPLEMENTED.

For each host star, the script downloads the light curve once (discard_after_read=True — raw photometry is never retained), then for each label class either injects a synthetic event or takes a real/time-reversed detection, runs the unmodified production detector (AsymmetricDipDetector) on it, and — if a matching candidate resulted — extracts its 19 features (calibration/features.py::FEATURE_NAMES) and records one labelled row.

Seven classes, not the original five (confirmed directly from source, ALL_CLASSES in generate_training_labels.py):

  • comet, symmetric, reversed — localized asymmetric-dip shapes, matched to a specific injected epoch within match_tolerance_days.
  • flare — localized false-positive lookalike (Next Steps D1).
  • starspot — whole-light-curve sinusoidal modulation (period 0.5–30 d), matched to the nearest detection to a random anchor time rather than a single true epoch.
  • noise — no injection at all; a real detection on real, unmodified data.
  • time_reversed_real — a real light curve with flux reversed in time.

Depth/amplitude sampling (DEPTH_GRID_PPM = (200, 300, 500, 750, 1000, 1500, 2000, 3000), weighted (1, 2, 3, 4, 4, 3, 2, 1)) is deliberately weighted toward the 500–2000 ppm region — the genuinely uncertain detection boundary — rather than sampled uniformly.

Hard hold-out enforcement: EXCLUDED_HOLD_OUT_TARGETS (from build_kepler_host_list.py) is asserted absent from the host list before generation starts (assert not (set(hosts) & EXCLUDED_HOLD_OUT_TARGETS)), and the same list is checked again at load time in train_classifier.py (§31.2). KIC 3542116 and KIC 11084727 — the validation targets — must never appear in training data.

A real bug found and fixed (2026-09-14): the generator originally never detrended before running the detector — every row generated before the fix ran on raw, undetrended flux. This was caught before anything untrustworthy had been committed anywhere, so no cleanup was needed, but it is a real, documented finding, not a hypothetical.

Output: one row per detected event — 19 features (from FEATURE_NAMES) plus label, host_star, injected_depth, injected_tau_over_sigma, seed, author, exptime. Runs recurringly via .github/workflows/train.yml (GitHub Actions, every 2 hours) and by hand. Real accumulated output lives in the external AJpro-merc/exocomet-hunter-data repository (training/labels_kepler.parquet, training/labels_tess.parquet — see 33_results.md), not in this repository's git history.

docs.title: 31.2 C2 — Train: BUILT — scripts/train_classifier.py
docs.text:
Status: IMPLEMENTED, backtest status improved since the last recorded log entry — verify current claim below.

Model: RandomForestClassifier (n_estimators=200, class_weight="balanced") wrapped in CalibratedClassifierCV (method="isotonic", cv=3). Confirmed directly from source: this is exactly what is implemented, no more and no less. HistGradientBoostingClassifier or a logistic-regression comparison model — mentioned in Next Steps as a possible "second model" — is not built.

Binary target, not the original 5/7-class framing: y = (df["label"] == "comet").astype(int) — comet versus every other class collapsed into one negative class. This matches C4's eventual comet_probability output directly (a single probability of "is this a comet," not a multi-class label).

Missing-value handling: SimpleImputer(strategy="median") plus an is_measurable indicator array appended per feature (_build_pipeline_inputs hstacks the imputed features with a same-shaped 0/1 "was this finite before imputation" matrix) — exactly as specified in Next Steps C2.

Split by host star: GroupKFold on host_star, used only to produce out-of-fold (OOF) predictions for threshold selection and completeness measurement (train_and_cross_validate). The final saved model is refit on the full dataset after OOF predictions are computed — standard practice, and correctly distinguished in the code and its docstring from the OOF predictions themselves.

Class imbalance: class_weight="balanced" on the underlying RandomForestClassifier.

Calibrated probabilities: CalibratedClassifierCV, isotonic method, as specified.

Hold-out enforcement — a hard exception, not a warning: load_labels() raises HoldOutError (a RuntimeError subclass) if either hold-out star's data is present in the input parquet files, and main() catches it, logs, and returns exit code 1 — training refuses to proceed rather than silently including hold-out data.

Provenance: models/manifest_<mission>.jsonl (append-only) records row count, class counts (df["label"].value_counts()), host-star list, training_set_hash (SHA-256 over the input parquet bytes), package versions (exocomet, scikit-learn, pandas, numpy — via importlib.metadata.version, degrading to "unknown" rather than raising), the chosen threshold, and both backtest results described below. A models/last_compare.json optionally records a before/after comparison against the immediately preceding manifest entry — for visibility, explicitly not a gate: the code comment states the locked decision is "always commit, never silently withhold a worse model."

The threshold itself is chosen from OOF negative-class scores at a fixed target false-positive rate: TARGET_FALSE_POSITIVE_RATE = 0.01 (1%), via np.quantile(negative_scores, 1.0 - 0.01). This is a real, implemented mechanism — but it is a training-time heuristic for picking a number, not the same thing as C3's "measure recall at 1% FPR" evaluation deliverable (§31.3). The threshold is selected using this rule; whether the resulting classifier's actual recall at that FPR is good has never been separately reported (that is exactly what C3 would do and has not done).

Two backtests are wired into train_classifier.py and run automatically on every training run:

  1. real_data_backtest() — fetches the real KIC 3542116 light curve live (never trained on — enforced by load_labels's hard exception), matches its 6 published dips within the configured tolerance, extracts features for each matched candidate, scores it with the just-trained model, and reports how many of the 6 score above the chosen threshold. This is a real, functioning code path that requires live network access to MAST.
  2. completeness_by_depth() — uses the already-computed OOF predictions, grouped by injected_depth, to report the classifier's own recovery fraction versus injected depth (distinct from the hand-rule completeness table measured earlier in the project).

On verification status: Next Steps.md (last updated 2026-09-16, the same date as this document) states C2 as "✅ built 2026-09-14, ⚠️ not fully verified", with the specific concern being that the real_data_backtest() network step hung for 9+ minutes and was killed before completing, in testing prior to the MAST-hang root-cause fix described in 29_reliability.md §29.1. That MAST-hang root cause (a truncated FITS file retried against a poisoned cache with no cleanup) has since been fixed and re-verified against live MAST data (Session Log 2026-09-15 §4, §11) — but that verification was performed inside ingest.py's fetch path, not inside a specifically-watched, complete run of train_classifier.py's real_data_backtest() function itself end-to-end with a real training set. No session log or manifest entry in this repository documents a completed, successful run of real_data_backtest() that produced a real backtest score. Until such a run is observed and recorded, this document treats C2's backtest step as: the underlying network-hang cause is fixed, but a full, successful, watched execution of this specific function has not been independently confirmed in any source read for this document. Status: IMPLEMENTED, UNVERIFIED (the specific concern from the last log entry is very likely resolved given the underlying root-cause fix, but no completed run of this exact function is documented anywhere read for this section — do not report a real-data-backtest score for KIC 3542116 as an established fact until a manifest entry containing one is found).

docs.title: 31.3 C3 — Evaluate: NOT IMPLEMENTED, NO EVALUATION NUMBERS EXIST
docs.text:
This is the deliverable that has not happened. State this plainly, because it is the easiest place in this entire specification to accidentally fabricate a number.

Next Steps PART C, item C3 specifies exactly what must be produced:

  • ROC-AUC and precision-recall AUC (PR stated as mattering more, since comets are rare).
  • Recall at a fixed false-positive rate of 1%.
  • Confusion matrix across the classes.
  • A completeness curve versus injected depth and versus τ/σ, compared against the hand rule.
  • Permutation feature importance.
  • The "final exam": all 6 KIC 3542116 dips must score above the chosen threshold.
  • A write-up in docs/research_log/006-classifier-v1.md, including what failed.

None of this exists. Specifically, verified by direct inspection:

  • No file named docs/research_log/006-classifier-v1.md exists. (docs/research_log/ contains exactly three files: 003-half-depth-contour-sign-error.md, 006-depth-offset-investigation.md, 007-delta-bic-is-direction-blind.md — note that 006 is already taken by the depth-offset investigation, a numbering collision with C3's proposed filename that would need resolving whenever C3 is actually written.)
  • No standalone ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, or "recall at 1% FPR" figure is reported anywhere in the codebase, the manifests, or any research log. The TARGET_FALSE_POSITIVE_RATE = 0.01 constant in train_classifier.py is used to choose a threshold, which is a different act from measuring and reporting the resulting recall at that operating point as a standalone evaluation metric — the latter has never been computed and printed/logged/written anywhere.
  • No confusion matrix has been generated.
  • No permutation feature importance has been computed.
  • No completeness-curve comparison between the classifier and the hand rule exists — completeness_by_depth() (§31.2) produces per-run numbers inside a manifest entry, which is the raw ingredient for such a curve, but no comparison figure or table against the ΔBIC+τ/σ hand rule's own completeness has been assembled.
  • The "final exam" (all 6 KIC 3542116 dips above threshold) has never been formally reported as a pass/fail result with an accompanying write-up, independent of whatever real_data_backtest() may or may not have printed to a training-run's stdout log (see §31.2's verification caveat).

Status: C3 NOT IMPLEMENTED / NOT RUN. Do not invent accuracy, precision, recall, ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, or completeness numbers for this classifier anywhere in this specification or elsewhere. If a manifest file (models/manifest_kepler.jsonl or similar) is later found in the external data repository containing a real real_data_backtest result from an actual training run, that specific manifest entry's numbers are real, dated, sourced data and may be cited by their own manifest-provenance fields (date, training-set hash, package versions) — but as of the sources read for this document, models/ in the external exocomet-hunter-data repository contains only a .gitkeep placeholder (confirmed by direct clone and listing, 2026-09-16 — see 33_results.md). No trained model artifact and no manifest entry currently exist anywhere.

docs.title: 31.4 C4 — Wire it in: BLOCKED on C3
docs.text:
Status: NOT IMPLEMENTED, correctly blocked.

Next Steps C4 specifies adding score.comet_probability to EventScore and to_row(), changing the flagging rule to flagged = comet_probability >= threshold (threshold chosen from C3's 1%-FPR measurement), and retaining the current physics-based ΔBIC+τ/σ rule as a reported comparison column.

Confirmed by direct inspection of core/types.py: EventScore has no comet_probability field, and CandidateRecord.to_row() has no such column. The production flagging rule remains exactly the ΔBIC+τ/σ conjunction from research log 007 (detect/scoring.py::score_event). This is the correct state given C3 has not produced a threshold to wire in — implementing C4 before C3 exists would mean choosing an arbitrary, unmeasured threshold, which the project's own standing discipline (never invent precision the numbers don't support — see Next Steps.md PART J's explicit rejection of an invented "0-100 Priority Score" for the same reason) argues against.

docs.title: 31.5 Summary table
docs.text: Item Status Evidence C1 — labelled training set generator IMPLEMENTED scripts/generate_training_labels.py, 7 classes, hold-out enforced C2 — train (RandomForest + CalibratedClassifierCV) IMPLEMENTED, backtest UNVERIFIED (root cause of prior hang fixed, but no confirmed completed run of real_data_backtest() found) scripts/train_classifier.py C3 — evaluate (ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, recall@1%FPR, confusion matrix, completeness, permutation importance, 6-dip exam) NOT IMPLEMENTED / NOT RUN — no numbers exist No models/manifest_*.jsonl found in the data repo beyond a .gitkeep; no docs/research_log/006-classifier-v1.md C4 — wire comet_probability into scoring NOT IMPLEMENTED, correctly BLOCKED on C3 EventScore/to_row() have no such field; flagging rule unchanged from research log 007

docs.title: 32. Visualization
docs.text:
Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051. Function list and behavior below are read directly from src/exocomet/viz/plots.py. All figures are written to disk via a non-interactive Matplotlib backend (matplotlib.use("Agg"), set at module import) — nothing in this module ever opens an interactive window, per the module docstring: "figures are written to disk, never shown interactively."

Module docstring framing (quoted, since it states the design intent precisely): "Plots here are working instruments, not decoration: the per-event figure exists so that a human can check what the asymmetry measurement actually did ... A detection that looks wrong on this plot is wrong, whatever the numbers say."

__all__ exports exactly five public functions: plot_asymmetry_distribution, plot_detrend_comparison, plot_event, plot_light_curve, plot_tail_direction.

docs.title: 32.1 plot_light_curve(lc, events=None, known_epochs=None, path=None, title=None)
docs.text: Plots a full light curve as relative flux in ppm versus time. Detected events (list[DipEvent]) are shaded as vertical bands (axvspan, blue, alpha 0.25) over their window. Published/known epochs (dict[str, float], label → time) are drawn as red dashed vertical lines with the label annotated above — this is what makes "recovered versus missed" visible at a glance against literature values. Title defaults to "{target_id} — {n_points:,} cadences, {baseline_days:.0f} d" if not given. Returns the saved Path, or None if path is None (the figure is still built and closed either way via the internal _save helper, which creates parent directories as needed and saves at 150 dpi with tight bounding box).

docs.title: 32.2 plot_detrend_comparison(raw, detrended, path=None, window_days=None, centre=None)
docs.text: Two stacked subplots (raw normalized flux on top, detrended flux below), sharing an x-axis, both in ppm. Answers, per its own docstring, "did the filter remove the trend without eating the dip?" If centre and window_days are both given, the top panel's x-axis is zoomed to that window so a specific event can be inspected before/after. The bottom panel's x-axis label reports the post-detrend scatter as a robust MAD-based estimate (1.4826 * median(|detrended.flux - median(detrended.flux)|) * 1e6, in ppm) directly in the axis label text.

docs.title: 32.3 plot_event(lc, record, baseline=None, path=None, pad_factor=3.0, known_epoch=None)
docs.text:
The primary per-event diagnostic figure. Plots flux with error bars (ax.errorbar) over a window padded to pad_factor times the event's duration around its minimum. If a baseline array is supplied, it is overplotted in green and used to compute the local out-of-dip level; otherwise the level defaults to 1.0. Marks:

  • The detection window as a shaded blue span.
  • The fitted minimum (event.t_min) as a solid blue vertical line.
  • A known/published epoch, if given, as a red dashed line.
  • The half-depth level as a dotted orange horizontal line (only if event.asymmetry is not None).
  • Both half-depth crossing times (ingress in purple, egress in brown) as dotted vertical lines.

The title reports depth_ppm, ingress/egress durations in hours, A_dur, A_slope, ΔBIC, and flagged when the event is measurable; when it is not (event.asymmetry is None), the title instead reports event.unmeasurable_reason. This is the figure the module docstring refers to directly — every number the score depends on is drawn on top of the data, so a wrong number is visible as a wrong picture.

docs.title: 32.4 plot_asymmetry_distribution(records, path=None, threshold=None)
docs.text: A histogram of the duration-asymmetry statistic a_dur across a whole batch of CandidateRecords, with all measurable events in gray and the subset that were flagged overlaid in blue on the same bins (np.linspace(-1, 1, 41)). An optional threshold is drawn as a red dashed vertical line. Answers, per its docstring, "whether flagged events are a distinct population or the tail of an ordinary one" — a population-level sanity check on the flagging rule rather than a single-event diagnostic.

docs.title: 32.5 plot_tail_direction(path=None, config=None, depth=2.0e-3, fast_ramp_days=0.1, slow_ramp_days=0.5, noise_sigma=1.0e-4)
docs.text: The figure behind research log 007's finding. Builds two entirely synthetic, in-memory light curves (Kepler long-cadence sampling, 2000 points, Gaussian noise) via the internal _inject_ramped_dip helper — a piecewise-linear dip with independently controllable ingress/egress durations, not the same comet_profile/symmetric_profile shapes used by the detector's own model comparison. One event has a fast ingress and slow egress (the physical, trailing-tail comet case); the other is its exact mirror image (a leading tail, which no real dust tail produces). Both are run through the real, unmodified AsymmetricDipDetector, and the two-panel figure annotates each with its actual ΔBIC, τ/σ, A_dur, and flagged/not-flagged verdict, color-coded green/red. Everything in this function is generated in-process — nothing is read from disk or network — specifically so the figure is reproducible from source alone. This is the direct evidence underlying the claim in research log 007 that ΔBIC alone is direction-blind and the τ/σ condition is load-bearing (see 28_limitations.md and 31_machine_learning.md context, and 05_detection_theory.md for the scoring rule itself).

docs.title: 32.6 Shared conventions
docs.text:
• All flux values are plotted as (flux - 1.0) * 1e6, i.e. relative flux in parts-per-million, via the module-level PPM = 1.0e6 constant — consistent with how depths are reported everywhere else in the codebase (DipEvent.depth_ppm).
  • Every function accepts path: Path | str | None; passing None builds and immediately discards the figure (useful for tests that only check the function doesn't raise) — see the internal _save() helper, which is the single point where figures are written and closed (plt.close(fig)), avoiding figure-handle leaks across repeated calls.
  • No function in this module performs network access or reads files other than what is passed in as arguments — all data dependencies are explicit parameters.

docs.title: 33. Results Repository
docs.text: Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16. This section describes the external AJpro-merc/exocomet-hunter-data repository, verified directly by cloning it fresh (git clone https://github.com/AJpro-merc/exocomet-hunter-data.git) and listing its contents on 2026-09-16 — not by reading a description of it.

docs.title: 33.1 Why a separate repository
docs.text: Per that repository's own README.md (quoted): "Not a scientific product on its own. Every row here is either synthetic (a fake comet/flare/starspot/etc. shape injected into a real light curve) or a plain detection on unmodified real photometry, produced by the code in the main repo." It exists so that recurring, automated GitHub Actions jobs (ingest.yml, train.yml) have somewhere to commit generated artifacts without growing the main exocomet-hunter repository's git history with binary/data churn. Source photometry itself (raw FITS) is never stored here — only small, derived measurements.

docs.title: 33.2 Real directory layout, as of 2026-09-16
docs.text:
exocomet-hunter-data/
├── README.md
├── ledger.jsonl                       # 33 lines (append-only, one JSON object per attempt)
├── extract/
│   ├── Kepler/                        # 17 parquet files, e.g. KIC_1161345.parquet
│   └── TESS/                          # 7 parquet files, e.g. beta_Pic.parquet
├── results/
│   ├── Kepler/                        # 17 .jsonl files, one per target in extract/Kepler
│   └── TESS/                          # 7 .jsonl files, one per target in extract/TESS
├── models/
│   └── .gitkeep                       # EMPTY — no trained model or manifest committed yet
└── training/
    └── .gitkeep                       # EMPTY — no accumulated label parquet committed yet

Every extract/<mission>/<target>.parquet file has a matching results/<mission>/<target>.jsonl file, and both are referenced from ledger.jsonl — e.g. one ledger line reads:

{"target_id": "KIC 1161345", "mission": "Kepler", "status": "success", "timestamp_utc": "2026-09-15T17:51:45.851701+00:00", "attempt": 1, "error": null, "extract_path": "extract/Kepler/KIC_1161345.parquet", "results_path": "results/Kepler/KIC_1161345.jsonl"}

This is real, live output from scripts/ingest.py running on the hourly ingest.yml GitHub Actions schedule (confirmed enabled and active per Session Log 2026-09-15 §12), against the 33 hardcoded seed targets (23 Kepler + 10 TESS) described in Next Steps.md.

docs.title: 33.3 models/ and training/ are currently empty — directly relevant to 31_machine_learning.md
docs.text: Both directories contain only a .gitkeep placeholder file, confirmed by direct listing. This independently corroborates the C3 finding in 31_machine_learning.md: no trained classifier artifact (.joblib), no manifest_<mission>.jsonl provenance file, and no accumulated labels_<mission>.parquet training set have ever been committed to this repository. scripts/train_classifier.py (C2) and scripts/generate_training_labels.py (C1) are both implemented and runnable, but their outputs — per this direct check of the one place those outputs would land — do not yet exist anywhere durable. .github/workflows/train.yml runs the generation step on a 2-hour schedule per its own design (Session Log 2026-09-15 §5), but as of this repository snapshot has not yet produced or committed a training/labels_*.parquet file that survived to be pushed, or a direct clone of the data repo would have found it.

docs.title: 33.4 Per-mission layout described in the data repo's own README
docs.text:
Quoted directly, since it is the authoritative description of intended (not necessarily yet populated) layout:

  • training/labels_kepler.parquet — labelled feature rows, Kepler track. Described as "safe, no open correctness bugs."
  • training/labels_tess.parquet — labelled feature rows, TESS track. Exists only post-A2-fix (the TESS cadence/pipeline pinning fix).
  • models/*.joblib — trained classifier(s), overwritten weekly, no dated snapshots — full history lives in the manifest instead.
  • models/manifest_*.jsonl — one line per training run (see 31_machine_learning.md §31.2 for exact fields).
  • models/last_compare.json — most recent run's backtest scores versus the previous run's, for spotting regressions; "the model still gets committed either way — this is visibility, not a gate."
  • models/threshold_*.json — the probability cutoff chosen per model.

All of the above are described as append-only by convention (manifests never rewritten) and generated automatically by .github/workflows/train.yml, unattended.

docs.title: 33.5 Summary

Contents extract/Kepler/, extract/TESS/ Yes 17 + 7 parquet extracts, one per processed target results/Kepler/, results/TESS/ Yes 17 + 7 .jsonl detection-result files, matching extracts ledger.jsonl Yes 33 append-only attempt records training/ No — .gitkeep only No labelled training set has been committed models/ No — .gitkeep only No trained model, manifest, threshold, or comparison file has been committed

docs.title: 34. Development
docs.text: Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051. Commands below are drawn from pyproject.toml's actual configuration and Next Steps.md's "Reference: commands that are easy to forget" section — nothing here is invented tooling.

docs.title: 34.1 Install
docs.text:
cd exocomet-hunter
python3.12 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[dev]"

requires-python = ">=3.11" (pyproject.toml); the README's own install instructions use python3.12 explicitly. The [dev] extra pulls in pytest, pytest-cov, pytest-benchmark, hypothesis, mypy, ruff, black, pre-commit, pandas-stubs, types-PyYAML. A separate [docs] extra (mkdocs-material, mkdocstrings[python]) exists for building documentation — G2 in Next Steps.md (a deployed MkDocs site) is PLANNED, not built; the dependency is declared but no mkdocs.yml or docs-site build has shipped.

docs.title: 34.2 Console entry point
docs.text:
[project.scripts]
exocomet = "exocomet.cli:main"

Once installed (pip install -e .), the exocomet command is available directly:

exocomet run "KIC 3542116" --mission Kepler
exocomet validate
exocomet inject --n 20

See 35_code_reference/cli.md for the full subcommand reference.

docs.title: 34.3 Run the pipeline directly (without the installed console script)
docs.text:
from exocomet.io.download import fetch_light_curve
from exocomet.detrend.detrend import detrend_savgol
from exocomet.detect.comet_detector import AsymmetricDipDetector

lc = detrend_savgol(fetch_light_curve("KIC 3542116", mission="Kepler"))
for record in AsymmetricDipDetector().run(lc):
    if record.score.flagged:
        print(record.event.t_min, record.event.depth_ppm, record.score.delta_bic)

(As given in README.md, "Use" section.)

docs.title: 34.4 Test
docs.text:
pytest tests/unit -q                     # 167 tests, ~4 s (measured 2026-09-16, see 27_testing.md)
pytest tests/integration -m network       # requires live MAST access
pytest --cov=exocomet tests/unit          # configured, never yet run — see 27_testing.md §27.3

pyproject.toml's [tool.pytest.ini_options] defines network and slow custom markers; -m "not network" deselects network tests explicitly if needed (the default testpaths = ["tests"] with addopts = "-ra --strict-markers" means an undeclared marker is a hard error, not a silent typo).

ruff check src tests                     # 34 findings as of 2026-09-16 — not yet clean, see 27_testing.md §27.4
ruff check src tests --fix               # would auto-fix 12 of the 34
mypy                                     # currently blocked by a NumPy-stub/Python-version mismatch, see 27_testing.md §27.5

python scripts/generate_training_labels.py --n-per-class 20 --out data/training/labels_v1.parquet --mission Kepler
python scripts/train_classifier.py --in labels_kepler.parquet --out-model models/kepler.joblib --manifest-out models/manifest_kepler.jsonl

python scripts/ingest.py                 # fetch -> extract -> detect -> results -> ledger, resumable
