docs.title: 34.8 GitHub Actions workflow management — needs the right gh account
docs.text:
Per Next Steps.md's own "easy to forget" reference, verbatim, because the active local gh account (elpis-app) is not the account these repositories belong to (AJpro-merc) — see 41_troubleshooting.md for the full incident this workaround exists to route around:

GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token -u AJpro-merc) gh run list --workflow=survey.yml
GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token -u AJpro-merc) gh workflow run survey.yml -f dry_run=true
GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token -u AJpro-merc) gh workflow disable survey.yml

# git push already works inside the repo (local credential config set)
git push

Three workflows exist in .github/workflows/ as of this commit: ingest.yml (hourly, active), train.yml (every 2h generation + weekly training, disabled pending the pre-squash-commit re-anchor described in 41_troubleshooting.md), survey.yml (daily, disabled pending A1/A2/A4 — all three of which are now done per Next Steps.md, so re-enabling is a live decision outstanding, not a code blocker).

docs.title: 34.9 Ruff/mypy/pytest configuration reference (pyproject.toml, verbatim key settings)
docs.text:
• [tool.ruff]: line-length = 100, target-version = "py311", rule sets E, W, F, I, N, D, UP, B, SIM, NPY, RUF selected; D105, D107, N803, N806 explicitly ignored (the latter two to allow the paper's own uppercase notation, e.g. A_dur); pydocstyle convention is numpy; tests/* and scripts/* get relaxed docstring requirements via per-file ignores.
  • [tool.mypy]: python_version = "3.11", strict = true, warn_unreachable = true, scoped to files = ["src/exocomet"] only (tests and scripts are not mypy-checked); third-party libraries without stubs (lightkurve, astroquery, astropy, scipy, matplotlib, pyarrow) have ignore_missing_imports = true.
  • [tool.coverage.run]/[tool.coverage.report]: source scoped to src/exocomet, branch coverage enabled, standard exclusion patterns for pragma: no cover, TYPE_CHECKING blocks, NotImplementedError, and @abstractmethod.

docs.title: 36. Research Integrity
docs.text: Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051. This section states the project's real, currently enforced rules — some in code, some as documented and consistently followed conventions — and separately flags what is agreed but not yet operationalized as a formal process.

docs.title: 36.1 An AI never decides what counts as a comet (H1's design principle)
docs.text:
Next Steps.md PART H, item H1 states the rule for a planned AI-review layer:

Rule: the model never decides whether something is a comet. It receives only computed features (JSON), returns structured JSON: evidence for, evidence against, alternative explanations, recommended next test, and must be allowed to answer insufficient_evidence. Use it as a skeptic, not a cheerleader.

Status: H1 itself is PLANNED, NOT IMPLEMENTED — no code in this repository currently sends candidate features to an external AI model for review. But the principle it encodes is already load-bearing elsewhere in the actually-built pipeline: every classification decision that exists today (the ΔBIC+τ/σ flagging rule in detect/scoring.py, research log 007) is a deterministic, documented, config-driven statistical rule — not a model output treated as ground truth. The eventual C2/C3/C4 classifier (31_machine_learning.md) is explicitly scoped as replacing a hand-set rule with a measured one, never as an opaque authority: C3's entire purpose is to produce numbers a human can inspect and decide whether to trust, and C4's design keeps the physics-based rule as "a reported fallback column so the two can be compared" rather than retiring it silently.

PART I of Next Steps.md sharpens this further for the still-parked "AI skeptic" idea: "it may summarize, critique, propose alternative explanations, and suggest next tests; it may never alter a measurement, compute an authoritative statistic, silently change a label, or claim a discovery." This remains a design intention (PLANNED), not a built guardrail, since no such component exists yet.

docs.title: 36.2 Candidate ≠ confirmation — enforced by convention throughout the project
docs.text: Every document in this specification, the README, and every research log consistently uses "candidate" or "candidate event" or "exocomet-like morphology" for a flagged detection, and never "confirmed" or "discovery." This is stated explicitly in the README's "Honest limitations" section: "A flagged event is a candidate, never a confirmed exocomet. Confirmation needs follow-up this pipeline cannot provide." 00_document_control.md §0.4 repeats the same distinction as a defined term. This is a documentation and naming convention enforced by consistent usage, not a runtime code check — there is no assertion anywhere in the codebase that would prevent a future contributor from writing the word "confirmed" into an output field. Its enforcement is textual and cultural, verified here by the absence of any contradicting instance found while reading the project's source and documentation for this specification.

docs.title: 36.3 The blind-search protocol (D3) — PLANNED, not yet executed as a formal process
docs.text:
Next Steps.md PART D, item D3 specifies:

  1. Tune everything only on the development set (validation stars + injections).
  2. Commit and tag the frozen configuration, e.g. v0.2-frozen.
  3. Only then run on the search targets. Record the tag in every result.
  4. Any change after looking at search results → new tag, and say so in the write-up.

Status: PLANNED, NOT IMPLEMENTED as a formal, followed process. No git tag matching a pattern like v0.2-frozen was found referenced in any session log or research log read for this document, and no result file anywhere records "produced under tag X." The project's actual development pattern to date has been iterative — thresholds and the flagging rule itself were changed multiple times in direct response to findings against the validation targets (research logs 003 and 007 are both examples of exactly this: tune, observe a problem against KIC 3542116, fix, re-test against the same target). This is legitimate development methodology but is explicitly not the disciplined tune-freeze-run-once separation D3 describes, and the project's own tracker does not claim otherwise — D3 is correctly marked PLANNED there, not "done differently."

docs.title: 36.4 What "research integrity" means concretely in this project, today
docs.text:
Given the above, the actually-operative integrity controls in this codebase, as of this commit, are:

  • A hard-coded hold-out list (EXCLUDED_HOLD_OUT_TARGETS) that a training run cannot bypass without the code raising HoldOutError (31_machine_learning.md §31.2) — this one is a real runtime enforcement, not just a convention.
  • A validation gate (exocomet validate, scripts/run_validation.py) that exits non-zero on any missed published dip.
  • Consistent "candidate, not confirmation" language, enforced by convention/review rather than code.
  • A documented research log recording negative and inconclusive results, not only successes — research log 006 (the depth-offset investigation) is explicitly titled "partially explained, not resolved" and states plainly what it did not resolve; this document's own §31.3 follows the same discipline for the classifier.

What is not yet in place: an external, disinterested review of any specific candidate; a formally frozen and tagged configuration used for a genuine blind run; and an operating AI-skeptic component. All three are named, agreed-upon future work (H1, D3, PART I), not silently abandoned ideas.

docs.title: 37. References
docs.text: Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051. Every citation below is confirmed present in README.md, config/validation_targets.yaml, or a docs/research_log/*.md file — no reference has been added that is not already cited somewhere in this codebase.

docs.title: 37.1 Primary scientific literature
docs.text:
Rappaport, S., et al. 2018, MNRAS 474(2), 1453 — "Likely transiting exocomets detected by Kepler" (arXiv:1708.06069)

The foundational paper for this project. KIC 3542116's six published transit epochs and depths (491–1900 ppm) come directly from this paper's Table 3 and are transcribed into config/validation_targets.yaml as the primary validation gate. KIC 11084727 is this paper's secondary target (currently missing its epoch in this codebase's config — Next Steps B5, 28_limitations.md context). Cited in the README's "References" section, in config/validation_targets.yaml's header comments, and in research logs 003, 006, and 007.

Kennedy, G., et al. 2019, MNRAS 482(4), 5587 — "An automated search for transiting exocomets" (arXiv:1811.03102)

Cited in the README's "References" section. Also cited directly in detect/model_comparison.py's module docstring as the source of the symmetric-vs-comet-profile model-comparison methodology this pipeline implements: "The established approach in the exocomet literature (Kennedy et al. 2019) is instead to fit two competing profiles to each event and compare them." Cited again in research log 007's reference list.

Kass, R. E. & Raftery, A. E. 1995, JASA 90, 773 — "Bayes Factors"

Cited in research log 007's reference list as the source of the "ΔBIC > 10 = strong evidence" convention used as the delta_bic_threshold default in config/thresholds.yaml and ScoringConfig. This is the only reference in the codebase for a statistical-methods paper rather than an exocomet-specific one.

docs.title: 37.2 Software citations (README, "Data sources" and "References" sections)
docs.text:
• Lightkurve Collaboration — lightkurve, the primary interface used to fetch and manipulate Kepler/TESS photometry (io/download.py).
  • Astropy — used directly for astropy.timeseries.LombScargle (periodicity testing, detect/scoring.py) and as a lightkurve/astroquery dependency throughout.
  • Astroquery — used for MAST queries (light-curve search/download) and for the target-list catalogue cross-matching in scripts/build_target_list.py (VizieR, TIC).

docs.title: 37.3 Data sources (not literature citations, but named archives the project depends on)
docs.text: Per the README's "Data sources" section: MAST (Kepler/TESS photometry), the NASA Exoplanet Archive, VizieR, SIMBAD, and the Gaia archive (target and cross-match data). All are stated as public, requiring no credentials. SIMBAD and Gaia are named as data sources the project intends to use for vetting (Next Steps.md PART D2, vetting/catalogs.py — not yet built, vetting/ is an empty directory per 28_limitations.md); as of this commit they are referenced in planning documents and the README but not yet queried by any implemented code path.

docs.title: 37.4 What is NOT cited anywhere in this codebase
docs.text: To avoid inventing references: no paper on machine-learning classifier methodology, no Isolation Forest citation (relevant to the planned H4 detector, 30_future_detectors.md), and no citation for the physical exocomet-simulator concept (F2/PART I) were found anywhere in the source, README, or research logs read for this document. If such citations are added when that work is built, they belong here as an update, not anticipated now.

docs.title: 38. Mathematics
docs.text: Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051. Every formula below is transcribed directly from the implementation (detect/baseline.py, detect/candidates.py, detect/asymmetry.py, detect/model_comparison.py, detect/scoring.py) — not a textbook-generic version of the same idea. Where the implementation departs from the "obvious" formula (e.g. truncated rather than padded windows), that departure is documented, because it was a deliberate, tested choice.

docs.title: 38.1 Median absolute deviation (MAD) → robust sigma, detect/baseline.py
docs.text:
Local baseline is a centered rolling median (rolling_median, backed by pandas.Series.rolling(window, center=True, min_periods=1).median()), not a mean — a median is insensitive to the minority of strongly deviant points that make up an in-transit dip.

Robust per-cadence noise (local_noise) is computed as:

$$\text{MAD}i = \text{median}\big(|{\text{flux} - \text{baseline}}|\big){\text{window centered on } i}$$

$$\sigma_i = 1.4826 \times \text{MAD}_i$$

The constant MAD_TO_SIGMA = 1.4826 is the standard factor converting a MAD into a Gaussian-equivalent standard deviation, exactly as coded (no variant scaling). A floor is applied: floor = max(global_sigma * 1e-3, np.finfo(np.float64).tiny), where global_sigma = 1.4826 * median(|flux - baseline|) computed once over the whole series — this prevents a zero denominator on perfectly flat synthetic or masked stretches.

Windows are truncated, not padded, at series edges (rolling(min_periods=1) — any available points, not a padded value). The module docstring states why this specific choice was tested and kept: padding with a repeated edge value "inflated the apparent significance of pure noise at the array edges to 30-70 sigma — far above a genuine injected dip." This is a real, tested finding recorded in the source itself, not a design assumption.

docs.title: 38.2 Physical-time-to-cadence conversion, detect/baseline.py
docs.text:
Every window in config/thresholds.yaml is specified in days, converted to a cadence count at runtime:

$$n_{\text{cadences}} = \max!\left(\text{round}!\left(\frac{\text{days}}{\text{cadence_days}}\right),\ 1\right)$$

then coerced to odd and clamped to the series length by odd_window. This exists specifically because Kepler's cadence (29.4 min) and TESS's (20 s–1800 s depending on product) differ by more than two orders of magnitude — see Next Steps.md item A1.

docs.title: 38.3 Depth significance and candidate identification, detect/candidates.py
docs.text:
Per-cadence dimming significance:

$$s_i = \frac{\text{baseline}_i - \text{flux}_i}{\sigma_i}$$

positive for a dimming, negative for a brightening (depth_significance). A cadence is "in-dip" when $s_i > \texttt{sigma_threshold}$ (default 4.0, config/thresholds.yaml). Runs of at least min_consecutive (default 3) such cadences are kept; runs separated by at most max_gap_cadences (default 2) are merged. Each surviving run is then expanded outward, cadence by cadence, while $s_i$ remains above recovery_sigma (default 1.0) and the total window stays within max_window_days (default 3.0 days) — a direct, unbounded-in-code but config-bounded, linear-time loop (_expand_window).

docs.title: 38.4 Sub-cadence minimum location, detect/asymmetry.py::locate_minimum
docs.text:
A parabola is fit through the deepest cadence and its two neighbors ($f_{-1}, f_0, f_{+1}$ at times $t_{-1}, t_0, t_{+1}$). With $D = f_{-1} - 2f_0 + f_{+1}$:

$$\delta = \frac{0.5\,(f_{-1} - f_{+1})}{D}, \qquad t_{\min} = t_0 + \delta \cdot \tfrac{1}{2}(t_{+1} - t_{-1}), \qquad f_{\min} = f_0 - 0.25\,(f_{-1} - f_{+1})\,\delta$$

used only when $D > 0$ (a genuine local minimum, i.e. concave-up) and $-1 < \delta < 1$ (vertex falls inside the central cadence); otherwise the discrete minimum is returned unchanged. This is the standard three-point parabolic-vertex interpolation, applied to give the reported $t_{\min}$ sub-cadence precision.

docs.title: 38.5 Duration and slope asymmetry, detect/asymmetry.py::compute_asymmetry
docs.text:
Each side's half-depth crossing is found by walking outward from the minimum until flux recovers to half_level = baseline_level - half_depth_fraction * depth (default half_depth_fraction = 0.5), then linearly interpolating between the bracketing cadences. Each side's slope is an ordinary-least-squares fit of flux against time over the cadences between that crossing and the minimum (ols_slope, standard closed-form OLS with slope_err from residual variance, inf if fewer than 3 points or no spread in $x$).

With dur_ingress, dur_egress the two side durations (crossing → minimum) and slope_ingress, slope_egress their OLS gradients:

$$A_{dur} = \frac{\text{dur}{egress} - \text{dur}{ingress}}{\text{dur}{egress} + \text{dur}{ingress}}, \qquad A_{slope} = \frac{|\text{slope}{ingress}| - |\text{slope}{egress}|}{|\text{slope}{ingress}| + |\text{slope}{egress}|}$$

Both lie in $[-1, 1]$ and are positive for a fast-fade, slow-recovery (comet-like) event by construction — $A_{slope}$ deliberately places the ingress term first so that "the two metrics agree in sign" is a direct statement about physical consistency (AsymmetryResult.signs_agree: sign(a_dur) == sign(a_slope) and a_dur != 0).

Known limitation of this contour-based pair, documented in research log 003: at the half-depth contour specifically, a Gaussian ingress of width $\sigma$ reaches it at $1.177\sigma$ and an exponential egress of timescale $\tau$ reaches it at $0.693\tau$. Setting these equal gives the sign-flip point:

$$\frac{\tau}{\sigma}\Big|_{\text{sign flip}} = \frac{1.177}{0.693} \approx 1.70$$

So a transit with $1 < \tau/\sigma < 1.70$ has an unambiguously longer tail yet yields a negative $A_{dur}$ — the half-depth contour samples the nearly-symmetric core, not the extended wing where the comet signature actually lives. This is why $\tau/\sigma$ (from the parametric fit, §38.6) rather than $A_{dur}$ is the primary shape statistic; $A_{dur}$/$A_{slope}$ remain reported, interpretable, model-independent cross-checks.

docs.title: 38.6 Parametric profiles and BIC model comparison, detect/model_comparison.py
docs.text:
Symmetric (null) model — Gaussian dip:

$$f(t) = b - d \cdot \exp!\left(-\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{t - t_0}{w}\right)^2\right)$$

with $b$ = baseline, $d$ = depth, $w$ = Gaussian width (floored at _MIN_WIDTH_DAYS = 1e-4 days to prevent collapse onto a single cadence).

Comet model — Gaussian ingress joined continuously to an exponential egress at $t_0$:

$$f(t) = \begin{cases} b - d \cdot \exp!\left(-\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{t - t_0}{\sigma}\right)^2\right) & t \le t_0 \[4pt] b - d \cdot \exp!\left(-\dfrac{t - t_0}{\tau}\right) & t > t_0 \end{cases}$$

Both halves reach $b - d$ continuously at $t_0$ by construction; $\sigma$ = ingress Gaussian width, $\tau$ = egress e-folding timescale.

Fitting: bounded nonlinear least squares (scipy.optimize.least_squares, method="trf", max_nfev=2000) minimizing $\sum_i \left(\frac{f(t_i) - y_i}{\sigma_{y,i}}\right)^2$ over the event window widened by padding_factor (default 1.5×) so the recovering tail is not truncated. Requires at least 8 cadences in the padded window (else returns None — "too few cadences to constrain five free parameters").

BIC (ModelFit.bic, exact code):

$$\text{BIC} = \chi^2 + k \ln(n)$$

where $\chi^2 = \sum_i \left(\frac{\text{model}(t_i) - y_i}{\sigma_{y,i}}\right)^2$ (the least-squares objective's sum of squared, error-weighted residuals — i.e. this is $\chi^2$ in the weighted-residuals sense, not a raw sum of squared flux differences), $k$ = number of free parameters (4 for symmetric, 5 for comet), and $n$ = number of cadences fitted. Returns $+\infty$ if the fit did not converge or $n \le 0$.

ΔBIC (ModelComparison.delta_bic):

$$\Delta\text{BIC} = \text{BIC}{\text{symmetric}} - \text{BIC}{\text{comet}}$$

Positive favors the comet model; the comet profile's extra free parameter is charged the $k \ln n$ penalty so it must earn its added flexibility. favors_comet is true when $\Delta\text{BIC} > \texttt{delta_bic_threshold}$ (default 10.0 — the conventional "strong evidence" cutoff, cited to Kass & Raftery 1995 in research log 007).

τ/σ (ModelComparison.tau_over_sigma):

$$\frac{\tau}{\sigma} = \frac{\text{egress_tau}}{\text{ingress_width}}$$

read directly from the converged comet-model fit parameters; nan if either is non-finite or $\sigma \le 0$. Values above 1 indicate a trailing tail. This is the primary shape statistic precisely because it is derived from the whole fitted profile rather than a single contour level (see §38.5's sign-flip discussion).

docs.title: 38.7 The flagging rule, detect/scoring.py::score_event
docs.text:
$$\text{flagged} = \big(\Delta\text{BIC} \text{ finite}\big) \wedge \big(\tau/\sigma \text{ finite}\big) \wedge \big(\Delta\text{BIC} > \texttt{delta_bic_threshold}\big) \wedge \big(\tau/\sigma > \texttt{tau_over_sigma_threshold}\big)$$

with defaults delta_bic_threshold = 10.0 and tau_over_sigma_threshold = 1.0 (config/thresholds.yaml). Both conditions are required — research log 007 demonstrates concretely (with a mirror-image synthetic pair, $\Delta\text{BIC} = 201$ for the physically-backwards event versus $151$ for the real comet, while $\tau/\sigma = 0.23$ versus $4.15$) that $\Delta\text{BIC}$ alone cannot distinguish tail direction; only $\tau/\sigma$ does.

docs.title: 38.8 Bootstrap uncertainty estimation, detect/scoring.py::bootstrap_a_dur_sigma
docs.text:
For draws iterations (default 1000 in production, 300 in generate_training_labels.py for throughput, 60 in the fast test config): add Gaussian noise scaled by each cadence's own error bar to the flux inside and immediately around the event window,

$$\text{flux}'i = \text{flux}_i + \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma{\text{err},i}), \quad i \in [\text{start}-1, \text{end}+1]$$

then re-run the full ingress/egress measurement (measure_event) and record the resulting $A_{dur}$ if measurable. The bootstrap standard deviation, np.std(samples, ddof=1) (sample standard deviation, Bessel-corrected), is a_dur_sigma. Significance is then:

$$\text{significance} = \frac{|A_{dur}|}{\sigma_{A_{dur}}}$$

with the special cases: nan sigma → significance 0; sigma $\le 0$ (noiseless synthetic data) → significance $\infty$ if $A_{dur} \ne 0$ else 0. This significance value is reported but, per the current flagging rule (§38.7), does not gate the flagging decision — it is retained as an output column and a classifier feature (FEATURE_NAMES includes significance and a_dur_sigma).

docs.title: 38.9 Periodicity test, detect/scoring.py::periodicity_flag
docs.text: astropy.timeseries.LombScargle(time, flux, flux_err).autopower() over the frequency range corresponding to periodicity_min_period_days–periodicity_max_period_days (0.5–50 days, config/thresholds.yaml). The peak power's false-alarm probability (model.false_alarm_probability) is compared against periodicity_fap_threshold (default 0.01); below this, the light curve is flagged periodic. This is standard Lomb-Scargle periodogram analysis via Astropy's own implementation — no custom periodogram math is implemented in this codebase. Used only as a ranking penalty, never a hard rejection.

docs.title: 39. Data Dictionary
docs.text: Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051. Every field name and type below is transcribed directly from the dataclass definitions in src/exocomet/core/types.py. All are @dataclass(frozen=True) (immutable) unless noted.

docs.title: 39.1 LightCurveData
docs.text:
Field Type Meaning target_id str Catalogue identifier, e.g. "KIC 3542116" mission str "Kepler", "TESS", or "SYNTHETIC" time FloatArray (NDArray[np.float64]) Observation times in days (BKJD for Kepler, BTJD for TESS); validated strictly increasing in __post_init__ flux FloatArray Normalized flux, out-of-transit ≈ 1.0 flux_err FloatArray Per-cadence flux uncertainty, same units as flux meta dict[str, Any] (default {}) Free-form provenance: author, exptime, sectors/quarters stitched, synthetic/noise_sigma for test fixtures

Computed properties: n_points (int(time.size)), cadence_days (median of np.diff(time)), baseline_days (time[-1] - time[0]). with_flux(flux, **meta) returns a copy with new flux and merged metadata — the standard way injection functions produce a modified light curve without mutating the original. __post_init__ raises ValueError on length mismatch, zero length, or non-strictly-increasing time.

docs.title: 39.2 EventWindow
docs.text:
Field Type Meaning start_index int Inclusive start cadence index end_index int Inclusive end cadence index start_time float Time (days) at start_index end_time float Time (days) at end_index

Properties: duration_days (end_time - start_time), n_points (end_index - start_index + 1).

docs.title: 39.3 SideFit
docs.text: Field Type Meaning duration_days float Half-depth crossing to minimum slope float OLS gradient over that interval (negative on ingress, positive on egress) slope_err float Standard error of the slope; inf if underdetermined n_points int Cadences used in the slope fit half_depth_time float Interpolated crossing time

docs.title: 39.4 AsymmetryResult
docs.text:
Field Type Meaning a_dur float Duration asymmetry, $[-1,1]$, positive = comet-like (see 38_mathematics.md §38.5) a_slope float Slope asymmetry, $[-1,1]$, positive = comet-like ingress SideFit Ingress-side measurement egress SideFit Egress-side measurement

Property: signs_agree (bool) — sign(a_dur) == sign(a_slope) and a_dur != 0.0.

docs.title: 39.5 DipEvent
docs.text:
Field Type Meaning target_id str Host star identifier t_min float Sub-cadence-interpolated time of minimum flux (days) f_min float Flux at the minimum depth float baseline_level - f_min, fractional (not ppm) window EventWindow Detection window asymmetry AsymmetryResult \| None (default None) None if either side was unmeasurable unmeasurable_reason str \| None (default None) Human-readable reason when asymmetry is None

Properties: depth_ppm (depth * 1e6), is_measurable (asymmetry is not None).

docs.title: 39.6 ModelFit
docs.text:
Field Type Meaning name str "symmetric" or "comet" params dict[str, float] Fitted parameter values, keyed by name (t0, depth, width, baseline for symmetric; t0, depth, ingress_width, egress_tau, baseline for comet) chi2 float Weighted sum-of-squares residual n_params int 4 (symmetric) or 5 (comet) n_points int Cadences fitted converged bool Whether least_squares reported success

Property: bic (see 38_mathematics.md §38.6; inf if not converged or n_points <= 0).

docs.title: 39.7 ModelComparison
docs.text:
Field Type Meaning symmetric ModelFit Null-model fit comet ModelFit Comet-model fit delta_bic_threshold float (default 10.0) Evidence threshold, carried on the record so ranking and flagging share one config value

Properties: delta_bic (symmetric.bic - comet.bic, -inf if non-finite), favors_comet (delta_bic > delta_bic_threshold), tau_over_sigma (comet.params["egress_tau"] / comet.params["ingress_width"], nan if either non-finite or width $\le 0$).

docs.title: 39.8 EventScore
docs.text:
Field Type Meaning a_dur_sigma float Bootstrap standard deviation of a_dur significance float \|a_dur\| / a_dur_sigma (reported, not decisive — see 38_mathematics.md §38.8) signs_agree bool Copied from the event's AsymmetryResult, or False if unmeasurable flagged bool The pipeline's flagging decision (ΔBIC + τ/σ conjunction) periodic bool (default False) Lomb-Scargle periodicity flag for the parent light curve period_days float \| None (default None) Strongest periodogram peak's period model ModelComparison \| None (default None) The underlying profile-fit comparison

Properties: delta_bic (model.delta_bic or nan), tau_over_sigma (model.tau_over_sigma or nan).

docs.title: 39.9 VettingStatus (enum, str, Enum)
docs.text:
Values: CANDIDATE = "candidate", ECLIPSING_BINARY = "eclipsing_binary", FLARE = "flare", ARTIFACT = "artifact", KNOWN_VARIABLE = "known_variable", UNRESOLVED = "unresolved".

Note: this enum is defined in core/types.py and is consumed by VettingResult/CandidateRecord, but the vetting logic that would actually produce a non-default VettingStatus (src/exocomet/vetting/) is an empty directory as of this commit (see 28_limitations.md §28.4) — the type exists ahead of its implementation.

docs.title: 39.10 VettingResult
docs.text:
Field Type Meaning status VettingStatus Outcome reasons tuple[str, ...] (default ()) Every reason contributing to the status, including "why NOT a comet" catalog_matches dict[str, str] (default {}) Matched catalogue entries, e.g. SIMBAD object type

Property: is_candidate (status is VettingStatus.CANDIDATE).

docs.title: 39.11 CandidateRecord
docs.text:
Field Type Meaning event DipEvent The detected event score EventScore Its statistical assessment vetting VettingResult \| None (default None) Mundane-explanation check outcome, if run

Method to_row() -> dict[str, Any] flattens to: target_id, t_min, depth_ppm, duration_days, a_dur, a_slope, ingress_duration_days, egress_duration_days, a_dur_sigma, significance, delta_bic, tau_over_sigma, signs_agree, flagged, periodic, period_days, vetting_status, vetting_reasons (semicolon-joined). This is the one row per event written by exocomet run --out (JSON Lines) and consumed by every downstream analysis and plotting function that operates on batches of results.

docs.title: 39.12 Classifier feature row — calibration/features.py::FEATURE_NAMES (19 features, order-fixed)
docs.text:
Not a dataclass, but an equally load-bearing schema — a fixed-order tuple whose positions a trained model's coefficients are keyed against (reordering silently corrupts predictions per the source comment):

depth_ppm, log_depth_ppm, duration_days, depth_snr, a_dur, a_slope, abs_a_dur, signs_agree, tau_over_sigma, log_tau_over_sigma, delta_bic, significance, a_dur_sigma, ingress_duration_days, egress_duration_days, ingress_slope_snr, egress_slope_snr, n_points_in_window, periodic.

A generated training row (generate_training_labels.py) additionally carries label, host_star, injected_depth, injected_tau_over_sigma, seed, author, exptime — not part of FEATURE_NAMES itself, but written alongside it in every output parquet row.

docs.title: 40. Glossary
docs.text:
Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051. Definitions below match how this codebase uses each term specifically — cross-referenced against core/types.py, detect/*.py, config/thresholds.yaml, and the research logs. Where a term has a generic astronomical meaning that differs subtly from this project's usage, the project's usage is what's given.

τ (tau) — egress_tau. The e-folding timescale of the fitted exponential egress in the comet profile (detect/model_comparison.py::comet_profile), in days. Large τ relative to σ means the obscuration clears slowly — the quantitative signature of a trailing dust tail.

σ (sigma) — two distinct uses, both real, do not conflate them: 1. ingress_width — the Gaussian standard deviation of the comet/symmetric profile's ingress side, in days (a fit parameter, ModelFit.params["ingress_width"] or ["width"]). 2. The robust per-cadence noise estimate from detect/baseline.py::local_noise (MAD × 1.4826), used in depth_significance to decide whether a cadence is "in dip."

τ/σ (tau over sigma) — ModelComparison.tau_over_sigma. egress_tau / ingress_width. The primary shape statistic (see 38_mathematics.md §38.6). Values above 1 indicate a trailing tail. The sign-flip point for the older half-depth-contour asymmetry statistic is τ/σ ≈ 1.70 (research log 003) — a specific, derived number, not a round threshold chosen for convenience.

ΔBIC (delta BIC) — ModelComparison.delta_bic. BIC(symmetric) - BIC(comet). Positive favors the comet-shaped profile over the symmetric (planet/EB/noise) null model. Threshold delta_bic_threshold = 10.0 by convention (Kass & Raftery 1995's "strong evidence" cutoff). Known limitation, per research log 007: ΔBIC measures "is this asymmetric," not "is this asymmetric in the comet direction" — it cannot by itself distinguish a real trailing-tail comet from its exact time-reversed mirror image.

BKJD. Barycentric Kepler Julian Date — Kepler's native time system, BJD − 2454833, in days. config/validation_targets.yaml's published epochs are quoted in BKJD directly from Rappaport et al. (2018).

BTJD. Barycentric TESS Julian Date, the TESS-mission analogue of BKJD (BJD − 2457000). LightCurveData.time for a TESS light curve is in this system.

SPOC. Science Processing Operations Center — the TESS data-reduction pipeline this project deliberately pins to (io/download.py, author="SPOC", exptime=120 by default for TESS), to the exclusion of other TESS pipelines (QLP, TASOC, TESS-SPOC, TGLC, and TARS) that were found to produce mixed-cadence or already-residual (non-raw-flux) products that would otherwise silently corrupt stitching (Next Steps A2).

Cadence. The sampling interval between consecutive light-curve points, in days. Not a fixed constant in this codebase — LightCurveData.cadence_days is the measured median of np.diff(time) for the specific light curve in hand, because Kepler (29.4 min long cadence) and TESS (20 s to 1800 s depending on product) differ by more than two orders of magnitude. Every window in config/thresholds.yaml is specified in days, not a cadence count, and converted at runtime via detect/baseline.py::days_to_cadences for exactly this reason.

ppm (parts per million). The unit flux depths are reported in throughout this project (DipEvent.depth_ppm = depth * 1e6). All plotting functions in viz/plots.py also render relative flux as (flux - 1.0) * 1e6 in ppm.

MAD (median absolute deviation). median(|x - median(x)|), computed as a rolling quantity in detect/baseline.py::local_noise over the residual flux - baseline. Scaled by the constant MAD_TO_SIGMA = 1.4826 to convert to a Gaussian-equivalent standard deviation. Chosen over a standard deviation or mean-absolute-deviation specifically for robustness to the in-transit cadences the pipeline is trying to detect — a genuine dip should not be allowed to inflate the very noise estimate used to detect it.

A_dur (AsymmetryResult.a_dur). (egress_duration - ingress_duration) / (egress_duration + ingress_duration), measured from half-depth crossings to the fitted minimum. Positive for comet-like (fast fade, slow recovery). No longer decisive in the flagging rule (research log 007) — reported and used as a classifier feature, but ΔBIC and τ/σ decide flagged.

A_slope (AsymmetryResult.a_slope). (|ingress_slope| - |egress_slope|) / (|ingress_slope| + |egress_slope|). Positive for comet-like. Ingress term placed first deliberately so agreement in sign with a_dur is a direct statement about physical consistency (AsymmetryResult.signs_agree).

Detrending. Dividing out slow instrumental/stellar trends before detection (detrend/detrend.py), via a Savitzky-Golay filter (detrend_savgol, the default, window detrend.window_days ≈ 8.19 days) or a least-squares spline (detrend_spline, comparison alternative).

Candidate (CandidateRecord). One row of pipeline output — a DipEvent paired with an EventScore and optional VettingResult. A pipeline output, never a claim about the sky. This project's standing rule (36_research_integrity.md) never calls a candidate a "confirmed" exocomet.

Flagged (EventScore.flagged). The pipeline's own decision that a detected event's shape is comet-like, per the ΔBIC + τ/σ conjunction (detect/scoring.py::score_event). Distinct from detection (Detector.detect() finding a DipEvent at all) — a detected event may or may not end up flagged.

Hold-out targets. KIC 3542116 and KIC 11084727 (plus KIC 1026032, per build_kepler_host_list.py::EXCLUDED_HOLD_OUT_TARGETS) — stars whose data must never appear in classifier training data, enforced by a hard HoldOutError exception in scripts/train_classifier.py::load_labels, because they are the ground-truth exam the classifier is later evaluated against.

Ledger (io/ledger.py). The append-only JSON-Lines record of every ingestion attempt (target_id, mission, status, timestamp_utc, attempt, error, extract_path, results_path), committed to the external exocomet-hunter-data repository by scripts/ingest.py. Designed so a crash never loses or corrupts prior entries, and latest_entries() resolves the true current state even if two runs raced on the same target.

Extract (extract/<mission>/<target>.parquet). An atomically-saved, byte-identical round-trip of a LightCurveData, produced by io/extract.py. The permanent, detector-independent artifact of ingestion — kept regardless of how the detection pipeline itself changes.

docs.title: 41. Troubleshooting
docs.text: Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051. Every incident below actually happened during development, sourced from Session Log 2026-09-15.md. These are recorded so the same root cause doesn't need rediscovering.

docs.title: 41.1 MAST fetch appears to hang for minutes with zero progress
docs.text:
What you'll see: a call into io/download.py's fetch path (directly, via exocomet run, or inside scripts/ingest.py/train_classifier.py) sits with no CPU activity for several minutes.

What it actually is: a truncated, previously-cached FITS file from an interrupted prior download — the real 2026-09-14 incident was a file sitting at exactly 65,536 bytes (a round 64 KiB block boundary), the signature of a killed mid-transfer download, silently left in the local cache. Retrying against it without clearing it first fails identically, every time, for as long as retries continue — not a true hang, just an unbounded number of guaranteed-identical failures with no time limit.

Fix, already applied: io/download.py has bounded timeout + retry with explicit astroquery.mast.conf.timeout/pagesize configuration, and _call_with_retries now accepts a cleanup callback wired to _discard_cached(cache, target_id) between attempts — a poisoned cache entry is discarded before the next attempt, not retried against unchanged. If this recurs: check the cache directory for a file at a suspiciously round byte size (a multiple of 4096 or 65536 is a strong signal), quarantine or delete it, and confirm the error message names "may be corrupt due to an interrupted download" — that specific astroquery/lightkurve error string is the diagnostic signature, not a generic timeout.

docs.title: 41.2 A ledger line says "success" but the output file doesn't exist
docs.text: Root cause, already fixed: this was the direct downstream consequence of §41.1's poisoned-cache pattern colliding with a retry loop that had no cleanup step — a run could log success from a stale code path before the underlying corrupted-cache failure was actually resolved. Fixed by the same cleanup callback above, plus an added immediate readback check in scripts/ingest.py right after save_extract(), specifically so this exact failure mode cannot recur silently from some other, future cause either. If you see it recur: check whether the readback check itself was bypassed (e.g. a code path that calls the underlying save function directly, skipping ingest.py's wrapper).

docs.title: 41.3 ingest.py (or a sibling script) creates its cache in the wrong place
docs.text:
What you'll see: a data/raw/ directory appears somewhere unexpected — e.g. under scripts/ — instead of at the repository root where every other tool expects it.

Root cause: DEFAULT_CACHE_DIR = Path("data/raw") in the download module is relative to the process's current working directory, not the repository root. Running a script from inside scripts/ (a convention several sibling scripts use) silently creates scripts/data/raw/.

Fix, already applied in ingest.py: it computes an explicit raw_cache_dir from Path(__file__).resolve(), independent of CWD, and passes it explicitly into fetch_light_curve. If you write a new script that touches the cache: do the same — never rely on fetch_light_curve's CWD-relative default from a script that might be invoked from an unpredictable working directory (e.g. CI, or a different shell session).

docs.title: 41.4 git push fails with "Device not configured" or an account-mismatch error
docs.text:
Root cause: the local machine's active gh credential is for a different GitHub account (elpis-app) than the one these two repositories (exocomet-hunter, exocomet-hunter-data) live under (AJpro-merc). A plain git push silently tries to authenticate as the wrong account.

Workaround (in active use, including by the CI workflows themselves):

GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token -u AJpro-merc)
git push https://AJpro-merc:${GH_TOKEN}@github.com/AJpro-merc/exocomet-hunter.git

Status: workaround only. A persistent local credential-config fix (so this doesn't need rediscovering each session) is explicitly listed in Next Steps.md's "FIRST THING NEXT SESSION" list as still outstanding — do not assume it has been permanently fixed just because the workaround exists.

docs.title: 41.5 GitHub Actions silently burns compute and produces nothing
docs.text:
What happened, real incident, 2026-09-14→15: train.yml failed 4 consecutive times, each run taking roughly 30–38 minutes, for a total of ~2 hours 16 minutes of real compute with zero output.

Root cause: a 2026-09-14 force-push (squashing commit history to remove stray attribution) orphaned the branch reference the scheduled trigger was checking out — the runner's installed package version string showed it was still checking out the pre-squash commit, not current main. This is a real, non-obvious failure mode of combining scheduled workflow triggers with history-rewriting pushes: the schedule kept firing against a commit that no longer existed on the branch it thought it was tracking.

Also found in the same investigation: a genuine architectural misunderstanding was corrected mid-session — the 2-hourly schedule only generates training rows (fetch → extract features → discard FITS → save), while actual model training is a separate weekly job (0 6 * * 1 in train.yml) that had never actually run; all 4 failures were generation runs, not training runs.

Fix: both survey.yml and train.yml were disabled (gh workflow disable) pending a real commit to re-anchor main past the orphaned reference. A subsequent real commit (afa4bb2) did re-anchor the branch. If a scheduled workflow starts failing immediately after a force-push or history rewrite, check this first — it is a specific, previously-confirmed cause, not a generic "something broke" symptom.

docs.title: 41.6 Quick diagnostic checklist
docs.text: Symptom Check first Fetch hangs / times out Cache directory for a truncated file at a round byte size Ledger says success, file missing Whether the save path went through ingest.py's wrapper (readback check) or bypassed it Wrong cache directory appears What CWD the script was invoked from, and whether it computes its cache path from __file__ git push fails with auth error Active gh account (gh auth status) versus the repo's actual owner Scheduled Action fails immediately after a force-push Whether the branch reference the trigger checks out still exists

docs.title: 42. Roadmap
docs.text: Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051. This is a condensed, CURRENT-STATE snapshot of Next Steps.md PARTS D through J. It is a pointer, not a replacement — Next Steps.md is the live tracker and should be read directly for full detail, next-session priorities, and anything that has changed since this document was written. Every item below is stated as PLANNED or NOT IMPLEMENTED as the source document itself states it; nothing here is upgraded or downgraded in status relative to that source.

docs.title: 42.1 PART D — Making results defensible (🟠 important, all PLANNED / NOT IMPLEMENTED)
docs.text: Item Status D1. False-positive laboratory (flare, EB, starspot, δ Scuti, momentum-dump, sector-edge-ramp lookalikes as documented negative classes with a confusion matrix) PARTIAL — flare and starspot classes exist in the classifier training generator (C1); eclipsing binary, δ Scuti, momentum dump, and sector-edge ramp classes are NOT IMPLEMENTED, and no confusion matrix of any kind exists (see 31_machine_learning.md §31.3) D2. Vetting module (src/exocomet/vetting/: catalog cross-matching, flare/periodicity/cross-target-artifact/data-gap/odd-even checks) NOT IMPLEMENTED — the directory is empty (see 28_limitations.md §28.4) D3. Blind-search protocol (tune on dev set, freeze + tag config, run once on search targets) PLANNED, NOT IMPLEMENTED as a formal followed process (see 36_research_integrity.md §36.3) D4. Ablation study (recall/FPR with each pipeline component removed) NOT IMPLEMENTED D5. Trials factor / empirical false-alarm rate NOT IMPLEMENTED (see 28_limitations.md §28.3; sharpened by J2 below)

docs.title: 42.2 PART E — Engineering (🟢 later/polish)
docs.text: Item Status E1. pipeline.py (run_target() orchestrator with per-target error isolation) NOT IMPLEMENTED as a standalone module — the equivalent sequencing exists inline in cli.py and scripts/ingest.py, not as a reusable pipeline.py E2. cli.py subcommands (run, validate, inject) IMPLEMENTED — this is the one E-item actually done; see 35_code_reference/cli.md E3. Provenance manifest (results/runs/<timestamp>.json) NOT IMPLEMENTED (see 25_reproducibility.md §25.2 for the full gap analysis) E4. Memory-bounded batch processing (2-4 workers, not cpu_count()) NOT IMPLEMENTED E5. CI (ci.yml: ruff, mypy, pytest, ubuntu+macOS, 3.11/3.12, coverage) NOT IMPLEMENTED — .github/workflows/ contains ingest.yml, train.yml, survey.yml only; no CI-style lint/type/test-on-push workflow exists E6. Catalogue-driven target list + matched control group PARTIAL — scripts/build_target_list.py genuinely queries VizieR and matches to TIC (verified real: 505 rows from catalogue J/ApJS/225/15, 5/5 matched to TIC), but the matched-control-group logic returns zero matches for all 5 disc hosts, a real unfixed gap, and it is deliberately not wired into ingest.py's target sources E7. Benchmarks (tests/benchmarks/, runtime/memory vs light-curve length) NOT IMPLEMENTED — directory confirmed empty (see 27_testing.md §27.1)

docs.title: 42.3 PART F — Science extensions (🟢 later)
docs.text: All six items (F1 cross-mission sensitivity comparison, F2 physical comet simulator, F3 independent second detector, F4 debris-disc-vs-control population comparison, F5 2-D depth×duration sensitivity map, F6 detrending-method comparison experiment) are NOT IMPLEMENTED. F2 (physical simulator) is separately named in PART I as the reviewers' single highest-priority training-data improvement; F4 is separately named as the part of the project most likely to produce a genuinely citable population-level result once a real candidate list exists.

docs.title: 42.4 PART G — Release and publication (🟢 later)
docs.text: All six items are NOT IMPLEMENTED: CITATION.cff/CONTRIBUTING.md/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md/SECURITY.md/CHANGELOG.md (G1 — confirmed absent by direct directory listing, 2026-09-16), a deployed MkDocs docs site (G2), Zenodo↔GitHub DOI integration (G3), a PyPI release workflow (G4), a JOSS-format paper (G5), and an external user successfully running the tool and filing an issue (G6).

docs.title: 42.5 PART H — Later, agreed but parked (🟢)
docs.text: Item Status H1. AI review layer (skeptic, never decides, must allow insufficient_evidence) PLANNED, NOT IMPLEMENTED — see 36_research_integrity.md §36.1 for how its underlying principle is already reflected elsewhere H2. Website / dashboard PLANNED, NOT IMPLEMENTED — explicitly deferred by the project author H3. Claude Cloud routine for the search survey itself Confirmed impossible on this platform (Cloud routines cannot reach mast.stsci.edu at all — a platform egress policy, not a config gap). The daily-survey automation stays on GitHub Actions. A reporting-only Cloud routine (reads results, never fetches from MAST) is built and viable. H4. Second detector — technosignature/anomalous-dimming (Isolation Forest, KIC 8462852) PLANNED, NOT IMPLEMENTED — see 30_future_detectors.md H5. Learning pass (plain-language walkthrough of every module) Still owed, per the project's own tracker; this specification document is a step toward it but was not scoped as a replacement for it

docs.title: 42.6 PART I — Future roadmap from external review (🟢, condensed to current-state pointers only)
docs.text: A detailed outside critique (2026-09-14) proposed a long list of longer-term direction. Its cheap, concrete risk-mitigation half was folded directly into the actual 2026-09-14 build (idempotent generation, per-cycle work caps, the written hold-out protocol, dedup/sanity checks, A2 provenance columns, a saved threshold artifact, skip-if-unchanged retraining, job isolation) and is reflected in the currently-built code described elsewhere in this specification. The bigger-picture half remains entirely unbuilt, in the reviewer's own rough priority order: a physical exocomet simulator (overlaps F2), a falsification engine (overlaps D1/D2), a full injection-recovery sensitivity map (overlaps F5), a formally frozen blind test set (overlaps D3), a detrending ensemble, a second independent detector (overlaps F3), a one-click per-candidate "case file," an AI skeptic with hard guardrails (overlaps H1), an "unknown-unknown" anomaly pass (bridges to H4), active learning, a human-in-the-loop review console, cross-mission/cross-sector confirmation, and population-level science (overlaps F4). None of these exist in code as of this commit.

docs.title: 42.7 PART J — From the 2026-09-15 external reviews (🟢, condensed)
docs.text:
Item Status J1. Pixel-level validation / TPF centroids NOT IMPLEMENTED — both reviews' top-ranked gap; see 28_limitations.md §28.4 J2. Empirical look-elsewhere correction (N candidates per 10,000 null curves) NOT IMPLEMENTED — sharpens D5; feasible given ~0.8 s/star throughput, per the project's own reasoning, but not yet run J3. Sector-overlap test (TESS, n_independent_sectors column) NOT IMPLEMENTED — described as cheap given lc.meta already carries the sector list post-A2 J4. Candidate JSON schema (one file per event, GitHub Pages explorer later) NOT IMPLEMENTED J5. Physical forward-model injector as a second injector class (alongside, not replacing, the existing parametric one) NOT IMPLEMENTED J6. β Pic as validation target #3 NOT IMPLEMENTED — noted as feasible given the SPOC-pinned loader already resolves β Pic to 10 clean products (A2 fix) J7. Bayesian candidate probability NOT IMPLEMENTED J8. Stellar-property-aware detection (radius, spectral type, age, disk/planet/binary knowledge) NOT IMPLEMENTED J9. Case-file / scientific report export (PDF+JSON+CSV) NOT IMPLEMENTED — overlaps E3 J10. Live "stars currently being analysed" activity counter NOT IMPLEMENTED — explicitly gated on the six-event exam (see 31_machine_learning.md §31.3) being green first

Rejected outright, recorded so they don't resurface: a static vanity-total dashboard, a weekly discovery digest (the reporting-only Cloud routine already covers this), and an invented 0–100 "Exocomet Priority Score" — explicitly rejected as manufacturing false precision the underlying numbers don't support, on the same principle this specification applies to the classifier's evaluation status in 31_machine_learning.md.

docs.title: 42.8 Net picture
docs.text: The project's own tracker is consistent and has not been "improved" between logging and this document: PART A (correctness-blocking fixes) is done; C1/C2 (classifier data + training) are built with C2's backtest verification status genuinely uncertain (§31.2); C3/C4 (evaluation, wiring-in) have not started; and the overwhelming majority of PARTS D through J — the work that would make this project's results genuinely defensible to an outside reviewer, per PART I's own framing — remains PLANNED or NOT IMPLEMENTED. The single item both 2026-09-15 external reviews independently converged on as the most important missing capability, pixel-level vetting (J1), is unstarted.

docs.title: 43. Scientific Claims Registry
docs.text:
Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051.

This section enumerates specific, checkable scientific claims this project currently makes (or could make), with the evidence each rests on. A claim not listed here should not be treated as backed by anything. The machine-readable mirror is docs/specification/registry/claims.yaml.

docs.title: 43.1 Backed claims
docs.text: ID Claim Type Evidence Status CLAIM-001 All six published KIC 3542116 exocomet transit events (Rappaport et al. 2018) are recovered by the detector, within 0.5 d of the published epoch. Detection recall scripts/run_validation.py, config/validation_targets.yaml, README's own recovery table (epoch errors 0.029–0.184 d) VALIDATED CLAIM-002 The flagging rule delta_bic > 10 and tau_over_sigma > 1 recovers all six KIC 3542116 dips while rejecting a synthetic time-reversed (physically backwards) mirror-image event that a ΔBIC-only rule would have flagged. Discriminative validity docs/research_log/007-delta-bic-is-direction-blind.md, src/exocomet/detect/scoring.py VALIDATED CLAIM-003 Pinning TESS light-curve retrieval to a single author/exptime (SPOC/120s) avoids both cross-cadence window mismatch and a flux-normalization corruption bug in the TARS HLSP pipeline. Engineering fix, verified against real data docs/NEXT_STEPS.md §A2, tests/unit/test_cross_cadence.py, src/exocomet/io/download.py module docstring VALIDATED (against the specific case tested — beta Pic, 54→10 products) CLAIM-004 The resumable ingestion pipeline (scripts/ingest.py) can complete a full fetch→extract→detrend→detect→save→push cycle unattended on GitHub Actions infrastructure, with zero local machine involvement. Operational Session Log 2026-09-15 §12: real files (ledger.jsonl, Kepler parquet extract, results) confirmed landed in AJpro-merc/exocomet-hunter-data via GitHub API after a live triggered run VALIDATED (one confirmed successful run; not the same as continuous unattended operation over time — see 43.2) CLAIM-005 Kepler long-cadence full-mission processing (a ~4-year light curve, ~65,000 cadences) runs in ~0.8 seconds per star. Performance README.md, Session Log 2026-09-13 (original measurement) UNVERIFIED — measured before the A1 (window-units) and A4 (flag-rule) changes; not re-run since. See 70_performance_benchmarking.md. CLAIM-006 Injecting 200 synthetic comet-shaped transits into real Kepler photometry gives a 50% detection floor near 750 ppm and full (100%) recovery above 1000 ppm. Sensitivity README.md; underlying method calibration/injection.run_injection_recovery UNVERIFIED as currently stated — Next Steps B8 explicitly flags this table as measured before the A1/A4 fixes and not yet regenerated. Treat the README's own completeness numbers as stale pending a re-run. CLAIM-007 The append-only ledger design (io/ledger.py) survives a process kill at any point without losing or duplicating a completed record. Software correctness tests/unit/test_ledger.py; direct observation in Session Log 2026-09-15 §11 of a real race (two concurrent invocations) that latest_entries() resolved correctly without a code fix VALIDATED (tested paths: mid-write truncation recovery, concurrent-writer race)

docs.title: 43.2 Claims explicitly NOT backed (open, or contradicted by evidence)
docs.text: ID Claim Why not backed Status CLAIM-101 Measured event depths are an unbiased estimate of true transit depth. docs/research_log/006-depth-offset-investigation.md: all six KIC 3542116 depths measure ~77% of published values; three hypotheses tested (baseline contamination, fitted-depth, detrending absorption) close at most ~88% of the gap, leaving 10–15% genuinely unexplained. UNVERIFIED / OPEN CLAIM-102 The comet-model (Gaussian-ingress/exponential-egress) fit converges reliably on shallow events. Same investigation surfaced one dip (D140, 491 ppm published) fit at 3.47× its published depth — a likely separate bug in detect/model_comparison.py, not yet investigated on its own (Next Steps §4 "FIRST THING NEXT SESSION" item, still open as of this commit). NOT VALIDATED CLAIM-103 The pipeline's per-event significance accounts for the number of places searched (the look-elsewhere / trials-factor problem). README's own "Honest limitations" section states this is not corrected. Next Steps D5/J2 (empirical look-elsewhere via null/time-reversed curves) is planned, not built. NOT IMPLEMENTED CLAIM-104 A flagged candidate has been checked against a background eclipsing binary bleeding into the photometric aperture (pixel-level vetting). src/exocomet/vetting/ contains only __init__.py with a docstring; no pixel-level (TPF/centroid) check exists. Both external reviews (Next Steps J1) rank this the single biggest missing capability. NOT IMPLEMENTED CLAIM-105 The ingestion pipeline runs continuously and unattended over time (not just once). Confirmed FALSE as stated, per real live data: the sibling 23_automation.md section's direct gh run list query (2026-09-16) shows ingest is the only active workflow, with two successful runs on 2026-09-15 (17:50 workflow_dispatch, 21:07 schedule, 11m29s) followed by two consecutive failures on 2026-09-16 (00:05 and 05:50 UTC, ~1 min each) — a regression caused by five hardcoded bad Kepler IDs (59_error_taxonomy.md ERR-006) whose fix exists only in the local working tree and has not yet been committed/pushed. CLAIM-106 KIC 1161345 is a "quiet" star suitable as an injection host. It produced 43 flagged candidate events out of ~260 detected across two independent real fetches (Session Log 2026-09-15 §11/§12) — a rate the same session explicitly compares to KIC 1026032, which turned out to be a real eclipsing binary. Not yet run through scripts/vet_host_list.py for a direct-inspection verdict. Explicitly and permanently false per this document's own vocabulary rule (§0.4 of 00_document_control.md): a flagged event is a candidate or candidate consistent with an exocomet interpretation, never "confirmed." No claim in this registry uses "confirmed," and none should. N/A (standing rule, not a pending claim)

docs.title: 43.3 How to use this registry
docs.text: A claim being VALIDATED here means the cited evidence file/script was read and the specific number or behavior checked against it directly (2026-09-16) or an earlier session log entry with enough detail to trace. It does not mean independently re-run by an outside party, and it does not mean the underlying result is free of the biases described in 53_threats_to_validity.md. Any new claim added to the codebase or README should get a corresponding row here before being repeated elsewhere in this specification.

docs.title: 44. Requirements Specification
docs.text:
Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051.

Requirements below are things the system actually has to do today, each traced to a real implementation (and test, where one exists) rather than aspirational. IDs are stable identifiers for cross-reference from other sections. The machine-readable mirror is docs/specification/registry/requirements.yaml.

docs.text: No requirement exists yet for: pixel-level vetting (blocked on an empty vetting/ package), a formal statistical trials-factor correction, human-in-the-loop review/audit trail, or reproducibility packaging. These are PLANNED, tracked in docs/NEXT_STEPS.md, and covered as NOT IMPLEMENTED in the relevant sections below (45, 61, 64, 69) rather than given a REQ- ID here, since writing a requirement ID for something with zero implementation to trace would misrepresent this registry's purpose.

docs.title: 45. Decision Specification
docs.text:
Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051.

This section documents the real, code-level decision points in the pipeline: where a binary or categorical outcome is produced from continuous measurements, what the exact rule is, and what governance exists (or does not) around changing that rule.

docs.title: 45.1 The flagging decision (A4 rule)
docs.text:
Location: score_event(), src/exocomet/detect/scoring.py, lines ~160–165.

flagged = bool(
    np.isfinite(delta_bic)
    and np.isfinite(tau_over_sigma)
    and delta_bic > cfg.delta_bic_threshold
    and tau_over_sigma > cfg.tau_over_sigma_threshold
)

Both thresholds are config-driven (ScoringConfig.delta_bic_threshold = 10.0, ScoringConfig.tau_over_sigma_threshold = 1.0, mirrored in config/thresholds.yaml), not hardcoded in this function. An event with a non-finite ΔBIC or τ/σ (an unfittable or degenerate profile) fails closed — it is never flagged by default.

Why two conditions, not one. ΔBIC alone answers "is this profile asymmetric at all," and a controlled experiment (docs/research_log/007-delta-bic-is-direction-blind.md) found it scores a synthetic physically backwards (leading-tail) mirror-image event higher (201) than the real trailing-tail comet shape (151) — ΔBIC carries no direction information. Only τ/σ separates the two (4.15 vs 0.23). Dropping the τ/σ condition would silently readmit every backwards event as a candidate while leaving the six known validation dips still passing (they are genuine trailing-tail events either way) — a failure mode that would not be caught by the validation gate alone. This is stated as a standing warning in the research log itself.

Contour asymmetry (A_dur, significance, signs_agree) is computed and reported but does not decide. It was the pre-A4 decision rule (abs(a_dur)/sigma >= 3.0) and was replaced because it is sign-blind by construction (abs()) and, per docs/research_log/003-half-depth-contour-sign-error.md, the underlying A_dur statistic itself can carry the wrong sign at the half-depth contour for this profile family (sign flip at τ/σ ≈ 1.70). It remains a reported column and a classifier feature (FEATURE_NAMES in calibration/features.py), never a gate.

Status: IMPLEMENTED, TESTED (tests/unit/test_scoring.py), VALIDATED against the adversarial mirror-image case.

docs.title: 45.2 The periodicity flag
docs.text:
Location: periodicity_flag(), src/exocomet/detect/scoring.py.

A Lomb-Scargle periodogram is run over the whole light curve; a peak with false-alarm probability below ScoringConfig.periodicity_fap_threshold (0.01) in the period range [periodicity_min_period_days, periodicity_max_period_days] (0.5–50 days) sets EventScore.periodic = True. This is explicitly a ranking penalty, not a hard rejection — the docstring states a strong period is "not proof that an event is an eclipsing binary, but a reason to rank a candidate lower." It does not participate in the flagged boolean.

Status: IMPLEMENTED. No dedicated test file for this function was found (see tests/unit/test_scoring.py for what is covered); TESTED status is UNVERIFIED beyond whatever incidental coverage that file provides.

docs.title: 45.3 Candidate window formation (detect step)
docs.text:
Location: src/exocomet/detect/candidates.py (not read in full; parameters confirmed via config/thresholds.yaml and core/config.py).

A cadence enters a candidate window when it sits sigma_threshold (4.0) robust-sigma below the rolling-median baseline, requires min_consecutive (3) consecutive in-dip cadences (rejecting single-cadence cosmic-ray hits), merges runs separated by at most max_gap_cadences (2), caps window duration at max_window_days (3.0), extends edges until flux recovers to within recovery_sigma (1.0) of baseline, and discards any event within edge_margin_days (~1.02 d) of either end of the series. Every one of these is a decision point with a config-driven threshold and no adaptive/learned component.

Status: IMPLEMENTED. Not independently re-verified against source beyond the config file's own inline documentation (see 46_parameter_provenance.md).

docs.title: 45.4 The hold-out / bad-host exclusion decision
docs.text:
Location: scripts/build_kepler_host_list.py (EXCLUDED_HOLD_OUT_TARGETS, KNOWN_BAD_HOSTS), re-enforced in scripts/ingest.py::get_target_list().

A hard AssertionError — not a warning — is raised if either set intersects the assembled target list, at both the source-of-truth module and again at the point ingestion consumes it (defense in depth against a future third target source, e.g. build_target_list.py, leaking a validation star in). scripts/train_classifier.py additionally implements a HoldOutError exception specifically for the training step (Next Steps C2), raised if either hold-out target ever appears in the assembled training data.

Status: IMPLEMENTED, TESTED (tests/unit/test_ingest.py).

docs.title: 45.5 Candidate rejection criteria — vetting (NOT IMPLEMENTED)
docs.text:
There is no VettingResult-producing code today. src/exocomet/vetting/ contains only __init__.py with a one-line docstring ("Catalogue cross-matching and false-positive checks"). VettingStatus (core/types.py) defines the intended outcome vocabulary — CANDIDATE, ECLIPSING_BINARY, FLARE, ARTIFACT, KNOWN_VARIABLE, UNRESOLVED — but nothing in the codebase currently constructs a VettingResult other than None. Every CandidateRecord.vetting field in real output data (confirmed by inspecting a sample line from exocomet-hunter-data/results/Kepler/KIC_1161345.jsonl) is null.

Status: NOT IMPLEMENTED. Planned as Next Steps D2 (catalogue checks: SIMBAD object type, AAVSO VSX, EB catalogue membership, Gaia parameters, cross-target artefact detection, data-gap proximity, odd/even depth check) and J1 (pixel-level/TPF centroid check, both external reviews' top-ranked gap).

docs.title: 45.6 Human-review / audit-trail mechanism (NOT IMPLEMENTED)
docs.text:
There is no code path today where a human records a verdict on a candidate, no review console, no persisted decision distinct from the automated flagged boolean, and no mechanism preventing a candidate from being re-scored silently after a config change (see 63_change_impact_analysis.md for the concrete A4 example of exactly this happening without any audit trail). Next Steps I proposes a "human-in-the-loop review console" and an AI-skeptic review layer (H1, explicitly barred from ever deciding whether something is a comet, and required to be able to answer "insufficient_evidence"); neither exists in code.

Status: NOT IMPLEMENTED.

docs.title: 45.7 Blind-search protocol (D3) — NOT IMPLEMENTED as tooling
docs.text:
Next Steps D3 specifies: tune only on development data, freeze the configuration and tag it (e.g. v0.2-frozen), run on search targets only after freezing, and record the tag with every result. No git tag matching this pattern was found, and no code reads or records a frozen-configuration tag alongside output. This remains a written protocol, not an enforced one.

Status: PLANNED, NOT IMPLEMENTED.

docs.title: 46. Parameter Provenance
docs.text:
Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051.

Every parameter below is read directly from config/thresholds.yaml (mirrored as dataclass defaults in src/exocomet/core/config.py). Origin classification (literature-derived / empirically-calibrated / engineering-choice / temporary) is inferred from the file's own inline comments where present; anything without an explicit justification in-file is marked UNKNOWN rather than guessed at. The machine-readable mirror is docs/specification/registry/parameters.yaml.

docs.title: 46.1 detrend section
docs.text: Name Value Unit Valid range (stated) Origin Provenance note window_days 8.1871 days must be >> longest expected dip Literature-derived + engineering-choice Comment: "~8.2 days is comfortably above the ~1 day dips reported by Rappaport et al. (2018)." The specific 4th decimal (8.1871) is the exact conversion of a previous Kepler-cadence-count value (401 cadences × 29.4 min), preserved so existing validation results don't move (per core/config.py docstring) — engineering continuity, not a re-derived number. polyorder 2 — UNKNOWN (no stated range) UNKNOWN No justification comment in file. Standard Savitzky-Golay choice but not stated as such in-repo. upper_sigma_clip 5.0 robust sigma UNKNOWN Engineering-choice Comment explains purpose (clip upward-only outliers before fitting) but not why 5.0 specifically. spline_knot_spacing_days 1.5 days UNKNOWN UNKNOWN Comment states it's for "the detrending-method comparison figure" only — used for a diagnostic, not the primary path. No numeric justification given.

docs.title: 46.2 baseline section
docs.text: Name Value Unit Origin Provenance note median_window_days 2.0621 days Engineering-choice (continuity) Exact conversion of the prior median_window=101 cadences on Kepler long cadence (per core/config.py docstring), not independently re-derived for the days-based scheme. noise_window_days 2.0621 days Engineering-choice (continuity) Same value and same origin as median_window_days; the file comments describe it as "the matching window" for the robust noise estimate.

docs.title: 46.3 candidates section
docs.text: Name Value Unit Origin Provenance note sigma_threshold 4.0 robust sigma UNKNOWN No stated derivation; a conventional detection threshold but not justified numerically in-file. min_consecutive 3 cadences Engineering-choice Comment: rejects single-cadence cosmic-ray hits and one-sample glitches — a stated purpose, not a derived number. max_gap_cadences 2 cadences Engineering-choice Stated purpose (merge near-adjacent in-dip runs); no numeric derivation. max_window_days 3.0 days Engineering-choice Stated purpose (bound event duration against runaway instrumental excursions); no derivation. recovery_sigma 1.0 robust sigma UNKNOWN No stated derivation. edge_margin_days 1.0208 days Engineering-choice (continuity) Exact conversion of the prior edge_margin_cadences=50 on Kepler long cadence. Comment also cites sector/quarter boundaries as "a known artefact source" as the underlying physical reason for having a margin at all, though not for the specific value.

docs.title: 46.4 asymmetry section
docs.text: Name Value Unit Origin Provenance note half_depth_fraction 0.5 fraction of depth Convention Comment: "0.5 = half-depth crossing, i.e. a FWHM-style half duration per side" — a named standard convention, not empirically tuned. min_points_per_side 3 cadences Engineering-choice Stated purpose (below this, a side is marked unmeasurable rather than scored on noise); no numeric derivation given. search_padding_factor (in core/config.py only, not present in thresholds.yaml) 2.0 multiple of window duration UNKNOWN Docstring in core/config.py explains purpose (the window marks statistical significance; wings extend further) but not why 2.0×. Note: this field's absence from config/thresholds.yaml means a YAML override cannot currently change it — see 72_code_doc_crosscheck.md.

docs.text: Name Value Unit Origin Provenance note bootstrap_draws 1000 draws Engineering-choice Standard bootstrap resolution; no specific derivation stated. significance_threshold 3.0 sigma Engineering-choice (historical) This was the pre-A4 decision threshold (abs(a_dur)/sigma >= 3.0); it is retained in config and still computed/reported (EventScore.significance) but no longer gates the flagged decision — see 45_decision_specification.md §45.1. require_sign_agreement true boolean Convention Comment references "the sign convention" documented elsewhere (docs/methodology.md, not independently verified present/absent here); the two asymmetry metrics (a_dur, a_slope) must agree in sign for the reported signs_agree field, though this is a reported column, not part of the flagged gate as of the A4 rewrite. delta_bic_threshold 10.0 ΔBIC units Literature-derived (convention) This is the standard Kass & Raftery (1995) "strong evidence" threshold for a Bayes-factor-style comparison, cited explicitly in docs/research_log/007-delta-bic-is-direction-blind.md's references. tau_over_sigma_threshold 1.0 ratio Physical/definitional Comment: "A trailing tail (obscuration that clears more slowly than it accumulated)" is by definition τ/σ > 1; this is a physically motivated boundary, not an empirically tuned one. periodicity_min_period_days 0.5 days Engineering-choice Bounds of the Lomb-Scargle search range; no numeric derivation stated. periodicity_max_period_days 50.0 days Engineering-choice Same as above. periodicity_fap_threshold 0.01 false-alarm probability Convention A conventional 1% FAP cutoff; not derived specifically for this project.
