Notes: survey.yml is architecturally distinct from ingest.yml/train.yml — it commits results back into this repository (results/processed_ledger.json, results/monitor_candidates.jsonl), not the separate data repo, and uses scripts/monitor_new_data.py rather than scripts/ingest.py. It predates the ingestion-architecture redesign (Session Log 2026-09-15 §5/§9) and, per Next Steps A3/PART A, was disabled pending the A2/A4 fixes. Live state, confirmed via the sibling 23_automation.md section's direct gh workflow list --all query (2026-09-16): survey and train are both disabled_manually; ingest is the only active workflow — though see 51_pipeline_observability.md §51.3 for the real, currently-failing state of that active workflow's two most recent scheduled runs.

All three workflows declare permissions: {contents: write} and a concurrency group matching their own name with cancel-in-progress: false, so a second trigger of the same workflow queues rather than runs in parallel or cancels the in-flight run.

docs.title: 57. API / Interface Contracts
docs.text:
Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051.

All signatures below are transcribed directly from src/exocomet/core/interfaces.py and src/exocomet/core/types.py (line numbers refer to the files as of commit 01c2051).

docs.title: 57.1 LightCurveSource (Protocol, runtime_checkable)
docs.text:
@runtime_checkable
class LightCurveSource(Protocol):
    def fetch(self, target_id: str, mission: str) -> LightCurveData: ...

Structural typing (Protocol + @runtime_checkable) — any object with a matching fetch method satisfies this interface without explicit inheritance. Real implementation: MastLightCurveSource in src/exocomet/io/download.py.

Status: IMPLEMENTED (one real implementation exists).

docs.title: 57.2 Detrender (Protocol, runtime_checkable)
docs.text:
@runtime_checkable
class Detrender(Protocol):
    def detrend(self, lc: LightCurveData) -> LightCurveData: ...

Real implementations: SavGolDetrender, SplineDetrender in src/exocomet/detrend/detrend.py (both are thin classes wrapping the module-level detrend_savgol/detrend_spline functions, which are what the rest of the codebase — cli.py, scripts/ingest.py — actually calls directly rather than going through these wrapper classes).

Status: IMPLEMENTED (two real implementations).

docs.title: 57.3 Vetter (Protocol, runtime_checkable)
docs.text:
@runtime_checkable
class Vetter(Protocol):
    def vet(self, event: DipEvent, lc: LightCurveData) -> VettingResult: ...

Real implementations: none. src/exocomet/vetting/ has no class satisfying this protocol. Every CandidateRecord.vetting field observed in real pipeline output (§45.5, §58) is None.

Status: DEFINED, NOT IMPLEMENTED.

docs.title: 57.4 Detector (abstract base class, not a Protocol)
docs.text:
class Detector(ABC):
    name: str = "detector"

    @abstractmethod
    def detect(self, lc: LightCurveData) -> list[DipEvent]: ...

    @abstractmethod
    def score(self, event: DipEvent, lc: LightCurveData) -> EventScore: ...

    def run(self, lc: LightCurveData) -> list[CandidateRecord]:
        return [CandidateRecord(event=event, score=self.score(event, lc)) for event in self.detect(lc)]

Unlike the other three interfaces, Detector is a real abc.ABC requiring subclassing (not structural typing), with a concrete run() method provided by the base class that composes detect() and score(). The docstring is explicit about why: "answers two questions... Splitting the two keeps the expensive statistical work off the path of the cheap first pass." Real implementation: AsymmetricDipDetector in src/exocomet/detect/comet_detector.py — the only Detector subclass in the codebase as of this commit. The module docstring states the planned second implementation (an anomalous-dimming/technosignature detector, Next Steps H4) is added "by implementing Detector... no orchestration code changes" — this claim is architecturally plausible given the interface design but is UNVERIFIED since no second Detector subclass has ever actually been written to test it.

Status: IMPLEMENTED (one real subclass; the extensibility claim is a design intent, not yet exercised by a second real implementation).

docs.title: 57.5 Data model contracts (core/types.py)
docs.text:
All are frozen (@dataclass(frozen=True)) — immutable once constructed, so downstream code cannot silently mutate a shared LightCurveData or CandidateRecord.

Type Fields Notes LightCurveData target_id: str, mission: str, time: FloatArray, flux: FloatArray, flux_err: FloatArray, meta: dict[str, Any] __post_init__ raises ValueError on length mismatch, empty arrays, or non-strictly-increasing time. Properties: n_points, cadence_days (median np.diff(time)), baseline_days. with_flux() returns a new instance with merged meta. EventWindow start_index: int, end_index: int, start_time: float, end_time: float Both index bounds inclusive. Properties: duration_days, n_points. SideFit duration_days, slope, slope_err, n_points, half_depth_time One ingress or egress side's linear fit. AsymmetryResult a_dur: float, a_slope: float, ingress: SideFit, egress: SideFit signs_agree property: np.sign(a_dur) == np.sign(a_slope) and a_dur != 0.0. DipEvent target_id, t_min, f_min, depth, window: EventWindow, asymmetry: AsymmetryResult \| None, unmeasurable_reason: str \| None depth_ppm = depth * 1e6. is_measurable = asymmetry is not None. ModelFit name, params: dict[str, float], chi2, n_params, n_points, converged bic property returns inf if not converged or n_points <= 0. ModelComparison symmetric: ModelFit, comet: ModelFit, delta_bic_threshold: float = 10.0 delta_bic = symmetric.bic - comet.bic (positive favors comet); favors_comet = delta_bic > delta_bic_threshold; tau_over_sigma reads comet.params["egress_tau"] / comet.params["ingress_width"], returns nan if either is non-finite or sigma <= 0. EventScore a_dur_sigma, significance, signs_agree, flagged, periodic: bool = False, period_days: float \| None = None, model: ModelComparison \| None = None delta_bic/tau_over_sigma properties delegate to model, nan if model is None. VettingStatus str, Enum: CANDIDATE, ECLIPSING_BINARY, FLARE, ARTIFACT, KNOWN_VARIABLE, UNRESOLVED Vocabulary defined; no code constructs any value other than implicitly via None (i.e., not constructed at all) as of this commit. VettingResult status: VettingStatus, reasons: tuple[str, ...] = (), catalog_matches: dict[str, str] is_candidate property: status is VettingStatus.CANDIDATE. No instance of this type is ever constructed by pipeline code as of this commit (§45.5). CandidateRecord event: DipEvent, score: EventScore, vetting: VettingResult \| None = None to_row() flattens to a dict of 19 fields for tabular output (used by cli.py, scripts/ingest.py, scripts/build_local_db.py).

docs.title: 57.6 CLI contract (src/exocomet/cli.py)
docs.text:
Command Args Exit codes exocomet run TARGET --mission {Kepler,TESS} (default Kepler), --config PATH, --all-events, --no-detrend, --out PATH 0 success; 1 on any exception (printed as error: {exc}); 2 if no subcommand given; 130 on KeyboardInterrupt exocomet validate --targets PATH (default config/validation_targets.yaml), --config PATH 0 if all expected published dips recovered (or none expected); 1 if any missed exocomet inject --n INT (default 20), --depths FLOAT..., --ingress FLOAT (default 0.1), --egress FLOAT (default 0.5), --target STR, --mission {Kepler,TESS}, --n-points INT (default 2000), --noise FLOAT (default 1e-4), --config PATH 0 always (no failure condition defined in cmd_inject)

Transcribed directly from build_parser() and main() in cli.py; not independently re-run against the installed console-script entry point here (tests/unit/test_cli.py exists and presumably exercises this, but was not read line-by-line here).

Status: IMPLEMENTED. Exit-code behavior TESTED via tests/unit/test_cli.py (existence confirmed; full assertions UNVERIFIED here — read tests/unit/test_cli.py directly for the exact cases covered).

docs.title: 58. Data Lineage
docs.text:
Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051.

Field-level lineage is described only for fields confirmed to exist in src/exocomet/core/types.py (§57.5); this section describes the chain a value travels through, not a generic ETL diagram.

docs.title: 58.1 The real chain
docs.text:
MAST (archive)
  → FITS (lightkurve download, cached locally under data/raw/mastDownload/)
  → lightkurve LightCurveCollection.stitch() [local CPU, no network]
  → _to_light_curve_data() [io/download.py]
        - drops non-finite time/flux/flux_err cadences  → meta["n_dropped_nonfinite"]
        - sorts by time, drops duplicate timestamps      → meta["n_dropped_duplicate_timestamp"]
        - normalizes flux by median raw flux             → meta["median_raw_flux"]
        - records author/exptime/sectors_or_quarters     → meta["author"], meta["exptime"], meta["sectors_or_quarters"]
  → LightCurveData (target_id, mission, time, flux, flux_err, meta)
  → [scripts/ingest.py step 2] save_extract() → extract/<mission>/<target>.parquet  (LAYER A — permanent, detector-independent)
  → [scripts/ingest.py step 3] raw FITS deleted
  → detrend_savgol() [detrend/detrend.py]
        - clips upward outliers only                     → meta["detrend_clipped_points"]
        - divides by Savitzky-Golay trend
        - records method/window                          → meta["detrend_method"], meta["detrend_window"]
  → AsymmetricDipDetector.detect() [detect/comet_detector.py] → list[DipEvent]
        - each DipEvent carries t_min, f_min, depth, window (EventWindow),
          and (if both sides measurable) an AsymmetryResult (a_dur, a_slope, ingress/egress SideFit)
  → AsymmetricDipDetector.score() [via detect/scoring.py::score_event] → EventScore
        - model: ModelComparison (symmetric vs comet ModelFit, delta_bic, tau_over_sigma)
        - a_dur_sigma, significance (bootstrap, reported not decisive)
        - flagged (delta_bic + tau_over_sigma gate, §45.1)
        - periodic, period_days (Lomb-Scargle, ranking-only)
  → CandidateRecord(event, score, vetting=None)   ← vetting is ALWAYS None today, no Vetter implementation exists
  → CandidateRecord.to_row() → flat dict (19 fields)
  → [scripts/ingest.py step 5] results/<mission>/<target>.jsonl   (LAYER B — this pipeline version's candidate events)
  → [scripts/ingest.py step 6] ledger.jsonl append (LedgerEntry: target_id, mission, status, timestamp_utc, attempt, error, extract_path, results_path)

docs.title: 58.2 What "vetting, currently a no-op" means concretely
docs.text: Every to_row() output observed in real data (verified directly against a cloned sample of exocomet-hunter-data/results/Kepler/KIC_1161345.jsonl) has "vetting_status": null, "vetting_reasons": null. This is not a placeholder value chosen by convention — it is the literal, unavoidable result of CandidateRecord(event=event, score=self.score(event, lc)) never being constructed with a third vetting argument anywhere in the current codebase (Detector.run() in core/interfaces.py constructs every CandidateRecord this way). The lineage chain above therefore has a real, permanent no-op stage at "vetting" as of this commit; §45.5 and §57.3 cover why.

docs.title: 58.3 Field-level lineage for the two layers written to the data repository
docs.text:
Layer A — the extract (extract/<mission>/<target>.parquet). Contents: exactly the fields of LightCurveData (target_id, mission, time, flux, flux_err, meta), written via io/extract.py::save_extract() — confirmed byte-identical round-trip per Session Log 2026-09-15 §9. This layer is described in scripts/ingest.py's own docstring as "the permanent, detector-independent layer" — i.e., re-running a different or improved detector against the same extract does not require re-fetching from MAST.

Layer B — the results (results/<mission>/<target>.jsonl). Contents: one JSON line per CandidateRecord.to_row(), i.e. everything downstream of the detector. This layer is explicitly not detector-independent: scripts/ingest.py's own architecture-decision note (Session Log 2026-09-15 §9, conflict #4) states this layer "is being generated by a detector with an unresolved ~15% depth gap and an empty vetting/" and was accepted as a known limitation rather than a blocker, since Layer A remains valid and re-processable regardless of detector changes.

docs.title: 58.4 The ledger is lineage metadata, not scientific data
docs.text: ledger.jsonl entries (io/ledger.py::LedgerEntry) record which attempt produced (or failed to produce) a given extract_path/results_path, with a timestamp and attempt count, but do not record the code version, config version, or package versions used (§52.2) — so while the ledger answers "was this target processed and did it succeed," it cannot currently answer "under exactly what pipeline configuration."

docs.title: 59. Error Taxonomy
docs.text:
Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051.

Real error classes actually hit during this project's development, each with cause, detection, recovery, and known test coverage. Machine-readable mirror: docs/specification/registry/errors.yaml.

docs.title: ERR-001 — MastTimeoutError
docs.text:
• Class: exocomet.io.download.MastTimeoutError (subclasses TimeoutError).
  • Cause: A MAST network call (search_lightcurve or download_all) stalls on a socket that never returns, with no deadline. Root-caused 2026-09-15: a fetch for KIC 3542116 sat at zero CPU for nine minutes and had to be killed, twice, before bounded timeouts existed.
  • Detection: _call_with_timeout() runs the call on a daemon thread and raises MastTimeoutError if the thread is still alive after search_timeout/download_timeout seconds (60s / 300s defaults).
  • Recovery: _call_with_retries() retries up to DEFAULT_MAX_ATTEMPTS (3) times with exponential backoff (5s, 10s), optionally running a cleanup callback between attempts (see ERR-002). iter_light_curves() additionally enforces a hard per-target wall-clock budget (DEFAULT_TARGET_BUDGET, 900s) so one hung star cannot stall an entire batch.
  • Known limitation: the daemon thread itself cannot be cancelled — an abandoned thread may still be alive holding a socket after the caller stops waiting; the module docstring states this honestly ("this bounds how long the caller waits," not the underlying resource).
  • Test coverage: tests/unit/test_download_timeout.py.
  • Status: IMPLEMENTED, TESTED, VALIDATED (the fix's root cause was independently re-confirmed live: the same hang reproduced in 31 seconds instead of 9 minutes once the timeout was in place, revealing the true underlying cause — ERR-002).

docs.title: ERR-002 — Poisoned-cache retry (truncated FITS file)
docs.text:
• Class: Not a distinct exception type — surfaces as a lightkurve/astropy error containing "may be corrupt due to an interrupted download," wrapped by the ERR-001 retry machinery.
  • Cause: A download interrupted partway leaves a truncated FITS file cached on disk (observed twice: 2026-09-15, exactly 65536 bytes — a round 64 KiB block boundary, the signature of a kill mid-transfer; and again 2026-09-16 for a different star during live scripts/ingest.py testing). lightkurve/astropy finds the file already present at its cache path and does not know it is broken.
  • Detection: No proactive detection — discovered only when a subsequent read of the cached file fails with the "may be corrupt" error.
  • Recovery: Before 2026-09-15, none — a retry against the same poisoned cache failed identically every time, meaning "retry" was not actually retrying anything. Fixed by giving _call_with_retries() an optional cleanup callback, wired at the download_all call site to _discard_cached(cache, target_id) between attempts, so a retry now genuinely re-fetches rather than re-reading the same broken file.
  • Test coverage: No dedicated unit test simulating a truncated cache file was found; the fix is validated by direct observation (re-tested against the same failing target after the fix: clean success, per Session Log 2026-09-15 §11) rather than by an automated regression test.
  • Status: IMPLEMENTED, VALIDATED by direct observation; TESTED — NO (automated coverage gap).

docs.title: ERR-003 — Ledger false-success (a ledger line claiming success for a file that doesn't exist)
docs.text:
• Class: Not a distinct exception; a data-integrity bug in the caller, not the ledger module itself.
  • Cause: A first real single-target test (KIC 1161345) printed "1 succeeded" but the extract file was missing from disk afterward. Root cause traced to ERR-002 above (a live recurrence of the truncated-cache corruption for a different star), not a bug in io/ledger.py — the ledger correctly recorded what it was told, but the caller's retry logic was the actual point of failure.
  • Detection: Not reproducible by directly calling process_one_target() in isolation nor via the CLI script alone — only reproduced on a third real attempt against live MAST.
  • Recovery: Fixed at the root (ERR-002's cleanup callback). Additionally, scripts/ingest.py::process_one_target() now has a belt-and-braces immediate readback check right after save_extract(): if not ex_path.exists(): raise RuntimeError(...), explicitly so this exact failure mode "can never recur silently even if some other cause produces it later" (function docstring).
  • Test coverage: The readback check itself is straightforward source-verifiable logic (line ~268–274 of scripts/ingest.py); no test was found that specifically simulates save_extract silently failing to produce the claimed file.
  • Status: IMPLEMENTED (defensive check), VALIDATED by direct observation of the fix; TESTED — NO (no dedicated regression test for this exact scenario).

docs.title: ERR-004 — CWD-relative cache path
docs.text:
• Class: Not a distinct exception; a silent-wrong-behavior bug (no error raised at all).
  • Cause: DEFAULT_CACHE_DIR = Path("data/raw") in io/download.py is relative to the process's current working directory. Running scripts/ingest.py from inside scripts/ (matching sibling scripts' own convention) silently created scripts/data/raw/ instead of the repo-root cache the rest of the codebase assumes — flagged as a known risk earlier in the same session ("not trivially safe to change") before it actually manifested.
  • Detection: Found by direct observation during real MAST testing, not by an automated check.
  • Recovery: scripts/ingest.py::process_one_target() now computes an explicit raw_cache_dir from Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "data" / "raw", independent of the process's CWD, and passes it into fetch_light_curve() rather than relying on the library default. Note: io/download.py's own DEFAULT_CACHE_DIR module constant is itself unchanged and still CWD-relative — the fix is local to ingest.py's call site, not a change to the shared default. Any future caller of fetch_light_curve()/iter_light_curves() that does not pass an explicit cache_dir can still hit this same bug.
  • Test coverage: No test found asserting cache-directory resolution is CWD-independent.
  • Status: PARTIAL — fixed at the one call site known to have hit it (scripts/ingest.py); the underlying CWD-relative default in io/download.py remains, so this is a mitigated instance of a still-latent design issue, not a closed one. TESTED — NO.

docs.title: ERR-005 — _discard_cached silently matching nothing (a no-op disguised as success)
docs.text:
• Class: Not a distinct exception; a silent-wrong-behavior bug.
  • Cause: An earlier version of _discard_cached() matched a normalized slug of target_id against lightkurve's own pipeline-internal cache directory names — which never contain the catalog string a caller searched with (a Kepler product directory is named after Kepler's own zero-padded ID, kplr001161345_lc_..., with no "kic" anywhere; a TESS HLSP product embeds a zero-padded TIC number, unrelated to a resolved common name like "beta Pic"). The match therefore matched nothing, for any target, on either mission. discard_after_read=True had silently been a no-op since it was written — found 2026-09-14 when 166 MB of "already discarded" downloads had actually accumulated on disk.
  • Detection: Direct disk-usage inspection, not an automated check.
  • Recovery: _discard_cached() now wipes the entire mastDownload tree under the cache directory rather than attempting to match a specific target's subdirectory — correct as long as targets are processed one at a time (true of every current caller as of this commit: iter_light_curves, scripts/monitor_new_data.py, MastLightCurveSource). The function's own docstring notes a future parallel-worker batch (Next Steps E4) would need per-target cache subdirectories instead of this blunter approach.
  • Test coverage: UNVERIFIED — not confirmed whether a test asserts the cache tree is actually removed after a call.
  • Status: IMPLEMENTED, VALIDATED by direct observation (166 MB accumulation before, confirmed cleanup after).

docs.title: ERR-006 — Permanent vs. retryable failure conflation (bad KIC identifiers)
docs.text:
• Class: FileNotFoundError (raised by fetch_light_curve() when a MAST search returns zero products).
  • Cause: Five hand-curated KIC identifiers in KEPLER_HOST_STARS (never validated against a real catalog when the list was hand-curated, 2026-09-14) do not correspond to any real Kepler observation. Found live 2026-09-16: each failed identically across two separate hourly ingest.yml runs, six hours apart, with "Could not resolve ... to a sky position," each time burning the whole per-run target budget on nothing and failing the job outright, which also skipped the downstream TESS job (needs: kepler in ingest.yml).
  • Detection: Live observation of repeated identical failures across independent runs.
  • Recovery, two-part: (1) scripts/build_kepler_host_list.py removed the five bad IDs (KIC 1571512, 3735741, 3839966, 4457741, 4569375) from KEPLER_HOST_STARS outright, distinct from KNOWN_BAD_HOSTS since these simply do not exist as observed targets rather than having a real astrophysical reason to exclude. (2) scripts/ingest.py::run_ingest() now recognizes FileNotFoundError specifically as a permanent failure (is_permanent = isinstance(exc, FileNotFoundError)) and records it at attempt=max_attempts immediately — one ledger line, not max_attempts of them — so next_targets() excludes it from all future runs instead of re-selecting it forever.
  • Test coverage: UNVERIFIED whether tests/unit/test_ingest.py specifically exercises the permanent-vs-retryable distinction (it does test general failure recording, per Next Steps B6/§44.2 REQ-FUNC-004).
  • Status: PARTIAL — the fix exists only in the local working tree, NOT YET COMMITTED as of HEAD 01c2051. Direct inspection of git status/git diff confirms scripts/ingest.py's is_permanent/recorded_attempt logic and scripts/build_kepler_host_list.py's removal of the five bad KIC IDs are both uncommitted local modifications on top of 01c2051, not part of that commit. This is corroborated by real live evidence: 23_automation.md §23.2 (querying gh run list directly on 2026-09-16) shows the two most recent scheduled ingest runs (2026-09-16T00:05:07Z and 2026-09-16T05:50:28Z) both failed, in ~1 minute each — consistent with the committed (unfixed) code still hitting this exact bug in production, since those runs necessarily ran against 01c2051 as pushed, not the working-tree fix. The fix described above is real code that exists on this machine, but has not yet reached the live pipeline.

docs.title: Summary table
docs.text: ID Class Detection Recovery Test coverage ERR-001 MastTimeoutError Thread-join timeout Bounded retry + per-target budget TESTED ERR-002 Poisoned-cache retry Manual (error message match) cleanup callback before retry NOT TESTED (validated by observation) ERR-003 Ledger false-success Manual (disk vs. ledger mismatch) Immediate readback check NOT TESTED (validated by observation) ERR-004 CWD-relative cache path Manual (wrong directory observed) Explicit Path(__file__)-based resolution at one call site NOT TESTED; underlying default still latent ERR-005 _discard_cached no-op Manual (disk usage) Whole-tree wipe UNVERIFIED ERR-006 Bad KIC ID / permanent failure Manual (repeated live failures) Permanent-failure classification + list cleanup UNVERIFIED

docs.title: 60. Security and Trust
docs.text: Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051.

docs.title: 60.1 Credentials in use
docs.text:
DATA_REPO_TOKEN. A fine-grained GitHub personal access token, scoped to AJpro-merc/exocomet-hunter-data only, with Contents: Read and write permission. Stored as a GitHub Actions repository secret on AJpro-merc/exocomet-hunter (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions) — never committed to source, never present in any file in this repository. Used identically in .github/workflows/ingest.yml and .github/workflows/train.yml:

git clone "https://x-access-token:${{ secrets.DATA_REPO_TOKEN }}@github.com/${DATA_REPO}.git" data-repo

GitHub's own secret-masking redacts the token value from all workflow logs automatically; this project adds no logging of its own that could bypass that. Per Session Log 2026-09-15, adding this secret was explicitly treated as the user's own action, not something an AI assistant performs on the user's behalf ("entering credentials, even a repo secret, is outside what this assistant does").

No other credentials are handled by this project. MAST, VizieR, and the TESS Input Catalog are all queried anonymously/publicly (no API key or login required for the data accessed) — confirmed by direct reading of io/download.py and scripts/build_target_list.py, neither of which references any credential for those services. The README states this explicitly under "Data sources": "All public, no credentials required."

docs.title: 60.2 GitHub Actions permissions
docs.text:
All three workflows declare an explicit, minimal permissions: block rather than relying on the repository's default token permissions:

Workflow permissions: block ingest.yml contents: write train.yml contents: write survey.yml contents: write

contents: write is required because each workflow commits output back to a repository (either the separate data repo, via DATA_REPO_TOKEN, or — for the legacy survey.yml — this repository itself, via the default GITHUB_TOKEN). No workflow requests broader scopes (e.g. id-token, packages, pull-requests) than this. This is the full extent of the permissions review possible from static inspection of the YAML files; the actual effective permissions of the default GITHUB_TOKEN also depend on the repository's own Settings → Actions → General configuration, which is account/repo-owner-controlled state not visible from this codebase and was not independently verified from this environment.

docs.title: 60.3 Concurrency and race protection as a security-adjacent property
docs.text: Each workflow declares concurrency: {group: <name>, cancel-in-progress: false}, ensuring a second trigger of the same workflow queues rather than running concurrently against the same data repository — this is what prevents two simultaneous pushes from racing on the same git push (a real conflict class this project has already hit once, per Session Log 2026-09-15 §11's discussion of two independent local invocations racing against the same target/path — resolved correctly by the append-only ledger design rather than by this concurrency setting, but the setting is the intended first line of defense for the automated case).

docs.title: 60.4 What is explicitly out of scope / not applicable
docs.text: This project has no user-facing authentication, no web-exposed service, no database with access-control rules, and no handling of personal or sensitive data of any kind — its only "users" are the pipeline's own automated runs and its maintainer running CLI commands locally. There is no threat model document, and none is warranted at this project's current scope beyond the credential-handling practices described above.

docs.title: 60.5 A known account-identity friction (not a security bug)
docs.text: Session logs document a recurring operational friction, not a vulnerability: git push from a local machine intermittently fails with Device not configured because the local keychain's active gh account (elpis-app) differs from the account that owns the repository (AJpro-merc), requiring an explicit https://AJpro-merc:<token>@github.com/... push URL as a workaround. Next Steps item 5 lists "fix git push's account mismatch properly (a persistent local credential config, not a one-off token workaround)" as still open. This is a local development-environment configuration issue, not a repository or data-security concern, and is noted here only because it involves credential/account handling.

docs.title: 61. Reproduction Packages
docs.text: Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051.

docs.title: 61.1 Current state: NOT IMPLEMENTED
docs.text: There is no tooling in this repository that packages a single result (a candidate, a validation run, a training run) into a self-contained, independently reproducible bundle. Reproducing any specific number in this specification today requires manually reading session logs, cross-referencing commit history, and re-running scripts by hand against whatever data happens to still be reachable (real MAST archives, or the separate exocomet-hunter-data repository) — exactly the manual reconciliation process this specification itself had to go through to state the numbers it states.

docs.title: 61.2 What exists that a reproduction package could build on
docs.text:
• config/thresholds.yaml is versioned alongside the code that reads it, so the configuration half of reproducibility is available via git log / git show <commit>:config/thresholds.yaml, provided the commit is known.
  • scripts/train_classifier.py's manifest (models/manifest_<mission>.jsonl) is the one place a real, structured provenance record already exists: row count, class counts, host stars, date, package versions, training-set hash (§52.1). This is a genuine, working partial precedent for what a fuller manifest would look like.
  • io/extract.py's atomic parquet format for LightCurveData means the exact input photometry used for a given detection run is, in principle, recoverable byte-for-byte from extract/<mission>/<target>.parquet in the data repository — if that specific file is still present (nothing currently prevents it from being overwritten by a later re-fetch of the same target, since save_extract()'s atomicity guarantees write-safety, not version history).
  • Git itself provides code-version history for everything under src/, scripts/, config/; what is missing is linking a specific output artifact to a specific commit (§52.2).

docs.title: 61.3 What a real reproduction manifest would need
docs.text:
Following Next Steps E3/J9's own framing (a "case file" per candidate, PDF + JSON + CSV export), a genuine reproduction package for one result would need, at minimum:

  1. Commit — the exact git SHA of the code that produced the result (not currently recorded anywhere in pipeline output; see 52_scientific_state_versioning.md).
  2. Dataset version — which specific extract file(s) (with a content hash, not just a path) were used as input, since a path like extract/Kepler/KIC_3542116.parquet can be silently overwritten by a later re-fetch.
  3. Config — the resolved PipelineConfig (already serializable via PipelineConfig.to_dict(), but nothing currently calls this and persists the result alongside output).
  4. Environment — Python version, OS, and the exact installed versions of numpy/scipy/lightkurve/astroquery/scikit-learn etc. (the training manifest captures this for training runs only, per §52.1).
  5. Seed — RuntimeConfig.rng_seed (currently a single project-wide default, 42) plus whatever seed was actually threaded through the specific stochastic step (bootstrap draws, injection RNG) for that run.
  6. Output checksums — so a re-run's output can be compared byte-for-byte or statistically against the original, rather than only visually.

None of these six is currently written to any file by any script in this repository as a bundle. Individual pieces exist in isolation (git history for #1's raw material, the training manifest as a partial precedent for #3/#4/#5), but nothing assembles them per-result.

Status: NOT IMPLEMENTED. This section describes what would need to be built, per the explicit instruction that most of sections 43–76 are honestly short because the corresponding infrastructure does not yet exist.

docs.title: 62. Release and Versioning
docs.text: Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051.

docs.title: 62.1 Code versioning — real, partial
docs.text:
pyproject.toml uses setuptools-scm for dynamic versioning (dynamic = ["version"], [tool.setuptools_scm] fallback_version = "0.1.0.dev0") — the installed package version is derived from git tags/commit distance rather than a hardcoded string. Confirmed real: src/exocomet_hunter.egg-info/scm_version.json exists in the working tree (a setuptools-scm-generated artifact), and Session Log 2026-09-15 §5 independently confirms this mechanism is live by citing an actual resolved version string observed on a GitHub Actions runner (exocomet-hunter-0.1.0.dev1+g275706758) — which was itself diagnostic evidence in that session (it revealed the runner was checking out a stale pre-squash commit).

No git tags exist for a formal release — no v0.1.0, v1.0.0, or similar tag was found in this repository, so setuptools-scm is currently always resolving to a .devN+g<hash>-style development version, never a clean release version.

docs.title: 62.2 No formal release process
docs.text: There is no CHANGELOG.md at the repository root prior to this specification project (confirmed absent via direct ls check), no tagged release, no PyPI package published (Next Steps G4, "PyPI release workflow," is PLANNED), and no release checklist or process document anywhere in the repository.

docs.title: 62.3 No dataset versioning scheme
docs.text: The separate AJpro-merc/exocomet-hunter-data repository has no tags, no version manifest, and no scheme for saying "training run X used dataset version Y" beyond the training manifest's content hash of the specific parquet file at the time of that run (§52.1, §61.2). There is no way today to ask "what did the full dataset look like on 2026-09-14" other than checking out that commit in the data repository's own git history, if its history was preserved (it is a normal git repository, so this is possible in principle, but no tooling exists to make it convenient).

docs.title: 62.4 Specification versioning (this document)
docs.text: Per docs/specification/00_document_control.md §0.2, this is "v1.0" of the EHS-CTS specification, dated 2026-09-16, with the stated revision-history note that sections 11 onward (including this one) were being written by other contributors against the same repository state, out of scope for that section's own author. No policy exists yet for how a v1.1 would be produced, what would trigger it (a set number of commits? a major pipeline change? a fixed cadence?), or how it would relate to docs/CHANGELOG.md's planned 20-commit rollup mechanism (§ standing infrastructure, described in docs/DOCUMENTATION_WORKFLOW.md). This gap is itself worth naming: the specification project and the code-versioning project (§62.1–62.3) are currently three independent, unconnected versioning schemes with no defined relationship between them.

docs.title: 62.5 Summary
docs.text: Aspect State Code version (installed package) IMPLEMENTED (setuptools-scm, dev versions only, no tagged release) Formal release process NOT IMPLEMENTED CHANGELOG.md at repo root NOT IMPLEMENTED prior to this specification (this specification creates docs/CHANGELOG.md and docs/CHANGELOG_PENDING.md as standing infrastructure — see the Documentation Workflow section of this project) Dataset versioning (data repo) NOT IMPLEMENTED Specification versioning PARTIAL — a version number exists (v1.0) but no policy for how future versions are produced

docs.title: 63. Change Impact Analysis
docs.text: Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051.

docs.title: 63.1 Template
docs.text:
For any future code or configuration change, fill in the following before merging:

Field Description Changed component The specific file/function/config key changed. Dependent components Everything importing, calling, or reading the changed thing, transitively where relevant. Scientific effect What measured quantity, decision, or reported statistic changes, and in what direction/magnitude if known. Tests affected Which existing tests newly pass/fail/become-inverted, and which new tests were added. Results potentially invalidated Any prior output (candidate list, training data, published number) that was generated under the old behavior and may no longer be trustworthy. Specification sections affected Which sections of this document (00–76) now describe stale behavior and need a corresponding edit.

This template exists because no automated tooling produces this analysis — it is a manual checklist, deliberately, since this project has no dependency-graph or impact-analysis tool (§72_code_doc_crosscheck.md documents the same manual-process limitation for doc/code consistency specifically).

docs.title: 63.2 Worked example: the real A4 flag-rule change
docs.text:
Populated once, retroactively, against the real 2026-09-15 change, to prove the template is usable rather than aspirational.

Field Value Changed component src/exocomet/detect/scoring.py::score_event() — replaced flagged = abs(a_dur) / sigma >= 3.0 with flagged = delta_bic > cfg.delta_bic_threshold and tau_over_sigma > cfg.tau_over_sigma_threshold. Also touched: core/config.py (added delta_bic_threshold, tau_over_sigma_threshold to ScoringConfig), config/thresholds.yaml (added the same two keys), core/types.py (ModelComparison.favors_comet now reads the same threshold rather than a separately hardcoded 10.0, so the ranking metric and the flagging rule cannot drift apart). Dependent components Every caller of Detector.run() / score_event() — i.e. cli.py (cmd_run, cmd_validate), scripts/ingest.py, scripts/generate_training_labels.py, scripts/measure_depth_offset.py, scripts/run_validation.py, calibration/injection.py::run_injection_recovery() (its InjectionResult.flagged field). Any script or notebook that filtered candidate output on flagged == True inherits the new definition automatically. Scientific effect A reversed (physically backwards, leading-tail) synthetic event that the old rule flagged as a candidate is no longer flagged. ΔBIC-only ranking (the old rule's implicit behavior when abs(a_dur)/sigma happened to correlate with ΔBIC) is replaced by a two-condition rule that specifically requires direction (τ/σ > 1) in addition to magnitude of asymmetry — see docs/research_log/007-delta-bic-is-direction-blind.md for the adversarial test proving the two are not redundant (ΔBIC 201 for a reversed event vs. 151 for the real comet; only τ/σ separates them, 0.23 vs 4.15). The six published KIC 3542116 dips remain flagged under both rules (they are genuine trailing-tail events), so this change is invisible to the validation gate alone — which is exactly why the research log calls this "the same trap log 003 documented, arriving from a different direction." Tests affected tests/unit/test_scoring.py::test_reversed_asymmetry_is_flagged_with_the_opposite_sign was renamed to test_reversed_asymmetry_is_not_flagged and its assertion inverted — a test that used to assert "flagged" now asserts "not flagged" for the same synthetic input. A second test was added confirming significance is still populated for reversed events (the sign information remains available as a classifier feature even though it no longer gates the decision). Full suite: 72 tests passing after this change (up from 49 before this round of changes, per Session Log 2026-09-15 §3). Results potentially invalidated Any candidate list generated before this fix landed and filtered on flagged == True may include physically-backwards events that a corrected rule would reject. No such pre-fix candidate list is known to have been published or acted upon outside of development testing, per the session record — but this is asserted from the session log's own account, not independently re-verified against every historical artifact. Specification sections affected 16_statistics.md (flagged here as needing review since it likely describes the pre-fix detection theory / flagging rule — not independently re-verified against the fix here), 45_decision_specification.md (§45.1 — written to already reflect the post-fix state), 53_threats_to_validity.md (§53.4, construct validity — cites this exact case).

docs.title: 63.3 Why this section stops at one worked example
docs.text: Populating this template requires the kind of cross-referencing (git blame, session logs, test diffs) that was done once, carefully, for the one change with the richest documented paper trail (A4). Retroactively reconstructing an equally detailed table for every other historical change (A1, A2, the ledger fixes in §59, etc.) would either take significant additional research time or produce shallower, less-verified entries — this document deliberately avoids exactly that kind of manufactured depth. The template in §63.1 is the deliverable; §63.2 proves it is usable in practice.

docs.title: 64. Candidate Audit Trail
docs.text: Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051.

docs.title: 64.1 Vocabulary tiers (mandatory, never "confirmed")
docs.text:
Per this document's standing rule (00_document_control.md §0.4), and repeated here because this section is exactly where the temptation to shortcut it is highest:

  • Detection — Detector.detect() found a DipEvent. No claim about shape or origin.
  • Flagged — EventScore.flagged is True: the fitted profile passed the ΔBIC + τ/σ two-condition rule (§45.1). A statement about the shape being comet-like, not about the sky.
  • Candidate — a CandidateRecord, with or without flagged. A pipeline output, not a claim about the sky (00_document_control.md's own definition).
  • Candidate consistent with an exocomet interpretation — the strongest permitted characterization of a single flagged, unvetted event.
  • Never: "confirmed," "discovery," "detection of an exocomet" (as opposed to "detection of a dip event").

docs.title: 64.2 The real lifecycle, as implemented today
docs.text:
DipEvent (detect step)
  → EventScore (score step: delta_bic, tau_over_sigma, flagged, significance, periodic)
  → CandidateRecord(event, score, vetting=None)   ← vetting ALWAYS None, no Vetter exists (§45.5, §58.2)
  → CandidateRecord.to_row() → one JSONL line in results/<mission>/<target>.jsonl

There is no further lifecycle stage after this. A CandidateRecord is written once, by scripts/ingest.py, and nothing in the codebase subsequently reads it back to update its status, add a human verdict, or move it through any workflow state (new → under review → resolved, or similar). The vetting_status/vetting_reasons fields in the output row exist in the schema (CandidateRecord.to_row()) but are always null in every real output row inspected.

docs.title: 64.3 What "status lifecycle" would need, and does not have
docs.text:
• No persisted status beyond the one-time flagged boolean. There is no field, file, or database row anywhere that can hold "reviewed, rejected as eclipsing binary" or "reviewed, promoted to shortlist" for a specific candidate. config/thresholds.yaml's search.shortlist_size (20) implies a shortlisting concept ("candidates carried through to per-event diagnostic plots and manual vetting" per its own comment), but no code was found that actually constructs a shortlist from the ranked candidates — it is a config value with no consuming logic located.
  • No audit trail of who/what changed a candidate's status, or when. Since no status beyond flagged exists, there is nothing to audit.
  • No append-only or versioned record of vetting decisions, unlike the genuinely append-only io/ledger.py design used for target-processing attempts. If a Vetter implementation is eventually built (§45.5), whether its output is versioned/append-only or a mutable overwrite is an open design decision not yet made anywhere in the codebase.
  • No connection between the candidate audit trail and the change-impact process (§63). When the A4 flag rule changed, every prior candidate's flagged value became retroactively describable by a different rule, but nothing re-scored or re-labeled historical output, and nothing recorded which rule-version produced which candidate row (§52.2, provenance). A candidate row from before 2026-09-15 and one from after look identical in schema but were produced under materially different flagging logic, with no field distinguishing them.

docs.title: 64.4 Human review / verdict recording — NOT IMPLEMENTED
docs.text: Next Steps PART I's proposed "human-in-the-loop review console" (a small local UI to page through candidates — light curve, detrended view, AI review, test results — and record a verdict) does not exist in any form: no UI code, no verdict schema, no storage for a recorded human decision. This is the same gap already noted in 45_decision_specification.md §45.6 and is repeated here because it is specifically the mechanism that would give this audit trail its missing lifecycle stages.

docs.title: 64.5 Summary
docs.text: Stage Implemented?
