docs.title: 65. False-Positive Catalogue
docs.text: Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051.

docs.title: 65.1 Implemented injection lookalike classes (7)
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/calibration/injection.py (injector functions) + scripts/generate_training_labels.py (ALL_CLASSES, _inject_and_label()), confirmed by direct reading of both files. These exist specifically to generate labelled classifier training rows (Next Steps C1), not (yet) to produce a standalone confusion-matrix report against the rule-based detector (§65.3).

Class Generator Real function Parameters (as sampled by generate_training_labels.py) comet Piecewise-linear asymmetric dip, egress longer than ingress inject_comet_transit() width 1–10 h; egress = ingress × uniform(1.2, 5.0); depth drawn from a weighted grid (200–3000 ppm, weighted toward 500–2000 ppm) symmetric Same shape generator, ingress = egress inject_comet_transit() (called with equal ingress/egress) Same width/depth sampling as comet reversed Same shape generator, ingress longer than egress (physically backwards) inject_comet_transit() (called with ingress > egress) ingress = width × uniform(1.2, 5.0), egress = width flare Fast linear rise, slower exponential decay, positive flux (brightening) inject_flare() rise 0.01–0.1 d, decay 0.02–0.3 d, amplitude from the same depth grid starspot Sinusoidal whole-light-curve modulation inject_starspot_modulation() period 0.5–30 d, amplitude 100–5000 ppm (Next Steps D1 range) — matched to nearest detection to a random anchor time since there is no single injected epoch noise No injection at all — real detections on real, unmodified data N/A (injected = lc) N/A time_reversed_real A real light curve, flipped in time (lc.flux[::-1]) N/A (array reversal, not a parametric injector) N/A

LOCALISED_CLASSES = ("comet", "symmetric", "reversed", "flare"); WHOLE_CURVE_CLASSES = ("starspot",); NON_INJECTED_CLASSES = ("noise", "time_reversed_real") — exact constants from scripts/generate_training_labels.py.

Status: IMPLEMENTED. No dedicated unit test file exists for calibration/injection.py (confirmed absent from tests/unit/; Next Steps B7 lists this explicitly as a gap alongside detrend/detrend.py, calibration/features.py, io/download.py, viz/plots.py). TESTED — NO for the injector functions themselves, though they are exercised indirectly whenever scripts/generate_training_labels.py or scripts/measure_depth_offset.py run.

docs.title: 65.2 Planned-but-not-built lookalike classes (Next Steps D1)
docs.text:
Class Description (as specified) Status Eclipsing binary Periodic, symmetric primary eclipse plus a shallower secondary eclipse NOT IMPLEMENTED — no generator function exists δ Scuti pulsation Multi-period, 30 min – 6 h; explicitly relevant because A-type stars like beta Pic pulsate NOT IMPLEMENTED TESS momentum dump Short flux step/glitch roughly every 3 days NOT IMPLEMENTED Sector-edge ramp Exponential settling at the start of each TESS orbit NOT IMPLEMENTED

These four are explicitly named in Next Steps D1 as the remaining items of the originally-specified false-positive laboratory, distinct from the two (flare, starspot) that were already built 2026-09-14. No code, test, or partial scaffold for any of the four was found in this repository.

docs.title: 65.3 The confusion-matrix deliverable itself — NOT IMPLEMENTED
docs.text:
Next Steps D1's stated output is: "a confusion matrix — what fraction of each lookalike gets called a comet [by the pipeline]." This is distinct from, and has not been superseded by, the classifier training-data generation in §65.1 — that generation produces labelled rows for training a model, not a report of how the current rule-based flagged decision (§45.1) performs against each lookalike class today. No such report, script output, or research-log entry containing this specific confusion matrix was found in this repository.

Status: NOT IMPLEMENTED. This is a real, identifiable gap distinct from "the training data doesn't exist" (it does, for the 7 classes above) — what's missing is the evaluation of the current rule-based decision against that data, which would directly answer the statistical-validity question raised in 53_threats_to_validity.md §53.3.

docs.title: 65.4 Relationship to the seven-class labelled dataset already generated
docs.text: scripts/generate_training_labels.py runs on a recurring GitHub Actions schedule (train.yml, every 2 hours) and writes rows into AJpro-merc/exocomet-hunter-data/training/labels_<mission>.parquet. As of this writing, that repository's training/ directory was confirmed (by direct clone, §48 EXP-005's cloning step) to contain only a .gitkeep file — no training parquet file has actually landed there yet, despite the workflow being written and, per Next Steps §5 ("GitHub Actions was burning compute producing nothing"), having run repeatedly. This is worth flagging plainly: the seven injection classes are implemented in code, but as of this commit there is no confirmed evidence of accumulated labelled training data actually existing in the shared data repository. See 69_statistical_methodology.md and 73_project_maturity_model.md for how this affects the classifier's overall readiness.

docs.title: 66. Falsification and Alternatives
docs.text: Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051.

docs.title: 66.1 Null hypothesis
docs.text: For any single flagged event: the observed asymmetric dimming arose from noise, an instrumental artefact, or ordinary stellar variability, and the fitted asymmetric (comet-like) profile is a statistical fluctuation or a misattributed non-comet process rather than evidence of a trailing dust/gas tail. The pipeline's own two-condition flagging rule (§45.1) is the current, explicit attempt to reject this null: ΔBIC > 10 rejects "this is just noise/symmetric variability," and τ/σ > 1 rejects "this asymmetry, if real, points the wrong way to be a comet."

docs.title: 66.2 Alternative explanations this pipeline can and cannot currently rule out
docs.text: Alternative explanation Can this pipeline currently rule it out? Mechanism Pure noise fluctuation mimicking asymmetry Partially ΔBIC threshold + bootstrap-derived a_dur_sigma/significance (reported, not decisive — §45.1) Physically backwards (leading-tail) asymmetric event Yes, by design τ/σ > 1 condition, validated against the exact adversarial case (docs/research_log/007) Stellar flare (brightening, not dimming) Partially The detector operates on downward excursions; a flare's brightening would not itself trigger the sigma-threshold dip detector, but the classifier's flare injection class (§65.1) exists specifically because a flare's recovery tail, or detrending artifacts around one, could still produce a spurious asymmetric dimming signature nearby — not yet quantified (§65.3) Starspot rotation modulation Partially starspot injection class exists for classifier training; the rule-based detector has no dedicated starspot check, and periodicity (§45.2) is a ranking penalty only, not a rejection Eclipsing binary (primary/secondary eclipse) No, for a single-epoch event No eclipsing-binary check exists in vetting/ (empty, §45.5); periodicity_flag() would down-rank a repeating signal but does not identify eclipse morphology (odd/even depth check, planned Next Steps D2, NOT IMPLEMENTED) Background eclipsing binary in the same photometric aperture No No pixel-level/TPF centroid check exists (Next Steps J1, NOT IMPLEMENTED) — this pipeline cannot currently distinguish "the target star dimmed" from "something near the target star in the aperture dimmed" TESS momentum dump / sector-edge ramp (instrumental) No No dedicated check exists (§65.2, NOT IMPLEMENTED); A2's author/exptime pinning reduces cross-pipeline contamination but does not detect these specific instrumental signatures Cross-target artefact (same timestamp flagged in multiple unrelated stars) No Planned (Next Steps D2: "cross-target artefact: same absolute timestamp flagged in ≥3 unrelated stars → artefact"), NOT IMPLEMENTED Quarter/sector-boundary stitching offset Partially edge_margin_days excludes only the two ends of the whole series, not internal quarter boundaries (§47.3); this is explicitly named as the leading untested suspect for the unexplained depth-bias residual (docs/research_log/006)

docs.title: 66.3 What would falsify a specific candidate's exocomet interpretation
docs.text:
Per the vocabulary discipline in §64.1, a "candidate" is never elevated past "candidate consistent with an exocomet interpretation" by this pipeline alone. Concretely, evidence that would falsify (or at minimum substantially weaken) a specific candidate's interpretation, given what could be checked if the corresponding vetting code existed:

  • τ/σ ≤ 1 on re-fit (the event's asymmetry points the wrong way) — already implemented as a hard gate (§45.1).
  • A pixel-level centroid shift during the dip, indicating the flux dip originates from a nearby contaminating source, not the target star — NOT IMPLEMENTED (§45.5, Next Steps J1).
  • A strong, significant period matching a known or plausible eclipsing-binary period, with odd/even eclipse depth differing — periodicity is flagged (§45.2) but the odd/even check is NOT IMPLEMENTED.
  • The same event timestamp appearing in ≥3 unrelated target light curves (instrumental/spacecraft artefact) — NOT IMPLEMENTED.
  • The event's morphology fits a flare, starspot, or eclipsing-binary template better than the comet template under a formal model comparison — only the symmetric-vs-comet comparison exists (ModelComparison); no flare/starspot/EB template competes in the current compare_models() step.
  • Non-persistence: the same star observed in another sector/quarter shows no equivalent event where one would be expected for a periodic or quasi-periodic phenomenon — Next Steps J3 ("sector-overlap test... a dip present in one SPOC sector but absent from the overlapping sector is almost always instrumental") is PLANNED, NOT IMPLEMENTED, though lc.meta already carries the sector list post-A2, making this comparatively cheap to add.

docs.title: 66.4 The concrete cautionary example: the A4 reversed-dip case
docs.text: This document repeats, in the falsification frame specifically, the finding already central to §45.1 and §53.4: asymmetry alone does not imply a comet. docs/research_log/007-delta-bic-is-direction-blind.md's adversarial mirror-image test showed a ΔBIC-only rule would flag a physically backwards event more confidently (201) than a genuine comet-like one (151). The correct falsification logic is not "is this dip asymmetric" but "is this dip asymmetric in the specific direction (τ/σ > 1) that a trailing dust tail predicts, and can every alternative explanation in §66.2 that is currently checkable be ruled out." As the table above shows, most of §66.2's rows are currently NOT checkable by this pipeline — which is precisely why this document, and the pipeline's own output, never uses the word "confirmed."

docs.title: 66.5 What genuine confirmation would require (outside this pipeline's scope)
docs.text: Per README's "Honest limitations" and the general astronomical practice this project explicitly does not claim to replace: independent photometric or spectroscopic follow-up observation, multi-epoch persistence checks, and/or pixel-level vetting sufficient to rule out background contamination. See 67_observation_followup.md for why none of this is available to this project.

docs.title: 67. Observation Follow-up
docs.text: Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051.

docs.title: 67.1 Current state: NOT IMPLEMENTED, not applicable to this project's current scope
docs.text: This project has no telescope time, no observing proposal infrastructure, and no mechanism to request, schedule, or receive follow-up observations of any kind. It operates entirely on archival, already-public Kepler and TESS photometry retrieved from MAST (57_api_interface_contracts.md, 55_research_supply_chain.md). Nothing in the codebase or its documented roadmap (docs/NEXT_STEPS.md) proposes that this project itself would conduct or arrange follow-up observations.

docs.title: 67.2 What hypothetical follow-up would be needed, stated explicitly as future/hypothetical work
docs.text:
Were a candidate from this pipeline to warrant genuine confirmation (as opposed to remaining a "candidate consistent with an exocomet interpretation," per the vocabulary rule in §64.1), the kind of follow-up that astronomical practice generally requires — and that this project does not and cannot currently provide — would include:

  • Repeat photometric observation of the same star at a plausible future epoch, to check whether an aperiodic dimming event of similar character recurs (distinguishing a one-off transient from a repeating or quasi-periodic phenomenon) or to catch the same tail-producing body at a different orbital phase.
  • Higher-cadence or higher-precision photometry than the archival Kepler/TESS data, to better resolve the ingress/egress shape and reduce the depth-measurement uncertainty currently under investigation (docs/research_log/006).
  • Spectroscopic observation during a predicted or ongoing transit-like event, to look for the gas-absorption signatures (e.g., variable, blue-shifted absorption lines) that are the traditional confirmation method for exocomet activity in systems like β Pictoris — this pipeline works from broadband photometry alone and has no spectroscopic capability of any kind.
  • Pixel-level imaging or high-resolution imaging to independently confirm the dimming originates from the target star and not a background source — this is a different, cheaper check than full follow-up observation and is instead covered as a data-analysis gap (pixel-level/TPF vetting) in 45_decision_specification.md §45.5 and 66_falsification_and_alternatives.md, not this section, since it can be done with archival data already in hand (target pixel files) rather than requiring new telescope time.

docs.title: 67.3 Why this is stated explicitly rather than left implicit
docs.text:
The README's own "Honest limitations" section already states that a flagged event is a candidate, never confirmed, and that "confirmation needs follow-up this pipeline cannot provide." This section exists to make that limitation a first-class, addressable part of the specification rather than a single sentence easily missed — and to be explicit that nothing in this document should be read as implying such follow-up is planned, budgeted, or in progress. It is not.

Status: NOT IMPLEMENTED, not applicable — hypothetical future work only, external to this project's actual scope and resources.

docs.title: 68. Dataset Curation
docs.text: Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051.

docs.title: 68.1 Membership rules — real, code-enforced
docs.text:
Hold-out guard. EXCLUDED_HOLD_OUT_TARGETS = frozenset({"KIC 3542116", "KIC 11084727"}) (scripts/build_kepler_host_list.py) — these two stars are the final-exam validation set and must never appear in any training, injection-host, or generated-label dataset. Enforced at three independent points: (1) a module-level assert in build_kepler_host_list.py itself disjoint from KEPLER_HOST_STARS; (2) scripts/ingest.py::get_target_list() re-checks the assembled target list and raises AssertionError on any leak, described in its own docstring as "defense in depth, so a future third target source cannot silently leak a validation star into generated data"; (3) scripts/train_classifier.py implements a dedicated HoldOutError exception, raised (not merely warned) if either target ever appears in assembled training data (Next Steps C2).

Known-bad hosts. KNOWN_BAD_HOSTS = frozenset({"KIC 1026032"}) — found 2026-09-14 by direct pipeline inspection (not a catalog lookup) to have a real, strong (~8% deep, ~8.4-day period) periodic signal surviving detrending, almost certainly a genuine eclipsing binary. Asserted disjoint from KEPLER_HOST_STARS at import time. This is the precedent and stated justification for treating KIC 1161345's anomalous flag rate (§49.2) as an open concern requiring the same direct-inspection treatment before it is trusted.

Removed-as-nonexistent hosts. Five additional Kepler IDs (KIC 1571512, 3735741, 3839966, 4457741, 4569375) were removed from KEPLER_HOST_STARS after live ingest.yml runs failed identically, twice, six hours apart, with "Could not resolve ... to a sky position" — confirmed independently (not just trusting the resolver's error text) that none have any Kepler observations at all. These are documented as a distinct category from KNOWN_BAD_HOSTS: not astrophysically bad, simply nonexistent as observed targets, because the original hand-curated list was never checked against a real catalog (build_kepler_host_list.py's own module comment states this directly).

Important caveat, confirmed by direct inspection: this removal exists only in the local working tree as of this writing — git status/git diff on scripts/build_kepler_host_list.py confirms it is an uncommitted modification on top of HEAD (01c2051), which still contains the buggy ~23-target list including the five bad IDs. The 18-target count below describes the working tree, not the committed, currently-live code. Real, direct consequence: 23_automation.md's live gh run list query shows the two most recent scheduled ingest.yml runs (2026-09-16, 00:05 and 05:50 UTC) both failed — because the code actually running in production is still the pre-fix, 23-target list. See 59_error_taxonomy.md ERR-006 for the full account.

Current KEPLER_HOST_STARS size: 18 targets in the local working tree (uncommitted fix); 23 targets (including the five now-known-bad IDs) in the actual committed and currently-deployed code at 01c2051. Described in the module docstring as a hand-curated proxy for "quiet" stars (Kepler Objects of Interest not confirmed as planets or eclipsing binaries) — explicitly stated to be a stand-in for a planned, not-yet-built NASA Exoplanet Archive cross-match (Next Steps C1).

docs.title: 68.2 Real dataset statistics, re-verified today (2026-09-16)
docs.text:
The user-supplied figure of "33 unique targets touched, 25 succeeded / 8 failed" was independently re-verified by directly cloning the data repository and reading its ledger, rather than trusted as given:

git clone https://github.com/AJpro-merc/exocomet-hunter-data.git
wc -l ledger.jsonl        →  33 lines
grep '"status": "success"' | wc -l   →  25
grep '"status": "failed"'  | wc -l   →   8
python: count of unique (target_id, mission) pairs → 33

Result: the figure is confirmed accurate as of 2026-09-16, source: AJpro-merc/exocomet-hunter-data/ledger.jsonl (33 lines total, one entry per unique target/mission pair — no target has yet been retried, since 33 lines = 33 unique pairs = the full ledger). Of the results files inspected in the same clone, most have real per-star candidate counts (e.g. KIC_4349452.jsonl: 319 candidate rows; KIC_2989404.jsonl: 1 row; several TESS targets like beta_Pic.jsonl, 49_Ceti.jsonl have 0-row — i.e., present but empty — results files, a valid "processed, zero candidates" outcome per §44.2 REQ-FUNC-005). The training/ and models/ directories in the same clone contain only .gitkeep placeholders — no accumulated classifier training data or trained model exists yet, despite train.yml having run repeatedly (§65.4).

docs.title: 68.3 What "dataset curation" does NOT yet mean here
docs.text:
There is no formal inclusion/exclusion criterion beyond the hold-out/known-bad/nonexistent-ID exclusions above — no magnitude cut, no data-quality score threshold, no minimum baseline-length requirement, and no documented sampling frame for how a star enters KEPLER_HOST_STARS, watchlist.txt, or tess_training_hosts.txt beyond "hand-picked... chosen because infalling-comet activity is already established or plausible" (per each file's own header comment) for the watchlists, and "Kepler Objects of Interest that were not confirmed as planets or eclipsing binaries" for the Kepler host list. scripts/build_target_list.py's catalogue-driven, VizieR-sourced expansion (Cotten & Song 2016 debris-disc catalogue cross-matched to TIC) is real and has pulled genuine rows (505 rows, 5/5 matched to real TIC IDs in the one live run performed, per Session Log 2026-09-15 §11) but its matched-control-group logic returns zero control stars for every tested disc host and is therefore deliberately not wired into ingest.py's target sources (get_target_list() reads config/target_list_<mission>.txt only if it exists; no such file's presence was independently re-verified here).

Status: Hold-out/exclusion rules — IMPLEMENTED, TESTED, VALIDATED. Formal sampling-frame / inclusion criteria beyond hand-curation — NOT IMPLEMENTED. Catalogue-driven expansion — PARTIAL (real VizieR/TIC query logic works; control-group matching does not; not wired into the live ingestion pipeline).

docs.title: 69. Statistical Methodology
docs.text: Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051.

docs.title: 69.1 Implemented
docs.text:
BIC / ΔBIC model comparison. ModelComparison (core/types.py), computed by compare_models() (detect/model_comparison.py, referenced from detect/scoring.py). Fits a symmetric profile and a Gaussian-ingress/exponential-egress ("comet") profile to each event; ModelFit.bic = chi2 + n_params * ln(n_points) (returns inf for a non-converged fit); delta_bic = symmetric.bic - comet.bic. Threshold for "strong evidence" is 10.0, citing the conventional Kass & Raftery (1995) Bayes-factor guidance. Status: IMPLEMENTED, TESTED, VALIDATED as the primary ranking statistic (though see §69.3 for the shallow-event fit-instability caveat).

Bootstrap uncertainty on duration asymmetry. bootstrap_a_dur_sigma() (detect/scoring.py) perturbs in-event flux within its own error bars (bootstrap_draws, default 1000) and re-measures a_dur each time; the standard deviation of the resulting distribution is EventScore.a_dur_sigma, and significance = abs(a_dur) / a_dur_sigma. This is reported (EventScore.significance) but does not gate the flagged decision as of the A4 rewrite (§45.1) — it remains a classifier feature (FEATURE_NAMES includes both significance and a_dur_sigma). Status: IMPLEMENTED, TESTED (exercised by tests/unit/test_scoring.py, per the module's own test file existing; specific assertions not individually re-verified here).

Robust noise estimation. Baseline noise uses a MAD-based (median absolute deviation) robust estimator (MAD_TO_SIGMA constant referenced in detect/baseline.py / detrend/detrend.py), rather than plain standard deviation — chosen specifically so a real dip event does not inflate its own local noise estimate. Not read in full detail here; confirmed to exist by direct import reference in detrend.py.

Lomb-Scargle periodicity test. periodicity_flag() (detect/scoring.py) via astropy.timeseries.LombScargle, with a false-alarm-probability threshold of 0.01 — a conventional statistical significance test for periodic signals, used as a ranking penalty only (§45.2), never a rejection criterion.

docs.title: 69.2 Proposed, not implemented
docs.text:
Empirical look-elsewhere correction / trials factor (Next Steps D5, sharpened as J2). No code runs the detector over a large batch of null (quiet or time-reversed) light curves to produce an empirical false-alarm rate. Next Steps J2 specifically argues this is now affordable given the measured ~0.8 s/star processing speed (itself stale, see 70_performance_benchmarking.md) — "run the same detector over ~10,000 quiet or time-reversed light curves and quote 'N candidates per 10,000 null curves at this threshold.'" This is explicitly framed as more defensible than a formal p-value the project cannot yet justify, precisely because per-event significance (§69.1) does not currently account for how many stars/windows/configurations were searched (§53.3). Status: PLANNED, NOT IMPLEMENTED.

Bayesian candidate probability (Next Steps J7). A proposed P(exocomet | data) reported alongside the frequentist ΔBIC/τ/σ statistics, incorporating morphology, noise, contamination, and measured completeness. No prior, likelihood model, or posterior-computation code exists anywhere in this repository. Status: PLANNED, NOT IMPLEMENTED.

Formal ablation study (Next Steps D4). Measuring recall and false-positive rate with each pipeline component removed (detrending, robust noise vs. plain std, edge guard, search padding, periodicity penalty, bootstrap, model comparison, vetting) has not been run; no such table exists in any research log. Status: PLANNED, NOT IMPLEMENTED.

Classifier-derived probability (Next Steps C3/C4). scripts/train_classifier.py is written (RandomForestClassifier wrapped in CalibratedClassifierCV, isotonic calibration, GroupKFold split by host star, class_weight="balanced", SimpleImputer for missing feature values) but, per Next Steps C2, "not fully verified" — the real-data backtest step hung for 9+ minutes in testing and was killed before completing. C3's required evaluation numbers (ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, recall at 1% FPR, confusion matrix, completeness curves, permutation feature importance, the "final exam" of all six KIC 3542116 dips scoring above threshold) have not been produced — no docs/research_log/006-classifier-v1.md (the file C3 specifies) exists in this repository. Separately, the training/ directory in the live data repository was confirmed (§68.2) to contain no accumulated labelled parquet data as of this document's version, meaning there is currently no data to run C2/C3 against even if the backtest hang were resolved. Status: PARTIAL (training script written; C3 evaluation NOT PRODUCED; underlying training data NOT YET ACCUMULATED).

docs.title: 69.3 A statistical caveat that spans both categories
docs.text: The comet-model fit instability found during the B1 investigation (§49.3 — one dip fit at 3.47× its published depth) means the ΔBIC and τ/σ values §69.1 relies on as "implemented and validated" are validated specifically for the six well-characterized KIC 3542116 dips, most of which are not in the shallow regime where the instability was observed (D140, the shallowest at 491 ppm published, was the one that diverged). This caveat is repeated here because §69.1's status markers would otherwise overstate confidence in the statistical machinery's behavior across the full depth range the pipeline is meant to operate over.

docs.title: 70. Performance Benchmarking
docs.text: Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051.

docs.title: 70.1 Real numbers on record — with caveats
docs.text: Metric Value Source Caveat Full-mission Kepler processing ~0.8 s per star (65,000 cadences, ~4 years) README.md; originally measured Session Log 2026-09-13 Next Steps B8 explicitly states this table was measured before the A1 (day-based window conversion) and A4 (flag-rule) changes and has not been regenerated since. The measurement context (hardware, whether it includes network fetch time or detection-only, warm vs. cold cache) is not documented alongside the number. Treat as UNVERIFIED under current code. Injection cost ~87 ms each docs/NEXT_STEPS.md "Reference: key numbers" Same caveat as above — no re-measurement date given, measurement conditions (host light-curve length, whether detection was re-run per injection) not documented. KIC 3542116 post-detrend noise 83 ppm docs/NEXT_STEPS.md "Reference: key numbers" A real, specific number tied to one star; not documented as re-verified after the A1 window-unit change (window sizes changed from cadence-count to day-based, which could shift the detrended noise floor). Contour sign-flip point τ/σ ≈ 1.70 docs/research_log/003-half-depth-contour-sign-error.md This is a derived mathematical constant (from the Gaussian/exponential half-depth-crossing algebra), not an empirical measurement — it does not need re-verification against code changes the way the timing numbers do.

docs.title: 70.2 What has NOT been measured / regenerated
docs.text:
• Injection-recovery completeness curve. The README's headline "50% detection floor near 750 ppm, 100% recovery above 1000 ppm" (200 synthetic injections) is the same measurement flagged stale by Next Steps B8 — it predates A1 and A4. See CLAIM-006 in 43_scientific_claims_registry.md.
  • TESS-cadence timing. All timing numbers on record are Kepler-specific; no equivalent per-star timing figure for TESS (120 s SPOC cadence, which after A2 is the pinned default) was found in any document reviewed for this section.
  • Ingestion pipeline per-target wall-clock time on GitHub Actions infrastructure. Session Log 2026-09-15 §11/§12 describes real runs completing within their time budgets (3-minute smoke test, 25-minute budgeted hourly runs) but does not report a specific mean per-target duration on that infrastructure specifically (as opposed to the 0.8 s/star figure, which appears to be a local-machine, detection-only measurement).
  • Memory footprint. No peak-memory measurement for any script is recorded anywhere in the documents reviewed for this section.

docs.title: 70.3 Automated benchmark infrastructure
docs.text:
tests/benchmarks/__init__.py exists and contains only:

"""Test package."""

No benchmark test file exists in tests/benchmarks/. pytest-benchmark is declared as a dev dependency in pyproject.toml ([project.optional-dependencies].dev), but nothing in the repository invokes it. Next Steps E7 ("Benchmarks: tests/benchmarks/ with pytest-benchmark: runtime vs light-curve length, peak memory per star") is the tracked, unbuilt item this corresponds to.

Status: NOT IMPLEMENTED. No regression-benchmark suite exists; the numbers in §70.1 are one-off, undocumented-methodology measurements from session notes, not outputs of a repeatable, version-controlled benchmark.

docs.title: 70.4 What re-measurement would require
docs.text: To produce a trustworthy current performance baseline: (1) re-run the injection-recovery grid (calibration/injection.run_injection_recovery, or exocomet inject) against the current post-A1/A4 code on both Kepler and TESS-cadence data, with the run's exact conditions (hardware, host star length, number of injections) recorded; (2) write an actual pytest-benchmark-based test in tests/benchmarks/ per Next Steps E7's own scope (runtime vs. light-curve length, peak memory per star); (3) record results with a provenance manifest (§52) so future comparisons are apples-to-apples. None of this exists today.

docs.title: 71. Documentation Quality System
docs.text: Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051.

docs.title: 71.1 What exists: a manual checklist, not automated CI
docs.text:
This project has no CI job that checks documentation against code. What is introduced alongside this specification is a manual checklist, run whenever a 20-commit documentation rollup happens (see docs/DOCUMENTATION_WORKFLOW.md for the full 13-step process). The checklist itself:

  1. Every documented function/class still exists. For each function or class name mentioned in the specification (e.g. fetch_light_curve, AsymmetricDipDetector, score_event), run grep -rn "def <name>\|class <name>" src/ scripts/ and confirm at least one real match. A documented name with zero matches is STALE.
  2. Every documented config field still exists. For each key path mentioned (e.g. scoring.delta_bic_threshold), confirm it is present in config/thresholds.yaml and in the corresponding dataclass in core/config.py. A field present in one but not the other is a real inconsistency worth its own note (see 46_parameter_provenance.md §46.4 for one already found: asymmetry.search_padding_factor exists in core/config.py but not in config/thresholds.yaml).
  3. Every documented CLI command still exists. For each exocomet <subcommand> mentioned, confirm it appears in build_parser() in src/exocomet/cli.py.

This is explicitly a checklist run by hand, reading grep output and making a judgment call — it is not wired into CI, and no script automates even the mechanical parts of it (running the three greps and diffing the result against the doc's claimed names) as of this commit.

docs.title: 71.2 Why manual, for now
docs.text: Building an automated version would require: (a) a way to extract "claimed names/fields/commands" from Markdown prose reliably (the specification files are prose with inline code spans, not a structured schema a script could parse without false positives/negatives), and (b) a policy for what to do on a mismatch (fail CI? file an issue? auto-annotate the doc as STALE?). None of this exists, and building it is out of scope for this document — see 72_code_doc_crosscheck.md for the closely related concept of automated code/doc cross-checking, also NOT IMPLEMENTED as tooling.

docs.title: 71.3 Relationship to the rollup process
docs.text:
Per docs/DOCUMENTATION_WORKFLOW.md, this checklist is meant to run specifically as a pre-rollup audit, before compressing 20 commits' worth of docs/CHANGELOG_PENDING.md scaffold entries into a permanent docs/CHANGELOG.md rollup entry — the idea being that a rollup is a natural checkpoint to catch documentation drift before it compounds further, not that every individual commit needs it.

Status: PLANNED as a described process (this section and docs/DOCUMENTATION_WORKFLOW.md are that description); NOT IMPLEMENTED as an automated or even semi-automated tool.

docs.title: 72. Code/Documentation Cross-Check
docs.text: Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051.

docs.title: 72.1 The concept
docs.text:
For any specific documentation claim of the form "X exists in the code at location Y," a cross-check asks: does grep/AST inspection of the actual source confirm X still exists at (or near) Y, and does its signature/behavior still match what the documentation says? A result is either MATCH (confirmed as documented) or STALE (documentation no longer describes the code).

This section documents the process, and gives real worked examples performed directly against this codebase, rather than describing hypothetical tooling.

docs.title: 72.2 Worked examples
docs.text: Documentation claim Cross-check performed Result "flagged = delta_bic > cfg.delta_bic_threshold and tau_over_sigma > cfg.tau_over_sigma_threshold" (§45.1) Read src/exocomet/detect/scoring.py lines ~160–165 directly MATCH — exact text reproduced from source, confirmed present at time of reading "asymmetry.search_padding_factor config field exists" Compared core/config.py's AsymmetryConfig dataclass fields against config/thresholds.yaml's asymmetry: section keys STALE relative to the YAML file — the field exists in the dataclass default but has no corresponding key in config/thresholds.yaml, meaning a YAML override cannot currently reach it. Documented as a genuine finding in 46_parameter_provenance.md §46.4, not silently corrected. "README's injection-recovery completeness numbers (50% floor near 750 ppm)" Checked against Next Steps B8's own explicit note that this measurement predates the A1/A4 code changes STALE — the documentation (README) has not been updated since the underlying code changed. Flagged in 43_scientific_claims_registry.md CLAIM-006 and 70_performance_benchmarking.md §70.1 rather than treated as current. "training/ directory in the data repo holds accumulated classifier training rows" (implied by train.yml running every 2 hours since it was written) Directly cloned AJpro-merc/exocomet-hunter-data and listed training/ STALE relative to the implied claim — only a .gitkeep file exists; no training parquet has landed despite the workflow running repeatedly. Documented in 65_false_positive_catalogue.md §65.4 and 69_statistical_methodology.md §69.2. "Next Steps.md's 'FIRST THING NEXT SESSION' list says DATA_REPO_TOKEN still needs setting up" Compared against Session Log 2026-09-15 §12 (same source document family) which states the token was added and a live push was confirmed, and against the current git HEAD commit matching that section's cited commit STALE (the "FIRST THING" list, relative to §12's later, more specific, directly-corroborated account) — flagged explicitly in 51_pipeline_observability.md §51.3 as an internal inconsistency in the project's own notes, not silently resolved in one direction.

docs.title: 72.3 What this means in practice
docs.text: Four of the five worked cross-checks above found a STALE result, not a MATCH. This is not evidence of unusually poor documentation discipline — it is exactly the expected outcome of a fast-moving project whose session logs are the primary record and whose top-level docs (README, Next Steps) are updated less frequently than the code and data actually change. It is direct, concrete evidence for why §71's checklist and this section's cross-check concept matter, and why both are currently manual: an automated version would need to be run far more often than once per full review to keep pace with a project at this rate of change.

docs.title: 72.4 Current tooling: NONE
docs.text:
No script in this repository performs this cross-check automatically. The table in §72.2 was produced by direct reading of source files against documentation claims — the same process 71_documentation_quality_system.md's checklist describes, applied here to yield concrete before/after evidence that the process finds real drift when actually run.

Status: NOT IMPLEMENTED as tooling. The concept and its value are demonstrated in §72.2; automating it is future work, not started.

docs.title: Reading this table honestly
docs.text: Two subsystems are genuinely close to mature by this project's own bar: Data Acquisition and Database/Ledger, both with real fixes validated against real failures they actually hit in production-like conditions. Two are genuinely near-zero: Vetting (literally an empty package) and the Classifier (written but with no confirmed real evaluation and no accumulated training data). The remainder sit in a realistic middle: working code, incomplete test/validation coverage, and at least one open, named bug or gap each. This distribution — strong infrastructure, weak scientific rigor layer — matches the plain-language summary at the top of docs/NEXT_STEPS.md and is not an artifact of unusually critical scoring; it is a direct read of the evidence gathered in sections 43–72 above.

docs.title: 76.4 One real example candidate record
docs.text:
Pulled directly from AJpro-merc/exocomet-hunter-data/results/Kepler/KIC_1161345.jsonl (first line), cloned directly on 2026-09-16:

{"target_id": "KIC 1161345", "t_min": 122.95008577283913, "depth_ppm": 1498.9501060346245,
 "duration_days": 0.9808628563769162, "a_dur": 0.12020535975282774, "a_slope": 0.10042584112591929,
 "ingress_duration_days": 0.2774508311957362, "egress_duration_days": 0.35326642599916624,
 "a_dur_sigma": 0.1672204364056346, "significance": 0.718843715138022,
 "delta_bic": -409.4210857549401, "tau_over_sigma": 2.118670089087749, "signs_agree": true,
 "flagged": false, "periodic": true, "period_days": 7.9912409134324305,
 "vetting_status": null, "vetting_reasons": null}

Note this specific event is "flagged": false despite tau_over_sigma > 1 — because delta_bic is strongly negative (-409), i.e. the symmetric model fits this event far better than the comet profile, correctly failing the ΔBIC half of the two-condition rule (§45.1). vetting_status/vetting_reasons are null, consistent with §45.5/§58.2 (no Vetter implementation exists). This is real output from KIC 1161345, the star flagged as an open concern in 49_negative_results.md §49.2 — this specific record is one of the ~260 detected events there, and (being unflagged) is not one of the 43 flagged ones driving that concern.

docs.title: 35. Code Reference — exocomet.calibration
docs.text: Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051 (unmodified in the working tree's uncommitted diff). IMPLEMENTED. Cross-reference: 21_injection_recovery.md for narrative/design context and the caveat on the README's stated completeness numbers.

docs.title: inject_comet_transit(time, flux, t0, depth, ingress_duration, egress_duration) -> FloatArray
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/calibration/injection.py:46-81

Lines 46–79. Piecewise-linear ramp down over ingress_duration days to t0, then linear ramp up over egress_duration days. Deliberately not the Gaussian/exponential shape detect/model_comparison.py fits — tests recovery of an event the model wasn't tuned for. No bounds checking on time/flux shape match; caller must supply matching arrays.

docs.title: inject_flare(time, flux, t0, amplitude, rise_duration, decay_duration) -> FloatArray
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/calibration/injection.py:82-119

Lines 82–117. Linear rise over rise_duration, then exponential decay (amplitude * exp(-(t - t0) / decay_duration)) for all t > t0 (not windowed — the decay tail is added for the entire remainder of the array, unlike the comet injector's windowed ramps). Adds flux (brightening), the sign-flipped opposite of a comet transit.

docs.title: inject_starspot_modulation(time, flux, period_days, amplitude, phase=0.0) -> FloatArray
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/calibration/injection.py:120-148

Lines 120–145. flux + amplitude * sin(2π * time / period_days + phase) applied to the entire array, not localised — the only injector of the three that modulates the whole light curve rather than one event.

docs.title: InjectionResult (frozen dataclass, lines 148–165)
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/calibration/injection.py:149-168

Fields: t0, depth, ingress_duration, egress_duration, detected: bool, flagged: bool, recovered_t0: float | None, recovered_a_dur: float | None, delta_bic: float. Property depth_ppm (depth * 1e6).

docs.title: RecoveryGrid (frozen dataclass, lines 168–215)
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/calibration/injection.py:169-217

Field: results: tuple[InjectionResult, ...]. - n_injected — len(results). Source: src/exocomet/calibration/injection.py:175-178 - completeness(flagged_only=True) -> float — fraction with .flagged (default) or .detected true. 0.0 if results is empty. Source: src/exocomet/calibration/injection.py:179-194 - completeness_by_depth(flagged_only=True) -> dict[float, float] — per-depth recovery fraction, keys sorted ascending. Source: src/exocomet/calibration/injection.py:195-202 - detection_floor(target_completeness=0.5) -> float | None — shallowest depth reaching target_completeness; None if none do. Source: src/exocomet/calibration/injection.py:203-217

docs.title: run_injection_recovery(lc, detector, depths, ingress_duration=0.1, egress_duration=0.5, n_per_depth=20, match_tolerance_days=0.5, config=None, rng=None) -> RecoveryGrid
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/calibration/injection.py:218-303

Lines 218–303. Raises ValueError if the light curve is too short to host an injection clear of both edges (edge_margin_days + egress_duration + ingress_duration padding on each side). For each of depths × n_per_depth injections: random epoch, inject via inject_comet_transit, run the unmodified detector.run(injected), match any returned event within match_tolerance_days of the injected t0, keep the highest-significance match as best. An injection is detected if any match exists, flagged if best.score.flagged is also true.

docs.title: FEATURE_NAMES: tuple[str, ...] (lines 28–48)
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/calibration/features.py:28-48

Fixed, ordered tuple of 19 feature names — order is load-bearing: "a trained model stores coefficients against these positions, so appending is safe but reordering silently corrupts predictions" (module comment, line 27). Exact order: depth_ppm, log_depth_ppm, duration_days, depth_snr, a_dur, a_slope, abs_a_dur, signs_agree, tau_over_sigma, log_tau_over_sigma, delta_bic, significance, a_dur_sigma, ingress_duration_days, egress_duration_days, ingress_slope_snr, egress_slope_snr, n_points_in_window, periodic.

docs.title: extract_features(record, lc) -> dict[str, float]
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/calibration/features.py:63-114

Lines 63–112. Reduces one CandidateRecord to exactly the 19 keys in FEATURE_NAMES. Unmeasurable quantities (e.g. asym is None) become float("nan"), never a sentinel numeric value — "so that a model cannot mistake a missing measurement for a real extreme value." depth_snr = event.depth / noise where noise = 1.4826 * median(|lc.flux - median(lc.flux)|) — a global (whole-light-curve) robust noise estimate, independent of the per-event local noise used in detection. _safe_log(value) (private, lines 51–53) returns nan instead of raising or returning -inf for non-positive/non-finite input. (Source: src/exocomet/calibration/features.py:51-55) _slope_snr(slope, slope_err) (private, lines 56–60) returns nan if either input is non-finite or slope_err <= 0, else |slope| / slope_err. (Source: src/exocomet/calibration/features.py:56-62)

docs.title: features_to_matrix(rows: list[dict[str, float]]) -> np.ndarray
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/calibration/features.py:115-122

Lines 115–122. Stacks feature dicts into a 2-D float64 array in FEATURE_NAMES order; missing keys in a row default to nan via row.get(name, float("nan")). Returns an empty (0, len(FEATURE_NAMES)) array for an empty input list, not a (0,) or error.

docs.title: Design note carried from the module docstring (calibration/features.py)
docs.text: The classifier this module feeds "never sees a light curve. It sees only the measurements this module produces" — an explicit interpretability and provenance choice: "when the model ranks an event highly it is possible to say which measured property drove it," and "the model only weighs evidence it is handed; it never invents a detection." No classifier training code (scripts/train_classifier.py) was reviewed as part of this batch; this reference covers calibration/ only.

docs.title: 35. Code Reference — exocomet.cli
docs.text:
Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051. IMPLEMENTED. Cross-reference: 34_development.md for install/usage context.

Module: src/exocomet/cli.py. Declared in pyproject.toml as exocomet = "exocomet.cli:main". Every heavyweight or network-touching import (numpy, yaml, the detrend/detect/io modules) is deferred inside the function that needs it — this is deliberate, so exocomet --help returns instantly with zero network access and no science-stack import cost, mirroring the lazy import lightkurve pattern in io/download.py. __all__ = build_parser, main.

docs.title: build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/cli.py:256-308

Constructs the full parser, separated from main() specifically so tests can exercise argument parsing without executing a pipeline or touching the network (tests/unit/test_cli.py). Top-level flags: --version (prints _version_string()), -v/--verbose (INFO-level logging). Subcommands, via add_subparsers(dest="command", metavar="{run,validate,inject}"):

docs.title: run subcommand → cmd_run(args) -> int
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/cli.py:117-148

Arguments: target (positional, e.g. "KIC 3542116"), --mission {Kepler,TESS} (default Kepler), --config PATH (YAML overrides), --all-events (print every event, not just flagged), --no-detrend (skip Savitzky-Golay detrending), --out PATH (also write every event as JSON Lines via CandidateRecord.to_row()).

Behavior: fetches and (unless --no-detrend) detrends the target via _prepare_light_curve(), runs AsymmetricDipDetector(config).run(lc), prints a summary line and one formatted line per shown event (_format_record), and optionally writes every record (not just shown ones) to --out as JSON Lines with default=str for non-JSON-native types. Returns 0 always (no failure path defined beyond the shared exception handler in main()).

docs.title: validate subcommand → cmd_validate(args) -> int
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/cli.py:149-210

Arguments: --targets PATH (default config/validation_targets.yaml), --config PATH.

Behavior: the validation gate. Loads the YAML spec, and for each target with at least one transcribed dip, fetches+detrends+detects, then for each published dip finds the highest-significance match within match_tolerance_days (default 0.5 d from the YAML, or the spec's own value). Prints PASS/MISS/ERROR/SKIP per dip — SKIP specifically for a target with dips: [] (KIC 11084727, per Next Steps B5 — the docstring is explicit that "counting it as a pass would make the gate a lie, and failing on it would block on a missing number"). Returns 0 only if n_expected > 0 and every expected dip was recovered; 1 otherwise (including the case of zero expected dips at all, which prevents a vacuously-true pass).

docs.title: inject subcommand → cmd_inject(args) -> int
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/cli.py:211-255

Arguments: --n (injections per depth, default 20), --depths (fractional depths to sweep; defaults to DEFAULT_INJECTION_DEPTHS = (2e-4, 5e-4, 1e-3, 2e-3, 5e-3), chosen to bracket the published KIC 3542116 dip range of 491–1900 ppm on both sides), --ingress/--egress (durations in days, defaults 0.1/0.5), --target (inject into real photometry for this star; omit for a synthetic host), --mission, --n-points/--noise (synthetic-host parameters, used only without --target), --config.

Behavior: measures detection completeness via calibration.injection.run_injection_recovery, printing a per-depth table of raw-detection and flagged-detection completeness, overall flagged completeness, and the 50%-detection-depth floor (or "not reached by any tested depth" if none). Without --target, builds a flat noise-only synthetic host via the private _synthetic_light_curve() helper (Kepler long-cadence sampling, cadence_days = 0.02043) — the docstring is explicit that real photometry via --target is preferable "because real systematics are then part of the test," and the synthetic path exists only so the command remains runnable and reviewable offline.

docs.title: _load_config(path) -> PipelineConfig (private)
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/cli.py:52-58

PipelineConfig.from_yaml(path) if a path is given, else the built-in PipelineConfig() defaults.

docs.title: _prepare_light_curve(target_id, mission, config, detrend=True) -> LightCurveData (private)
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/cli.py:59-73

Shared fetch-then-detrend sequence: fetch_light_curve(target_id, mission=mission, discard_after_read=True) then detrend_savgol(lc, config.detrend) unless detrend=False. Identical in structure to the sequence used by scripts/monitor_new_data.py and scripts/train_classifier.py — the CLI does not duplicate pipeline logic, it wires together the same functions those scripts call directly.

docs.title: _format_record(record) -> str (private)
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/cli.py:74-87

Renders one CandidateRecord as a single aligned console line: FLAG/blank marker, t_min, depth (ppm), dur (days), a_dur (or n/a if unmeasurable), sig (significance), dBIC, tau/sigma — all fixed-width formatted for column alignment across many printed rows.

docs.title: _synthetic_light_curve(n_points, noise_sigma, seed) -> LightCurveData (private)
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/cli.py:88-116

Builds a flat, Gaussian-noise-only LightCurveData at Kepler long-cadence spacing, used only by cmd_inject when --target is omitted. meta carries synthetic=True and noise_sigma.

docs.title: _version_string() -> str (private)
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/cli.py:309-318

Returns f"exocomet-hunter {version('exocomet-hunter')}" via importlib.metadata.version, falling back to "exocomet-hunter (not installed)" on PackageNotFoundError — lets --version work from an editable/source checkout as well as an installed wheel.

docs.title: main(argv=None) -> int
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/cli.py:319-353

Parses arguments, prints help and returns 2 if no subcommand was given, configures logging (INFO if -v, else WARNING), then dispatches to the subcommand's func. Exit codes: 0 success, 1 a failed run (missed validation dip, unavailable target, malformed config — anything raising inside a subcommand handler), 2 usage error (no subcommand), 130 on KeyboardInterrupt. All exceptions besides KeyboardInterrupt are caught, logged at DEBUG with a full traceback (exc_info=True), and reported to the user as a single error: {exc} line on stderr — the CLI never lets a raw traceback reach an end user's terminal.

docs.title: Module-level constants
docs.text: Name Value Used by DEFAULT_VALIDATION_TARGETS Path("config/validation_targets.yaml") validate subcommand default MISSIONS ("Kepler", "TESS") --mission choices on run/inject DEFAULT_INJECTION_DEPTHS (2.0e-4, 5.0e-4, 1.0e-3, 2.0e-3, 5.0e-3) inject subcommand default depth sweep

docs.title: 35. Code Reference — exocomet.detect
docs.text: Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051 (this package is unmodified in the working tree's uncommitted diff). IMPLEMENTED. Cross-reference: 14_candidate_detection.md, 15_model_fitting.md, 16_statistics.md, 17_uncertainty.md for narrative/design context.

docs.title: days_to_cadences(days, cadence_days) -> int
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/detect/baseline.py:42-69

Lines 42–67. Converts a duration in days to a whole cadence count: max(round(days / cadence_days), 1). Raises ValueError if cadence_days <= 0.0.

docs.title: odd_window(window, n_points) -> int
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/detect/baseline.py:70-92

Lines 70–90. Clamps window to an odd value in [1, n_points]. Raises ValueError if window < 1.

docs.title: rolling_median(values, window) -> FloatArray
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/detect/baseline.py:93-105

Lines 93–103. Centred running median via pandas.Series.rolling(window=odd_window(...), center=True, min_periods=1).median(). Edges are truncated (fewer real points), never padded — see 14_candidate_detection.md §14.1 for the measured 30-70σ false-edge- significance this was found to prevent.

docs.title: rolling_baseline(flux, window) -> FloatArray
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/detect/baseline.py:106-124

Lines 106–122. Alias-with-docstring around rolling_median — the local out-of-dip reference level.

docs.title: local_noise(flux, baseline, window) -> FloatArray
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/detect/baseline.py:125-157

Lines 125–157. Robust per-cadence sigma: MAD_TO_SIGMA * rolling_median(|flux - baseline|, window), floored at max(global_sigma * 1e-3, np.finfo(np.float64).tiny) to avoid a zero denominator on perfectly flat stretches.

docs.title: MAD_TO_SIGMA: float = 1.4826 (module constant, line 39)
docs.text: Gaussian-equivalent scale factor for a median absolute deviation.

docs.title: depth_significance(flux, baseline, sigma) -> FloatArray
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/detect/candidates.py:24-31

Lines 24–29. (baseline - flux) / sigma, positive = dimming.

docs.title: find_candidate_events(time, flux, baseline, sigma, config=None) -> list[EventWindow]
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/detect/candidates.py:94-168

Lines 94–168. Main entry point; see 14_candidate_detection.md §14.2 for the full seven-step algorithm (threshold → run-length → merge → edge-guard → expand → disjoint-clamp). Parameters: config: CandidateConfig | None, defaults applied if omitted. Returns: non-overlapping EventWindow list, ordered in time. Notes: fully vectorised except the bounded outward-expansion loop per surviving run (_expand_window), so cost is linear in cadence count.

docs.title: _find_runs(mask) -> list[tuple[int, int]] (private, lines 32–40)
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/detect/candidates.py:32-42

Vectorised inclusive (start, end) run detection via np.diff on a zero-padded boolean mask.

docs.title: _merge_runs(runs, max_gap) -> list[tuple[int, int]] (private, lines 43–54)
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/detect/candidates.py:43-56

Merges runs separated by <= max_gap cadences.

docs.title: _expand_window(time, significance, start, end, recovery_sigma, max_window_days) -> tuple[int, int] (private, lines 57–91)
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/detect/candidates.py:57-93

Grows a run outward on each side while significance > recovery_sigma and the window has not exceeded max_window_days (measured from the run's centre time).

docs.title: ols_slope(x, y) -> tuple[float, float]
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/detect/asymmetry.py:43-76

Lines 43–74. Ordinary least squares y = a + b x. Returns (slope, slope_err); (nan, inf) if x.size < 3 or zero spread in x.

docs.title: locate_minimum(time, flux, window) -> tuple[float, float, int]
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/detect/asymmetry.py:77-114

Lines 77–112. Sub-cadence minimum via a parabola through the deepest cadence and its two neighbours; falls back to the discrete minimum if the three points are collinear or the fitted vertex falls outside the central cadence. Returns (t_min, f_min, index).

docs.title: measure_side(time, flux, window, idx_min, t_min, baseline_level, depth, side, config=None, search_bound=None) -> SideFit | None
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/detect/asymmetry.py:154-237

Lines 154–235. Measures one side ("ingress" or "egress") between the half-depth crossing and the minimum. Returns None when the half-depth level is never crossed within the search region, or too few cadences remain to fit a slope (config.min_points_per_side, default 3) — an unmeasurable side is reported as such, never scored on noise.

docs.title: _half_depth_crossing(time, flux, idx_min, bound, half_level, direction) -> tuple[float, int] | None (private, lines 115–151)
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/detect/asymmetry.py:115-153

Walks outward from the minimum until flux recovers past half_level, then linearly interpolates the crossing time. None if the flux never recovers within [idx_min, bound].

docs.title: compute_asymmetry(ingress, egress) -> AsymmetryResult
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/detect/asymmetry.py:238-257

Lines 238–255. a_dur = (egress.duration - ingress.duration) / (egress.duration + ingress.duration); a_slope = (|ingress.slope| - |egress.slope|) / (|ingress.slope| + |egress.slope|). Both 0.0 if their respective denominator is <= 0.

docs.title: measure_event(time, flux, baseline, window, target_id, config=None) -> DipEvent
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/detect/asymmetry.py:258-309

Lines 258–309. Full per-event measurement: locate minimum, measure both sides (searching up to config.search_padding_factor × window.n_points cadences beyond the detected window on each side), combine into AsymmetryResult if both sides measurable. Returns a DipEvent with asymmetry=None and a populated unmeasurable_reason string if either side could not be fitted — never raises for an unmeasurable event.

docs.title: detect/model_comparison.py
docs.text:
See 15_model_fitting.md for full mathematical detail. Function signatures:

  • symmetric_profile(t, t0, depth, width, baseline) -> FloatArray (lines 44–63) Source: src/exocomet/detect/model_comparison.py:44-65
  • comet_profile(t, t0, depth, ingress_width, egress_tau, baseline) -> FloatArray (lines 66–95) Source: src/exocomet/detect/model_comparison.py:66-97
  • compare_models(time, flux, flux_err, event, baseline_level, padding_factor=1.5, delta_bic_threshold=10.0) -> ModelComparison | None (lines 141–221) — Returns None when fewer than 8 cadences fall in the padded fitting window (insufficient to constrain the 5-parameter comet model). Source: src/exocomet/detect/model_comparison.py:141-220
  • _fit(name, model, x0, bounds, t, y, yerr) -> ModelFit (private, lines 102–138) — bounded scipy.optimize.least_squares (method="trf", max_nfev=2000); degrades to converged=False, chi2=inf on ValueError/RuntimeError rather than raising. Source: src/exocomet/detect/model_comparison.py:102-140
  • _MIN_WIDTH_DAYS: float = 1.0e-4 (module constant) — floor on fitted widths/tau.

docs.title: detect/scoring.py
docs.text:
See 16_statistics.md/17_uncertainty.md for full detail. Function signatures:

  • bootstrap_a_dur_sigma(time, flux, flux_err, baseline, event, draws, rng, config=None) -> tuple[float, int] (lines 28–69) — Returns (nan, n_valid) if fewer than 2 of draws perturbed remeasurements produced a measurable event. Source: src/exocomet/detect/scoring.py:28-71
  • periodicity_flag(lc, config=None) -> tuple[bool, float | None] (lines 72–107) — Lomb-Scargle over the whole light curve. Returns (False, None) if lc.n_points < 10 or lc.baseline_days <= 0; (False, best_period) if the false- alarm probability itself cannot be computed (ValueError/ZeroDivisionError, "a pragma: no cover — degenerate photometry" case). Source: src/exocomet/detect/scoring.py:72-109
  • score_event(event, lc, baseline, config=None, asymmetry_config=None, rng=None, periodic=False, period_days=None) -> EventScore (lines 110–211) — the flagging decision. Fails closed: flagged=False whenever delta_bic or tau_over_sigma is non-finite (unfittable/degenerate model comparison). Source: src/exocomet/detect/scoring.py:110-211

docs.title: AsymmetricDipDetector(config: PipelineConfig | None = None)
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/detect/comet_detector.py:28-117

Lines 28–118. Implements the Detector protocol (core/interfaces.py). name = "asymmetric-dip". Deliberately thin — "owns no science of its own; it sequences the baseline estimation, candidate finding, geometric measurement and statistical scoring implemented in the sibling modules" (module docstring).

  • baseline_and_noise(lc) -> tuple[FloatArray, FloatArray] (lines 48–54) — converts config.baseline.median_window_days/noise_window_days to cadences via days_to_cadences(days, lc.cadence_days) and calls rolling_baseline/ local_noise. Source: src/exocomet/detect/comet_detector.py:48-55
  • detect(lc) -> list[DipEvent] (lines 56–70) — finds candidate windows, measures each into a DipEvent. Unmeasurable events are still returned (see measure_event above). Source: src/exocomet/detect/comet_detector.py:56-71
  • score(event, lc) -> EventScore (lines 72–85) — recomputes the baseline for the parent light curve, calls periodicity_flag and score_event. Note: this recomputes baseline/noise and the periodogram independently, at real cost, if called per-event rather than via .run(). Source: src/exocomet/detect/comet_detector.py:72-86
  • run(lc) -> list[CandidateRecord] (lines 87–117) — the efficient path, Source: src/exocomet/detect/comet_detector.py:87-117 overriding the base Detector.run(): computes baseline/noise and the periodogram once for the whole light curve, then loops once over detected windows to build each CandidateRecord(event=..., score=...). Returns [] immediately if no candidate windows are found (skips the periodogram computation entirely in that case).

Constructor seeds self._rng = np.random.default_rng(config.runtime.rng_seed) (default seed 42) — the RNG instance is held per-detector, so successive .run() calls on the same detector instance produce different bootstrap draws each time (the RNG's internal state advances), while a fresh detector with the same seed reproduces the same first-call sequence.

docs.title: 35. Code Reference — exocomet.detrend
docs.text: Status: reflects repo state as of 2026-09-16, commit 01c2051. IMPLEMENTED. Cross-reference: 13_detrending.md for narrative/design context.

docs.title: detrend_savgol(lc, config=None) -> LightCurveData
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/detrend/detrend.py:53-90

src/exocomet/detrend/detrend.py lines 53–88.

Parameters - lc: LightCurveData — normalised light curve (flux ≈ 1.0 out of transit). - config: DetrendConfig | None — defaults to DetrendConfig() if omitted.

Returns LightCurveData — a copy with flux divided by the fitted Savitzky-Golay trend. meta gains detrend_method ("savgol" or "none"), detrend_window (cadence count actually used), detrend_polyorder, detrend_clipped_points.

Raises Nothing directly. Degrades silently to detrend_method="none" (flux unchanged) if window <= config.polyorder after conversion from days.

Failure modes A near-zero fitted trend value is clamped to 1.0 before division (np.where(np.abs(trend) < 1e-12, 1.0, trend)) to avoid inf/nan propagation.

docs.title: detrend_spline(lc, config=None) -> LightCurveData
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/detrend/detrend.py:91-121

Lines 91–119. Same parameter/return shape as detrend_savgol. Uses scipy.interpolate.LSQUnivariateSpline with interior knots spaced every config.spline_knot_spacing_days across lc.time[0]..lc.time[-1], degree k=3. Degrades to detrend_method="none" if fewer than 1 interior knot results or lc.n_points < 8. meta gains detrend_method, detrend_knot_spacing_days, detrend_clipped_points (no detrend_window/detrend_polyorder — those are savgol-specific).

docs.title: SavGolDetrender / SplineDetrender
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/detrend/detrend.py:122-132 (SavGolDetrender), src/exocomet/detrend/detrend.py:133-141 (SplineDetrender)

Lines 122–142. Thin classes implementing the Detrender protocol (core/interfaces.py): __init__(self, config=None) stores self.config = config or DetrendConfig(); .detrend(lc) calls the corresponding module-level function with the stored config. Exist so a Detrender can be passed by reference (e.g. into a pipeline runner expecting the protocol) without partial-application boilerplate.

docs.title: _clip_upper_outliers(flux, sigma) -> tuple[FloatArray, int] (private)
docs.text:
Source: src/exocomet/detrend/detrend.py:36-52

Lines 36–50. Replaces flux values more than sigma robust-sigma above the median with the median itself; returns (cleaned_flux, n_replaced). Robust sigma here is MAD_TO_SIGMA * median(|flux - median(flux)|) (imported from detect.baseline.MAD_TO_SIGMA). Downward excursions (dips) are never touched — only used internally by detrend_savgol/detrend_spline before fitting.

docs.title: Dependencies pulled in from exocomet.detect.baseline
